Serve args (not covered by collect_env): ``` --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice --default-chat-template-kwargs={"thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"high"} --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache False --speculative-config={"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5} --compilation-config={"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"} ``` Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`. `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` is byte-identical on current `main`, so this is not a stale-nightly artifact. ### The bug When the `deepseek_v4` reasoning parser is constructed with `thinking=true`, a response in which the model **never emits ``** has its **entire answer routed to `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty**. The trailing `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` (EOS) is also left un-stripped at the end of `reasoning_content`. The stray EOS is the visible symptom, but the misrouting is the actual bug: the user-facing answer never reaches `content`. Chat UIs render it as collapsed "thinking" text, and agents that read `message.content` receive nothing at all. Stripping the EOS alone would not fix this — it would leave the answer buried in the reasoning channel. Observed with a real client (`pi`), where a greeting rendered entirely as grey "thinking" text with no answer: ```json {"role": "assistant", "reasoning_content": "Good morning! How can I help you today?<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>", "content": ""} ``` Expected: `content` = `"Good morning! How can I help you today?"`, `reasoning_content` empty (the model did not deliberate), and no EOS in either field. ### Root cause In [`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L128`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L128): ```python initial_state=ParserState.REASONING if thinking else ParserState.CONTENT, ``` With `thinking=true` the engine starts in `ParserState.REASONING`, and the only exit is the `THINK_END` (``) transition at [L160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L160). DeepSeek-V4-Flash does not always emit `…`: on short replies it sometimes answers directly and hits EOS with no `` at all. The state machine then never leaves `REASONING`, so every chunk is emitted as `REASONING_CHUNK` and `content` stays empty. The terminal EOS is not dropped on that path either. The `initial_state` assumption holds only if the model is guaranteed to emit `` whenever thinking is enabled. It isn't — `thinking=true` gates the template/parser, not whether the model actually deliberates. I have **not** traced why the EOS specifically survives here; streaming carries real token ids, so the id-based drop would be expected to fire. Reporting that as observed rather than explained. ### Why clients hit this The parser reads `thinking` from `chat_template_kwargs` ([L220-L222](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9e57de71/vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py#L220-L222)). Any deployment setting `--default-chat-template-kwargs={"thinking":true,...}` (as the [DeepSeek-V4-Flash recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash) suggests) applies it to **every** request — including from OpenAI-compatible clients that never send `chat_template_kwargs` and have no notion of the kwarg. That is the common case for agent clients, so the server default silently puts all of their requests on the REASONING-start path. ### Reproduction Plain OpenAI-compatible streaming request, no `chat_template_kwargs` in the request (so the server default `thinking=true` applies): ```python body = { "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "stream": True, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": ""}, {"role": "user", "content": "good morning"}, ], } # Accumulate delta["content"] and delta["reasoning_content"] across the stream. # Misroute signature: content empty AND reasoning_content holds the answer + EOS. ``` Rates over 20-24 samples each, temperature 1.0 (the V4 default): | request | misrouted | |---|---| | agent system prompt + 50 tool defs (real client request) | 4/20 and 6/24 (~20-25%) | | same system prompt, tools removed | 2/24 | | generic short system prompt + the same 50 tool defs | 0/24 | | no system prompt (`"good morning"` alone) | 0/24 | | explicit `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking":false}` (CONTENT-start path) | 0/20 | It is sampling-dependent and provoked by a realistic agent system prompt that biases toward answering immediately; tool definitions raise the rate but do not trigger it alone. A long *synthetic* prompt (51k chars of repeated filler) did **not** reproduce it — prompt length is not the trigger, the instruction content is. That is why I can't reduce it to a self-contained prompt to paste here. Given that sampling dependence, the deterministic repro is at the parser level: construct the parser with `thinking=True` and feed it a model output containing no ``, e.g. `"Good morning! How can I help you today?<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>"`. Current behaviour routes all of it to reasoning; expected is `content`. ### Suggested fix Roughly in order of preference: 1. **Treat a response with no `` as content.** If generation ends while still in `REASONING` and no `THINK_START`/`THINK_END` was ever seen, flush the buffered reasoning to `content`. Fixes the "model didn't think" case without touching the deliberating case. 2. **Only enter `REASONING` on evidence of thinking** — keep `initial_state=CONTENT` and rely on the existing `(CONTENT, THINK_START) -> REASONING` transition. Depends on whether the chat template pre-fills an opening `` the parser never sees. 3. Independently, drop the terminal EOS on the reasoning path as is done on the content path. Happy to test a patch against this deployment and report rates back — it reproduces reliably enough at ~20-25% to validate a fix. ### Related - [#45877](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45877) — ported DeepSeek V4/V3.2 to the streaming parser engine (merged 2026-07-04). This report is against the merged code, not a regression from it. - [#46875](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46875) — general "special tokens don't leak in tool parsing" rework; does not cover this path.

signals.title: [Usability] Engine fails to start when available Mamba cache blocks < max_num_seqs (hybrid models + LoRA) — suggest auto-clamping with a warning
signals.text: **Summary**: For hybrid attention/SSM models (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.6 with Gated DeltaNet layers), engine startup hard-fails with: ``` ValueError: max_num_seqs (256) exceeds available Mamba cache blocks (243). Each decode sequence requires one Mamba cache block ... ``` The available block count depends on leftover memory after weights/LoRA/compilation, so the failure appears unpredictably when combining a larger checkpoint with `enable_lora=True` and a moderate `gpu_memory_utilization`. Observed on 1×L40S (48GB), vllm 0.24.0, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`: - Qwen3.5-4B W4A16 + `enable_lora=True` at util 0.85 → 243 blocks (< default 256) → startup failure - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W4A16 (21GB weights) + `enable_lora=True` at util 0.75 → **13 blocks** → startup failure **Suggestion**: since the default `max_num_seqs=256` reflects no user intent, auto-clamp `max_num_seqs` down to the available Mamba block count (with a WARNING log), or at least include the actionable remedy ("lower max_num_seqs / raise gpu_memory_utilization") in the error message. Currently each affected deployment has to discover the fix by trial and error. **Workaround we use**: pass `max_num_seqs` ≤ available blocks (e.g. 64) for LoRA-enabled hybrid engines.

TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Starting with vLLM 0.25.1, a large **dense** model (e.g. `Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` FP8, TP=8) that previously started fine now OOMs during CUDA graph capture (`capture_model()`), even with an otherwise-unchanged config. The regression is caused by the interaction of two things: 1. **Model Runner V2 is now the default for dense models.** 2. **The V2 runner's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` is a dummy that returns `0`**, so the memory profiler reserves **no** headroom for CUDA graph capture. The KV cache is then sized to consume the entire `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, and `capture_model()` later OOMs when it allocates the CUDA graph buffers. The legacy (V1) runner implements `profile_cudagraph_memory()` properly and reserves this memory (≈9.5 GiB for this config), which is why the same config works on 0.23.0. ### Root cause (with references to current `main`) **(a) V2 is selected by default for dense models** — `vllm/config/vllm.py`, `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` → `_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()`: ```python architectures = getattr(model_config, "architectures", []) return ( any(arch in DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES for arch in architectures) or not model_config.is_moe ) ``` For a dense model like `LlamaForCausalLM`, `is_moe` is `False`, so this returns `True` and V2 is selected when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset (its default). In 0.23.0, the equivalent logic also fell back to the legacy runner for **quantized** models, so FP8 Llama used the V1 runner and was unaffected. **(b) The V2 runner does not actually profile CUDA graph memory** — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: ```python def profile_cudagraph_memory(self) -> int: # NOTE(woosuk): It is TBD whether we keep this API or not. return 0 ``` This dummy was added in **PR #36520** ("[Model Runner V2] Add dummy `profile_cudagraph_memory` API", commit `6e956d9eca398005929d29f123607d1029800cc7`) two days after **PR #30515** ("[UX][Startup] Account for CUDA graphs during memory profiling") introduced the caller. It was a placeholder to satisfy the new interface and has never been implemented; it is still `return 0` on `main`. **(c) The worker subtracts this (zero) estimate when sizing the KV cache** — `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, `determine_available_memory()`: ```python if ( current_platform.is_cuda_alike() and self.vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode != CUDAGraphMode.NONE ): cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory() ... cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied = ( cudagraph_memory_estimate if envs.VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS # default True else 0 ) ... self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes = ( self.requested_memory - profile_result.non_kv_cache_memory - cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied # == 0 for the V2 runner ) ``` With `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=True` (the default) but the V2 estimate being `0`, the KV cache claims the entire remaining budget. There is then no room left for the CUDA graph buffers allocated during `capture_model()`, and startup OOMs. On GPUs without NVLink (e.g. L40S) the extra NCCL buffer pressure makes this more likely to manifest. ### Steps to reproduce (minimal, vLLM-native) ```python from vllm import LLM # Dense FP8 checkpoint, tensor-parallel across GPUs. # Reproduced on 8x L40S (no NVLink). llm = LLM( model="", tensor_parallel_size=8, gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, ) ``` - **0.23.0:** starts successfully (legacy runner reserves CUDA graph memory). - **0.25.1 / `main`:** OOMs during CUDA graph capture. - Setting `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` on 0.25.1 makes it start successfully again. ### Observed error (representative — please replace with your full traceback) ```text RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error (run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for details) ... torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate ... (raised during capture_model() / CUDA graph capture at startup) ``` ### Expected behavior CUDA graph capture memory should be reserved before the KV cache is sized, regardless of which model runner is selected, so that startup does not OOM on a config that fits with the legacy runner. ### Workarounds - `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` — forces the legacy runner, which reserves CUDA graph memory correctly. (Preferred; keeps CUDA graphs enabled.) - Lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` to manually leave headroom. - `enforce_eager=True` — disables CUDA graphs entirely (perf cost). ### Suggested fix Implement `profile_cudagraph_memory()` in the V2 runner (mirroring the legacy runner's implementation) so `determine_available_memory()` reserves the correct headroom. Alternatively, until the V2 API is implemented, either (a) account for CUDA graph capture memory in the V2 KV-cache sizing path, or (b) do not make V2 the default for configurations where CUDA graph capture memory is significant. I'm happy to open a PR porting the legacy `profile_cudagraph_memory()` logic into the V2 runner if that's the preferred direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Token truncation leaves stale Request.block_hashes and can cause incorrect KV cache hits
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> Not environment-dependent: this is a code-level invariant break in the scheduler / prefix-hashing path, reproduced against `main` @ `f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1` with the pure-Python script below (no GPU required). </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** When a request's tokens are truncated in place while `Request.block_hashes` is not, the retained hashes keep fingerprinting the replaced tokens. Prefix-cache, event, and offload consumers treat these hashes as authoritative identities, so the prefix cache can serve KV under a wrong identity: a later request whose prefix matches the OLD tokens gets a cache hit on KV computed from the NEW tokens — silently incorrect output — while the NEW token sequence misses blocks that are actually resident. The trigger reproduced deterministically below is the resumable streaming session path; the Mooncake/NIXL token-pop paths can violate the same invariant when the popped token is already hash-covered (see Related work). **Root cause** (permalinks pinned to `main` @ `f25953cc5`): 1. `Scheduler._update_request_as_session` discards the last sampled token(s) by truncating `_all_token_ids` past `num_computed_tokens` on the live `Request`, then extends it with the next input chunk and calls `update_block_hashes()` ([`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1282-1314`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1282-L1314)). 2. `Request.update_block_hashes` only appends ([`vllm/v1/request.py:244-260`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/request.py#L244-L260)); nothing in the tree ever truncates `request.block_hashes`. 3. The block hasher resumes from `start_token_idx = len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size` ([`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:691-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L691-L748)), so a block whose hash already exists is never recomputed. If a discarded sampled token had completed a hash block (for a single discarded token: `num_computed_tokens % hash_block_size == hash_block_size - 1`), the hash chained over the now-replaced token persists, and all later hashes chain from it. **Deterministic reproduction** (mirrors the statements `_update_request_as_session` executes at `scheduler.py:1293-1314`): ```python from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash from vllm.v1.request import Request init_none_hash(sha256) hash_block_size = 4 req = Request( request_id="session", prompt_token_ids=[1, 2, 3], sampling_params=SamplingParams(), pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(hash_block_size, sha256), resumable=True, ) req.append_output_token_ids(99) # completes hash block [1, 2, 3, 99] assert len(req.block_hashes) == 1 stale_hash = req.block_hashes[0] req.num_computed_tokens = 3 # sampled token 99 was never computed # --- what _update_request_as_session runs for the next streaming chunk [4] --- del req._all_token_ids[req.num_computed_tokens :] # scheduler.py:1297 req._output_token_ids.clear() # scheduler.py:1298 req._all_token_ids.append(4) # next input chunk req.update_block_hashes() # scheduler.py:1314 assert list(req.all_token_ids) == [1, 2, 3, 4] # block_hashes[0] still fingerprints [1, 2, 3, 99]: the hasher resumes at # len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size == 4 and never revisits block 0. assert req.block_hashes[0] == stale_hash # Explicit identity check: the retained hash is the OLD sequence's, not the new one's. import vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils as kcu assert req.block_hashes[0] == kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 99]) assert req.block_hashes[0] != kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 4]) ``` **Consequence (source derivation; the wrong cross-request hit requires prefix caching to be enabled).** At session-update time the boundary block has not yet been cached as a full block (its last token was never computed). The corruption lands when the resumed session is next scheduled: `allocate_slots()` commits the block under `request.block_hashes[0]` — the identity of `[1, 2, 3, 99]` — **before** the forward pass runs; the insertion chain is [`kv_cache_manager.py:493-503`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L493-L503) -> [`kv_cache_coordinator.py:283-287`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L283-L287) -> [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:443-450`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L443-L450) -> the insertion at [`block_pool.py:280-297`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L280-L297) (fine-grained hash-block configurations go through the partial-block callers at [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:787`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L787) / [`:1674`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1674) into [`block_pool.py:490-512`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L490-L512)); the subsequent forward then writes the KV computed from `[1, 2, 3, 4]` into that block. On lookup, `get_computed_blocks` matches `request.block_hashes` under the `num_tokens - 1` cap ([`kv_cache_manager.py:237-241`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L237-L241)) and resolves cached blocks via [`block_pool.py:198-223`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L198-L223): a later request continuing past that block with actual prefix `[1, 2, 3, 99, …]` (it must extend beyond the block because of the `num_tokens - 1` cap, so an exactly-four-token request does not hit) computes that same hash and gets the block — a prefix-cache hit on KV computed from different tokens, i.e. silently wrong output — while a later `[1, 2, 3, 4, …]` request computes a hash absent from the map and misses a resident block. The stale identities also flow into KV cache events (`BlockStored` payloads are emitted from the same pool paths, e.g. [`block_pool.py:331`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L331) and [`:527-528`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L527-L528)) and into offload keys (the offloading connector derives `OffloadKey`s from `request.block_hashes` in `update_offload_keys`, [`offloading/scheduler.py:306-316`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L306-L316)), so external indexers and offloaded copies inherit the wrong fingerprints. (The script pins the request-side invariant break; the pool-side consequence is derived from the cited paths — no end-to-end wrong-output run is included here.) **Candidate fix direction (text-only; see limitations).** In `_update_request_as_session`, invalidate hashes past the kept prefix before extending — `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // self.hash_block_size :]` (the scheduler holds `hash_block_size`): hashes of blocks fully inside `[0, num_computed_tokens)` remain valid, and the resumed hasher recomputes the boundary block. On this path that is also sufficient for the pool side, because the boundary block was never cached as a full block. Two limitations to be explicit about: (i) this is correct for **text-only** requests — with multimodal inputs the incremental hasher restarts its feature scan from the last MM feature in the request's current list — including newly appended ones (`curr_mm_idx = -1`) — not from the first feature overlapping the recomputed range ([`kv_cache_utils.py:713-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L713-L748)), so deleting the hash suffix alone can still yield wrong hashes — when the suffix recomputation starts from a non-zero boundary and the recomputed range overlaps earlier MM features while a later feature exists in the current list (confirmed by fresh-vs-incremental hash comparison for such cases; deleting all hashes and recomputing from token 0 does not hit this); covering multimodal requires also rewinding the MM scan start plus regression tests, or scoping the streaming fix to text-only sessions; (ii) a general fix for truncating already-computed tokens would additionally have to keep the `BlockPool` side consistent (`KVCacheBlock` block-hash state and the `cached_block_hash_to_block` mapping). Both are out of scope for the minimal fix here. I'm happy to send a fix PR for the text-only path unless the streaming-sessions folks would rather take it. **Related work (checked, not duplicates).** - #43372 (open) adds an explicit per-session KV-cache truncation API and clears `Request.block_hashes` on that new path; it does not touch `_update_request_as_session`, and clearing the request-side list alone does not cover the pool side for already-computed truncated tokens. Related — neither a duplicate nor a complete fix precedent. - Adjacent paths that can violate the same invariant (not reproduced end-to-end; should not block this fix): the Mooncake and NIXL connector token-pop paths for hybrid/Mamba models — NIXL's `_truncate_mamba_request_for_prefill` ([`nixl/base_scheduler.py:341-365`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_scheduler.py#L341-L365)) and the Mooncake connector's last-token pop ([`mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:701-707`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L701-L707)) — can leave stale `block_hashes` when the removed token is already covered by a computed hash (e.g. the pre-pop length lands exactly on a hash boundary). They warrant separate fixes/audits. cc @joshuadeng (streaming sessions, #28973) @Alex-ai-future (#48596) AI assistance was used in preparing this report; the reproduction script was verified against `main` @ `f25953cc5`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Perf][Kernel] Adopt PTX 9.4 `ldmatrix.s8.s4` (hardware INT4→INT8 expanding load) in W4A8-INT8 paths
signals.text: ## Summary PTX ISA 9.4 (CUDA 13.4.0 Developer Preview) exposes a new `ldmatrix` variant that performs **in-flight sign extension of packed INT4 to INT8 during the shared-memory matrix load**: ``` ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n16.{x1,x2,x4}{.shared{::cta}}.s8.s4 r, [p]; ``` Source data is densely packed signed 4-bit elements; the hardware expands them to signed 8-bit values in the destination fragment. This can eliminate the register-level INT4→INT8 unpack sequences (`lop3`/`prmt` bit tricks and PRMT LUTs) in our W4A8-INT8 kernels, and potentially the dequant-oriented weight interleaving in repack. Doc: PTX ISA 9.4, §9.7.16.5.15 (`ldmatrix`), https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/developer-preview/13.4/parallel-thread-execution/index.html ## Hardware verification (already done) Verified with `ptxas`/`nvdisasm` from CUDA 13.4.0 preview (`V13.4.46`), no GPU required: - `ptxas` accepts the instruction for **sm_90a, sm_100a/f, sm_103a, sm_107a/f, sm_110f, sm_120f, sm_121a** (PTX targets per doc: `sm_90a, sm_100f, sm_110f, sm_120f`). - SASS is a **single LDSM instruction** on every architecture — no unpack sequence is generated. The encoding is bit-identical across all seven targets (opcode `0x783b` = LDSM, modifier `0x9000/0x9100/0x9200` for x1/x2/x4; cf. `LDSM.16.M88` = `0x0000`, `LDSM.U4x16P64TO8.M816` = `0xa800`, `LDSM.U6x16P32TO8.M816` = `0xb000`). - Notably **Hopper (sm_90a) is supported** — the datapath appears to have existed in silicon since GH100; PTX 9.4 merely exposes it. Existing H100/H200 fleets benefit immediately. - `nvdisasm` 13.4 does not yet print a mnemonic for this modifier (hex only); expect this to be fixed in the GA release. ## Affected code paths (vLLM @ `76bf55240`, 2026-07-23) ### 1. Marlin W4A8-INT8 — replaceable (bit-exact) - `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/dequant.h:494` — `dequant<int32_t, kU4B8>`: unpacks two nibbles per pass with `(q & 0x0F0F0F0F | 0x80808080) - 0x08080808) ^ 0x80808080`, i.e. u4-with-bias-8 → s8. - `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/marlin_template.h:945` — `frag_b_quant` is loaded from shared memory with plain 128-bit loads over Marlin's dequant-interleaved layout, then dequanted at `marlin_template.h:1163` (`dequant_data`). - `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/gptq_marlin_repack.cu` — repack currently bakes in the dequant interleave. **Equivalence:** for `kU4B8`, stored nibble `v ∈ [0,15]` yields output `v − 8`. Storing `s4 = v XOR 0x8` at repack time (free) makes `sign_extend(s4) == v − 8` **bit-exact**. The ALU sequence (≈6 ops per 32-bit word × 2 fragments) disappears, and the B-fragment interleave in repack can be dropped in favor of the canonical 8-bit `ldmatrix` tile layout. ### 2. Machete W4A8-INT8 — replaceable (bit-exact) - `csrc/libtorch_stable/cutlass_extensions/vllm_numeric_conversion.cuh:213` — `NumericArrayConverter<int8_t, vllm_uint4b8_t>` implements the identical `[-8..7]` mapping via a PRMT LUT (`lut_4bit_to_8bit_convert`, line 158). Used by the Machete mainloop's register-transform stage. - Replacement means moving the conversion out of the CUTLASS transform pipeline into the smem→rmem copy atom; requires a new copy atom + prepacked-layout adjustment in `machete_prepacked_layout.cuh` rather than a converter swap. Larger change; track separately as phase 2. ### 3. Marlin W4A8-INT8 with runtime zero-point — partially replaceable - `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/dequant.h:570` — `sub_zp_and_dequant<int32_t, kU4>` (asymmetric AWQ-style zp, see #24722). Pure sign extension can't absorb a runtime zp, but `ldmatrix.s8.s4` + one packed s8 correction add (`zp − 8` per group) still beats the current mask/sub/xor sequence. Lower priority. ### 4. Out of scope - `cutlass_w4a8/` (W4A8-**FP8**, `MmaType = e4m3`): target type is FP8, not covered by this instruction. - `moe/moe_wna16_utils.h`, AWQ/GPTQ FP16 paths: dequant target is FP16/BF16. ## Proposed plan - [ ] **Phase 0 — layout verification**: confirm the `m8n16.s8.s4` output fragment layout matches `mma.m16n8k32.s8` operand-B fragments (the `m8n16`/`m16n16` 8-bit ldmatrix shapes were introduced in PTX 8.6 for exactly this pairing; verify the s4 source packing order within each 8-byte row against our repack output). Only `m8n16` is available for `.s8.s4` (no `.trans`), so B must be stored K-major in smem. - [ ] **Phase 1 — Marlin symmetric path (`kU4B8`)**: - repack: store `v XOR 0x8` nibbles, drop dequant interleave for the `is_a_8bit && !has_zp` configuration; - kernel: replace `frag_b_quant` plain loads + `dequant` with `ldmatrix.m8n16.x4.s8.s4`, guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH_FAMILY_SPECIFIC__` / arch macros for {90a, 100f, 110f, 120f} and `CUDA >= 13.4`; - keep the existing lop3 path as fallback for sm_80/86/89 and older toolkits. - **No on-disk/checkpoint format change**: repack runs at weight-loading time (`process_weights_after_loading` → `ops.gptq_marlin_repack`); both transforms live inside the repack kernel and only affect the in-GPU-memory layout. - The in-memory Marlin layout becomes kernel-variant-dependent (ldmatrix layout vs legacy interleave). Repack must take a layout-variant flag driven by the same arch/toolkit predicate as kernel selection; if repacked-weight caching across processes is ever introduced, the layout needs a version tag. - [ ] **Phase 1.5 — benchmark**: microbench LDSM-expand vs LDS+lop3 (MIO-pipe pressure vs ALU pressure; note Marlin is often ALU-bound in the dequant stage at high occupancy), plus end-to-end gptq W4A8-INT8 throughput on H100/H200, B200, RTX 5090. - [ ] **Phase 2 — Machete**: smem→rmem copy atom using `ldmatrix.s8.s4`, prepacked layout update. - [ ] **Phase 3 — zp path**: evaluate `ldmatrix.s8.s4` + packed correction add for `sub_zp_and_dequant`. ## Caveats - CUDA 13.4 is currently a **Developer Preview**; land behind a build-time gate and revisit at GA. Instruction availability/targets could still shift (precedent: a→f promotions between 8.6 and 8.8). - `nvdisasm` cannot yet name the instruction; debugging SASS requires reading hex until tooling catches up. - Ada (sm_89) and Ampere keep the existing path permanently — the instruction is sm_90+ only. ## References - PTX ISA 9.4 release notes: "Adds support for `.s8.s4` types for `ldmatrix` instruction for `.m8n16` shape" — targets `sm_90a, sm_100f, sm_110f, sm_120f`. - Existing sub-byte ldmatrix formats (`.b6x16_p32`, `.b4x16_p64`, unsigned, padded) introduced in PTX 8.6 for the f8f6f4 MMA path — the new `.s8.s4` differs in being **densely packed** and **sign-extending**. - #24722 (Marlin W4A8-INT8 dequant tricks this would supersede on sm_90+).

signals.title: [Performance] Measure Transformers backend startup time vs native
signals.text: This comes from an old comment and was never backed by measurements, so the first task is to establish whether the effect is real at all. It may not be. Runtime throughput was brought in line with native implementations in #47187, but nobody has measured startup time either before or since. ### Step 1: is there a difference? Time engine init for a model that has both implementations, e.g.: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl vllm Compare time-to-ready across a few runs and a couple of model sizes. Warm vs cold HF cache matters, so control for it. If there is no meaningful difference, say so and close this issue. That is a perfectly good outcome and still worth having measured. ### Step 2: only if a delta shows up The backend does some work at load time that native implementations do not, so these are plausible starting points rather than known causes: - `fuser.py` — `get_fuser` traces each module class with `fx` to match it against the available fusers. Cached per class, but tracing is not free. - `base.py` — `recursive_replace` walks the module tree applying fusers per instance. - Config resolution and `auto_map` handling for remote-code models. A profile of init (py-spy or cProfile) will be more informative than guessing from this list. ### Done when Either the startup delta is quantified and explained, or it is shown that there isn't a meaningful one and this is closed.

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_vllm ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Long-running vLLM engine processes leak host memory (VmRSS/VmData) on paths where a libtorch stable-ABI custom op with a `str` argument is dispatched **eagerly** in the hot loop. Each such call leaks ~48 bytes; over hours this grows unbounded and can OOM the engine (~0.5 GB/hour under continuous load in our reproduction). The root cause is **not in vLLM** — it is a bug in PyTorch's stable ABI, which heap-allocates a `std::string` when unboxing a `str` argument and never frees it. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Where it hits vLLM `reshape_and_cache_flash` is registered as a stable op with a `str kv_cache_dtype` argument: - schema: `csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp` (`reshape_and_cache_flash(Tensor key, ... str kv_cache_dtype, ...) -> ()`) - impl: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu` (`void reshape_and_cache_flash(..., const std::string& kv_cache_dtype, ...)`) - bind: `ops.impl("reshape_and_cache_flash", TORCH_BOX(&reshape_and_cache_flash))` On most paths this op is captured into a CUDA graph and replayed, so it is not re-dispatched per step and the leak does not accumulate. But on the **Voxtral/Whisper realtime streaming** path it is dispatched eagerly — once per attention layer per decode step — so every KV-cache write leaks and the process grows without bound. Any other eagerly-dispatched stable op with a `str` argument is affected the same way. ## Symptoms - Steady, linear host-memory growth (VmRSS/VmData) proportional to decode steps, not to batch size or sequence length. - Invisible to `tracemalloc` (the allocation is C++-side, not Python). - Not reclaimed by `malloc_trim(0)` — the memory is live, not fragmentation. - glibc `mallinfo2().uordblks` grows in lockstep with RSS. - Present only on eager (non-CUDA-graph) dispatch paths. ## Root cause (upstream) In PyTorch's `torch/csrc/stable/stableivalue_conversions.h`, the `str` → `std::string` unboxing (`ToImpl<std::string>::call`) does: ```cpp auto strptr = new std::string(data, length); // heap-allocated TORCH_ERROR_CODE_CHECK(torch_delete_string(handle)); return *strptr; // returns a COPY; *strptr is never deleted ``` Each unbox orphans one heap-allocated `std::string` control object (~48 bytes: `sizeof(std::string)` + allocator overhead; the value's characters are irrelevant since short strings like `"auto"` fit small-string optimization). Fix is upstream: construct the string on the stack instead of with `new`. See https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 for details and the patch. ## Impact on vLLM - Realtime/streaming ASR paths (Voxtral, Whisper) that dispatch KV-cache writes eagerly leak continuously and can OOM long-running servers. - Standard batched/CUDA-graph serving is largely unaffected because the op is replayed, not re-dispatched. ## Fix / mitigation - **Real fix:** upstream PyTorch (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340). The fix is header-only in the stable ABI, so vLLM's custom-op `.so` must be recompiled. - **Possible vLLM-side mitigations** while waiting for an upstream release: - Avoid re-dispatching stable ops with `str` arguments in eager hot loops (e.g. pass the dtype as an enum/int rather than a `str`, if a non-`str` schema is feasible). - Ensure the affected streaming paths use CUDA-graph capture/replay where possible. ## Reproduction Minimal, self-contained (CPU-only) reproduction of the underlying leak — two no-op stable ops identical except one takes a `str` — is in the upstream issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Environment ``` torch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 OS: Linux (x86_64) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.text: Kimi-K3 is a very successful launch. This issue is to track vLLM upstream work for feature enablement and performance optimization on ROCm. <details><summary>Day 0 features/baselines</summary> - AITER fused-moe: a16w4 (GENERAL) and a8w4 (INTERLEAVE ) were integrated for performance. Flydsl/opus a8w4 is perf is 3.5% higher than flydsl a16w4. - AITER MLA attention: non-causal mla-gluon kernel was used for 12 head. - AITER triton conv2d - AMD vendor specific KDA - DSpark speculative decoding: Target model used AITER MLA (gluon) and draft model used TRITON_MLA. signals.title: Hybrid multi-group KV: _update_requests_with_invalid_blocks crashes (too many values to unpack) on connector load-error blocks
signals.text: Title: Hybrid multi-group KV: `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` crashes with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)` whenever a connector reports invalid (load-error) blocks ## Version vLLM 0.26.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0-cu129-ubuntu2404), any KVConnectorBase_V1 integration that can return per-request invalid block ids (dfkv DfkvStoreConnector in our case). ## Model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (284B/13B MoE, hybrid Compressed Sparse Attention CSA + HCA + lightning indexer). This model has >1 `kv_cache_group`s (full-MLA main + several window/compress groups + indexer group — we see 5 groups after splitting). ## Repro 1. Serve with any external KV cache connector that implements `get_block_ids_with_load_errors()` (the dfkv connector in our setup). 2. Force one external load to report a failed/missing block (`hit != 1` or partial read) — for us this happened after a fresh engine restart against a ring with partial data. 3. First request that surfaces a load-error block kills the whole engine: ``` (EngineCore pid=577) ERROR ... [core.py:1332] Traceback ... engine_core.run_busy_loop → _process_engine_step → step_fn outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn() engine_core_outputs = self.scheduler.update_from_output(...) failed_kv_load_req_ids = self._handle_invalid_blocks(...) self._update_requests_with_invalid_blocks(...) (req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id) ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1) ``` `kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)` returns a seq with one entry per kv_cache_group (5 for this model); the unpack assumes exactly 1. ## Expected Per-group invalid-block handling: either iterate all groups' block id lists, or drop/mark blocks per-group. With our connector returning correct `hit=100%` loads the engine works fine, so the crash path is only reachable via the invalid-block flow — but any connector load error with a hybrid model is fatal (whole engine exits, container down). ## Notes - Engine runs the official vllm 0.26.0 container image, no patched vLLM code. - Full working repro environment available on request (scripts + ring + connector).

signals.title: [Bug]: gpt-oss chat completions return 500 "Unexpected token 200002 while expecting start token 200006" when ignore_eos=true
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM **0.26.0** and **0.18.0** (both reproduce), official `vllm/vllm-openai` images - `openai-harmony` 0.0.8 - Model: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, 1x H200, TP=1 - `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b --max-model-len 32768 --tensor-parallel-size 1` ### 🐛 Describe the bug A Chat Completions request with `ignore_eos: true` returns **HTTP 500** whenever the model finishes its Harmony turn before `max_completion_tokens` is reached: ```json {"error":{"message":"Unexpected token 200002 while expecting start token 200006","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}} ``` (200002 = `<|return|>`, 200006 = `<|start|>`) **Minimal reproducer** — one request, no streaming: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi."}], "max_completion_tokens": 512, "ignore_eos": true }' ``` The prompt matters: the answer must be **shorter** than `max_completion_tokens`. A prompt whose answer fills the budget never reaches the terminator and succeeds, which makes this look intermittent. | arm | 0.18.0 | 0.26.0 | |---|---|---| | short answer + `ignore_eos` | 500 | 500 | | answer longer than `max_completion_tokens` + `ignore_eos` | OK | OK | | short answer, no `ignore_eos` | OK | OK | ### Why `<|return|>` / `<|call|>` are the Harmony assistant stop tokens. `ignore_eos=true` suppresses stopping on them (`SamplingParams.update_from_generation_config`, the `if not self.ignore_eos:` guards), so generation continues past the end of the turn. Those trailing tokens are then fed to the `StreamableParser`, which is a state machine: after `<|end|>` it expects `<|start|>`, gets `<|return|>`, and raises. The exception is not caught, so the whole request fails. The parser half reproduces **without a server or GPU**: ```python from openai_harmony import HarmonyEncodingName, Role, StreamableParser, load_harmony_encoding enc = load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS) e = lambda s: enc.encode(s, allowed_special="all") stream = e("<|channel|>") + e("final") + e("<|message|>") + e("answer") + e("<|end|>") + e("<|return|>") p = StreamableParser(enc, role=Role.ASSISTANT) for t in stream: p.process(t) # HarmonyError: Unexpected token 200002 while expecting start token 200006 ``` vLLM is on both sides of this: it permits `ignore_eos` to override its own Harmony stop tokens, then treats the resulting token stream as a parse error. ### Impact `ignore_eos` is how benchmark tools pin output length so ISL/OSL combinations are controlled — both `vllm bench serve` (`--ignore-eos`) and GuideLLM use it. It is therefore hard to benchmark gpt-oss over Chat Completions at all. Measured with GuideLLM against 0.18.0 at ISL/OSL 1024/1024: **65% of requests failed** (971 errors, all this message). At OSL 128 the error rate was 0%, because the model rarely finishes a turn that early — so the failure rate scales with output length and can easily be mistaken for server saturation. `/v1/completions` is unaffected (no Harmony parsing on that path). ### Related - #41731 "[Bugfix] Respect ignore_eos for GPT-OSS Harmony stop tokens" — describes this exact cause, closed without merging (went stale on merge conflicts) - #41950 "[Bugfix] Stop Harmony stream parsing after parser errors" — the parser-side guard, closed without merging - #44009 "[Frontend] Clean up stop_token_ids override for Harmony" — merged, removed the `default_sampling_params` stop-token injection, but **does not fix this**: 0.26.0 still returns 500 (table above) - #22519 — same parser error via the tool-call path Either half would fix it: honor the Harmony stop tokens even under `ignore_eos` (#41731), or stop feeding a failed parser and fall back to raw tokens (#41950). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Made sure I searched the documentation and existing issues.

signals.title: [RFC]:  Unify the Tensor Type for Device-Pointer Storage to `torch.uint64`
signals.text: ### Motivation. In vLLM, several kernels accept `Tensor` objects whose elements are not ordinary numeric values but raw device pointers (i.e., `data_ptr()` of other tensors). These pointer tensors are used for batch memory copies, grouped operations (e.g., MoE where each expert has its own pointer array), attention block-table lookups, and cross-GPU IPC workspaces. Device pointers are semantically unsigned 64-bit values (`CUdeviceptr` / `uintptr_t`). However, the current vLLM codebase exhibits three inconsistent storage practices, one of which is clearly problematic: 1. **Unconditional use of `torch.int64`** — problematic. Assigning an unsigned address (`data_ptr()`) to a `torch.int64` tensor triggers `ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long` when the address exceeds `2^63-1`. This has been actually triggered on XPU for encoder-cache CPU offload [descriptor_buffers.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/worker/descriptor_buffers.py#L32) and Mamba speculative decoding state batch copy ([mamba_utils.py#L649](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L649)), with workaround PRs ([#49532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49532), [#50552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50552)) that keep `int64` + bit-reinterpretation. The cross-GPU IPC workspace ([lamport_workspace.py#L210](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py#L210)) carries the same latent risk. 2. **Platform-dependent branching (`int64` / `uint64`)** — currently works but is fragile. `swap_blocks_batch` uses `int64` for CUDA/ROCm and `uint64` for XPU [(`cache_kernels.cu#L86`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu#L86) [(`_custom_ops.py#L2831`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/_custom_ops.py#L2831). The KV-cache CPU offload [(`gpu_worker.py#L153`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L153) avoids the assignment pitfall only because it uses a `.numpy()` view, not because the branching logic is inherently safe. This approach forces every new call site to remember the correct dtype per platform — high maintenance cost and error-prone. 3. **Unconditional use of `torch.uint64`** — currently fine and already adopted in attention block-table pointer lookup [(`block_table.py#L82`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py#L82), LoRA batch Triton kernels [(`triton_ops/utils.py#L54`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/utils.py#L54), and KV-cache offload copy parameters [(`cuda_mem_ops.py#L111`)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py#L111). However, these work only because they currently construct the tensor in one go and do not perform element-wise assignment; if such assignment is introduced later, the same overflow error will reappear. Three unrelated modules (encoder-cache offload, Mamba speculative decoding, and Lamport workspace) have been hit — or are being hit — by the same problem at different times by different developers. This clearly indicates a **convention-level** issue, not a single code bug. The codebase currently lacks an explicit, copyable example; `int64` and `uint64` examples are almost evenly split, leaving new code to the author's personal judgment. ### Proposed Change. ### Goal Establish a clear vLLM-wide convention: **all tensors that store device pointers must use `torch.uint64`**. Specifically: - Remove all platform-based dtype branches — no special casing for CUDA/ROCm vs. XPU. - Align the low-level kernels (CUDA / Triton) that receive pointer arrays to expect `uint64` data, matching the upper layer. ### Prerequisite ⚠️ PyTorch currently does not support scalar assignment to `uint64` tensors (e.g., `t[0] = 2**63 + 5` raises `ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long`), even when the tensor itself is of type `uint64`. This issue is platform-independent (occurs on CUDA, ROCm, and XPU alike). The upstream PyTorch issue ([pytorch/pytorch#191458](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191458)) and its fix PR ([#191604](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191604)) are not yet merged. Until that fix lands, vLLM must adopt **workarounds** for assigning to `uint64` pointer tensors: - Use `.numpy()` views for element-wise assignment (see [`gpu_worker.py#L301-L303`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L301-L303)). ### Task List The following tasks can be implemented in separate PRs, gradually moving toward the unified type: - [ ] **Encoder-cache CPU offload** Change the dtype in [`descriptor_buffers.py#L32`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/worker/descriptor_buffers.py#L32) and [`worker/__init__.py#L112`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/worker/__init__.py#L112) to `uint64`, and align with [#49532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49532). - [ ] **Mamba speculative decoding state batch copy** Change the dtype in [`mamba_utils.py#L649`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L649) and [#L732](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py#L732) to `uint64`, and align with [#50552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50552). - [ ] **Cross-GPU IPC workspace** Modify [`lamport_workspace.py#L210`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py#L210) and its consuming kernels to use `uint64`. - [ ] **Unify `swap_blocks_batch`** Remove the platform branch for CUDA/ROCm vs. XPU, and update [`cache_kernels.cu#L86`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu#L86), [`_custom_ops.py#L2831`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/_custom_ops.py#L2831), and [`gpu_worker.py::_new_descriptor_buffers#L153`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L153) to consistently use `uint64`. - [x] **Upstream PyTorch fix** Advocate for merging [pytorch/pytorch#191604](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191604) (or an equivalent) to fix the `uint64` scalar assignment overflow. Until then, provide a shared **workaround helper** (e.g., `assign_uint64`) for vLLM modules to reuse, avoiding direct `__setitem__` operations. ### Alternatives Considered - **Keep status quo with platform branches**: Rejected — requires every new call site to remember platform-specific dtype, high maintenance cost, and the latent overflow risk remains. - **Use `torch.int64` everywhere with bit-reinterpretation**: Rejected — workaround PRs ([#49532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49532), [#50552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50552)) already exist but are fragile and do not solve the root cause. - **Use a custom wrapper type**: Rejected — adds unnecessary complexity and does not align with PyTorch tensor semantics. ### Backward Compatibility This change is backward compatible for existing `uint64` usages. For `int64` usages, callers that currently rely on signed interpretation may need to adjust. However, since these tensors store raw pointers, the signed interpretation is semantically incorrect; no valid use case should depend on it. ### Performance Impact No performance impact is expected. The dtype change does not affect kernel execution efficiency; it only affects tensor construction and assignment paths. ## Related Links - [pytorch/pytorch#191458](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191458) - [pytorch/pytorch#191604](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191604) - [vLLM PR #36423](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36423) - [vLLM PR #49532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49532) - [vLLM PR #50552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50552)

signals.title: [CI Failure]: test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8 — "invalid argument for fmha_fwd" on MI300X
signals.text: ### Name of failing test tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8 ### Basic information - [ ] Flaky test - [ ] Can reproduce locally - [ ] Caused by external libraries (e.g. bug in `transformers`) ### 🧪 Describe the failing test ## [CI Failure]: test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8 — "invalid argument for fmha_fwd" on MI300X ### Name of failing test `tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8` ### Basic information - [x] Flaky test (fails on the AMD image built for 2026-08-05; the same shard was green on 2026-08-03) - [x] Can reproduce locally on MI300X (`gfx942`) with the current AMD CI image - [x] Caused by external libraries (likely AITER / composable_kernel; not yet confirmed upstream) ### 🧪 Describe the failing test `amd-kernels-attention-test-1-mi300-1` fails with `5 failed, 1537 passed, 1781 skipped`. All 5 failures are the same test, same error: ```text FAILED kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8[dtype0-64-var_seq_len0] - RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd FAILED kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8[dtype1-64-var_seq_len1] - RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd FAILED kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8[dtype1-72-var_seq_len0] - RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd FAILED kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8[dtype1-72-var_seq_len1] - RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd FAILED kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8[dtype1-80-var_seq_len0] - RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd ``` Only 5 of the 12 parametrizations fail (`dtype ∈ {bfloat16, half}` × `head_size ∈ {64,72,80}` × `var_seq_len ∈ {[128,193],[256,384,511]}`); the rest pass, and the sibling job `amd-kernels-attention-test-2-mi300-1` passes. The test was added in #49937 ([ROCm] Add AITER FP8 ViT encoder attention, merged 2026-07-30). ### 📝 Error traceback The error is raised inside AITER's CK JIT dispatch, not in vLLM Python code: ```text MMEncoderAttention.forward_cuda → _forward_aiter_fp8 (vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mm_encoder_attention.py:755) → vit_aiter_fp8_attn_wrapper (vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py:131) → torch.ops.vllm.aiter_fp8_attn_wrapper (vllm/_aiter_ops.py:1486) → aiter.flash_attn_varlen_fp8_pertensor_func (aiter/ops/mha.py:4081) → _flash_attn_varlen_forward → mha_varlen_fwd (aiter/ops/mha.py:3011) md_name = mha_varlen_fwd_fp8bf16_nlogits_nbias_nmask_nlse_ndropout_nskip_pertensor blob_gen_cmd = .../composable_kernel/example/ck_tile/01_fmha/generate.py -d fwd_splitkv --receipt 200 ... E RuntimeError: invalid argument for fmha_fwd aiter/jit/core.py:1780: RuntimeError ``` The CK module compiles (the first case spends ~80s in JIT), but at launch the runtime arguments match no compiled `fmha_fwd` instance, so CK rejects the call. ### 📄 Full logs / build - Failing job: [vllm/ci #82340 · amd-kernels-attention-test-1-mi300-1](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82340#019fd00c-0c67-489b-9739-f2e86a29ec33) (exit status 1) - Passing baseline (same shard, `main`, 2026-08-03): [vllm/ci #82016](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82016#019fc832-d562-49b2-a427-59f07268889b) — `1542 passed, 0 failed` - Retried once; failure reproduces (not a within-run flake). ### 🔁 Regression evidence (image, not code) | | `main` #82016 (2026-08-03) | run #82340 (2026-08-05) | | --- | --- | --- | | Shard | 3314 items | 3314 items | | `aiter_fp8` cases reached | same 5 | same 5 | | Result | **1542 passed, 0 failed** | **5 failed** | | First case JIT time | 80.01 s | 79.65 s | | Arch | MI300X / `gfx942` | MI300X / `gfx942` | Same test code, same parametrizations, same hardware — only the build date differs, which points at the AMD test image / AITER-CK kernel set rather than a vLLM change. It surfaced on a PR that touches no ROCm / AITER / ViT / MMEncoder code. ### 🖥️ Environment - **Hardware:** AMD Instinct MI300X (`gfx942`) - **CI job:** `amd-kernels-attention-test-1-mi300-1` - **Image pins** (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`): `BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete`, `AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.19`, `PYTORCH_BRANCH=d0c8b1f3` (release/2.11), `TRITON_BRANCH=0f380657`, `FA_BRANCH=0e60e394` - **vLLM commit under test:** `f27555f2d8` (merge of `main` into a PR branch that does not modify ROCm code) ### 🔁 Reproduction ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py::test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8 -v # on MI300X (gfx942) with the current AMD CI image ``` ### Notes - Latest `main` build [#82449](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82449) had just reached this test when this issue was filed; result pending. If it is also red, the regression is confirmed on `main`, independent of any PR. cc @vllm-project/rocm maintainers of #49937. ### 📝 History of failing test ### 🕰️ History of failing test | Date | Build / ref | Job | `aiter_fp8` outcome | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-07-30 | #49937 merged | — | Test introduced (`test_mha_attn_varlen_forward_aiter_fp8`) | | 2026-07-30 | #49361 merged | — | `AITER_BRANCH` pinned to `v0.1.19` in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` | | 2026-08-03 | [`main` #82016](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82016#019fc832-d562-49b2-a427-59f07268889b) | `amd-kernels-attention-test-1-mi300-1` | ✅ `1542 passed, 0 failed` (all 12 params pass) | | 2026-08-05 | [PR #82340](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82340#019fd00c-0c67-489b-9739-f2e86a29ec33) | `amd-kernels-attention-test-1-mi300-1` | ❌ `5 failed` — `invalid argument for fmha_fwd` | | 2026-08-05 | PR #82340 (retry) | same | ❌ reproduces (not a within-run flake) | | 2026-08-05 | [`main` #82449](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82449#019fd032-5f84-44c3-a26f-b31f2e4f0b69) | same | ⏳ in progress at time of filing | **Observations** - The test passed cleanly on `main` as recently as **2026-08-03** and started failing on **2026-08-05**, so the flip is in that 2-day window. - No code in the failing path changed in that window: the test file (#49937) and `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` were last touched on 2026-07-30, and the `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins (`AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.19`, `PYTORCH_BRANCH`, `TRITON_BRANCH`, `FA_BRANCH`) were last modified on 2026-07-30. This is consistent with the AMD base image being **rebuilt** (regenerating the composable_kernel `fwd_splitkv` blob set) rather than any source change. - First observed failing: **2026-08-05, build #82340**. First observed passing: **2026-08-03, build #82016**. - The failure is a stable subset (5 of 12 parametrizations), not intermittent across parametrizations within a run. ### CC List. _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: [ROCm] DeepSeek-V4 sparse indexer is a dead end on non-MI3xx GPUs, though working torch fallbacks exist in-tree
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Abridged environment (key versions; 2-node cluster)</summary> ```text vLLM: 0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260808 PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0 Python: 3.14.4 ROCm: 7.14, RCCL 2.30.4 GPU: 2x AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU, gfx1151), 1 GPU per node Nodes: 2-node Ray cluster, TP=2, Thunderbolt interconnect (RCCL NET/Socket) Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8, fp8_ds_mla KV cache) AITER: built from source (ROCm/aiter @ main, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151); imports and JITs fine ``` Serve command: ```bash vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --distributed-executor-backend ray ``` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Three interacting gates currently make DeepSeek-V4 (and presumably any model using the DSA sparse indexer with `fp8_ds_mla`) impossible to run on ROCm GPUs other than MI3xx — while torch reference fallbacks for exactly this situation already exist in-tree, are wired with correct arguments, and work when made reachable (verified on a 2× gfx1151 cluster, now serving). **Gate 1 — the indexer requires AITER.** During the profiling forward pass, `sparse_attn_indexer.py::forward_hip` raises: ``` Sparse attention indexer ROCm path is only supported on AITER. Please enable aiter with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 ``` **Gate 2 — the advice in that error cannot work.** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is silently ignored on non-MI3xx because `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` hard-gates on platform: ```python def is_aiter_found_and_supported() -> bool: ... if current_platform.is_rocm() and IS_AITER_FOUND: from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx return on_mi3xx() return False ``` So the user is sent in a loop: the error demands an env var that the platform gate then discards, even with AITER installed and importable. **Gate 3 — the in-tree fallbacks are unreachable.** `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` contains `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` and `fp8_mqa_logits_torch`, and both dispatchers (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) already call them in their `else` branches when the AITER Triton module is unavailable. But reaching the dispatchers requires AITER enabled (gates 1–2), and with AITER enabled the module lookup always succeeds, so the AITER Triton kernels are always selected. On RDNA3/3.5 those AITER Triton kernels cannot compile regardless (no fp8 WMMA), so whitelisting the arch in gate 2 just moves the failure into Triton: ``` triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError o = tl.dot(q, k.T) ^ Unsupported lhs dtype fp8e4nv (aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py, deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1) ``` i.e. every path on this hardware terminates in an error one step before working fallback code. ### Reproduction 1. 2× gfx1151, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, serve command in the environment section → gate 1 error. 2. Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` → identical error (gate 2). 3. Whitelist gfx1151 in `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` → Triton `fp8e4nv` CompilationError in the AITER paged-MQA kernel (gate 3). ### Tested fix (cluster is serving with this) **a) `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`** — accept gfx1151 as AITER-capable: ```diff - from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx - - return on_mi3xx() + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx, on_gfx1151 + + return on_mi3xx() or on_gfx1151() ``` **b) `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — skip the AITER Triton module lookup on gfx1151 so the existing torch fallbacks run (same change in both dispatchers): ```diff - if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled(): + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151 + + # gfx1151: Triton cannot compile tl.dot with fp8e4nv inputs; skip the + # AITER Triton kernels so the torch reference fallback below is used. + if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151(): aiter_paged_mqa_logits_module = paged_mqa_logits_module() ``` ```diff + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151 + aiter_mqa_logits_module = None - if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled(): + if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151(): aiter_mqa_logits_module = mqa_logits_module() ``` The prefill dispatcher (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) needs the same gate: its AITER kernel performs the same fp8 `tl.dot` and fails identically on the first real prefill if only the paged path is patched. A cleaner resolution than piling onto the arch whitelist is probably per-kernel capability gating: dispatchers select the AITER Triton kernel only on archs where it is known to compile (mi3xx / gfx942 / gfx950 — the gfx942 special case already exists in `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`), else torch fallback — and gate 1's error message should not recommend an env var that gate 2 ignores. Happy to turn this into a PR if maintainers agree on the preferred shape. Note: the sparse-attention Triton kernels in the same file are unaffected — they dequantize fp8→bf16 in-kernel before `tl.dot` and compile fine on gfx1151. ### Secondary finding: torch fallback vs FULL cudagraph capture Once reachable, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` is not capture-safe (`.item()` / data-dependent host loops), but `@eager_break_during_capture` intentionally runs ops inline when `forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL` (`compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`), so FULL capture crashes: ``` File ".../rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 290, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item()) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing (hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported) ``` If the fallbacks become officially reachable, the op should be treated as non-capturable when the torch path is active (or cudagraph disabled for it). We run with `--enforce-eager` (also required on this cluster: piecewise capture deadlocked in RCCL NET/Socket collectives; related to #32180). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: vllm/vllm-openai:latest fails to start Gemma4 with Transformers 5.15.0
signals.text: ### Your current environment ```text Docker image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest vLLM: 0.27.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 Model: yasu-oh/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-NVFP4 Tensor parallel size: 2 KV cache dtype: fp8 ``` The Transformers version in the image can be confirmed with: ```bash docker run --rm \ --entrypoint python3 \ vllm/vllm-openai:latest \ -c 'import vllm, transformers; print("vLLM:", vllm.__version__); print("Transformers:", transformers.__version__)' ``` Output: ```text vLLM: 0.27.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug The current official release image `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` contains: ```text vLLM: 0.27.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 ``` When serving: ```text yasu-oh/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-NVFP4 ``` vLLM fails during startup with: ```text transformers.integrations.heterogeneity.configuration_utils.AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError: 'head_dim' is a per-layer attribute and may vary across layers. Access it via config.per_layer_config[i].head_dim. ``` The exception occurs in: ```text vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py ``` while accessing the Gemma4 `head_dim`. ### Workaround Downgrading only Transformers to 5.14.1 while keeping the same `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` base image and serving configuration resolves the issue. ```dockerfile FROM vllm/vllm-openai:latest RUN /usr/bin/python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir 'transformers==5.14.1' ``` With Transformers 5.14.1: * the same model loads successfully, * the vLLM engine initializes successfully, * the API server starts successfully, * `/v1/chat/completions` returns HTTP 200, * 32 concurrent requests run successfully. ## Related PRs * #49797 ? Fix Gemma 4 for upcoming Transformers version * #49959 ? Handle Transformers 5.15 Gemma4 schema ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.5 GDN CUDA kernels promote BF16 Q/K normalization to FP32
signals.text: ## Summary Qwen3.5's official BF16 GDN formula normalizes Q/K and computes beta in the activation dtype. vLLM currently promotes those operations to FP32 in its CUDA prefill and decode paths, then casts Q/K back to BF16. The difference compounds through recurrent state across GDN layers and can materially change cached decode likelihood on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. This is present in current vLLM `main` at `1044d19998df96408832b33ccc7120716c615969` and was measured on an Engram fork revision based on upstream `eca3041f0618118b960ce4423821a37748239255`. ## Official reference Transformers v5.5.3, commit `c6c8503869367af938666810e01a71866ca4fe93`, implements Q/K normalization as: ```python inv_norm = torch.rsqrt((x * x).sum(dim=dim, keepdim=True) + eps) return x * inv_norm ``` There is no `.float()` promotion, and beta is `b.sigmoid()`. With BF16 input, the multiplication, reduction result, reciprocal square root, normalized Q/K, and beta outputs are BF16. ## Affected vLLM paths - `fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py`: Q/K are loaded into FP32 before L2 norm; beta is also computed from an FP32-loaded value. - `fused_sigmoid_gating.py`: generic CUDA decode loads Q/K into FP32 before L2 norm and retains FP32 beta. - `fused_recurrent.py`: packed CUDA decode loads Q/K into FP32 before L2 norm. - Open PR #51674 adds a fused MTP CUDA decode kernel that likewise converts BF16 Q/K to float before its norm, so it should share the eventual semantic gate. No existing open issue or PR found by searches for Qwen3.5/GDN/l2norm, `fused_post_conv_prep`, or GDN normalization dtype addresses this correctness problem. PR #51674 is a performance path, not a duplicate fix. ## Measurements On a fixed official Qwen3.5-397B-A17B layer-12 input: - vLLM Q matches an FP32-normalize-then-BF16-cast variant exactly, while its relative L2 from the official BF16 formula is 0.2725%; K is 0.2695%. - Through the official recurrent fallback, changing only Q/K from BF16 to the FP32-promoted variant changes the recurrent core by 2.2951% relative L2. - Temporarily promoting only TorchTitan's Q/K, leaving beta, weights, recurrence, norm, and output projection unchanged, reduces vLLM-vs-reference relative L2 as follows: - recurrent core: 2.2765% -> 0.1496% - gated norm: 0.9860% -> 0.2713% - layer output: 0.9286% -> 0.3482% - At the selected first-divergent token, gated norm falls from 2.1971% to 0.2852%, and layer output falls from 2.3735% to 0.3901%. In a full 60-layer TP8 serving comparison, cached-decode NLL was 0.30910 in vLLM versus 0.40901 in the independent reference (0.09991 nat/token absolute, 24.43% relative on the small high-confidence decode NLL). Prefill, chunked prefill, aggregate, tokenizer identity, route normalization, loaded weights, and cache self-consistency were independently checked. A full patched rerun is still required before attributing the complete NLL residual to this fix. ## Expected behavior and proposed gate For Qwen3.5 BF16 activations, every CUDA prefill and incremental-decode path should exactly reproduce the official activation-dtype Q/K normalization and beta formula. A deliberate FP32-promotion variant should differ on a pinned sensitivity fixture. FP32 inputs should preserve current behavior. The fix should cover fused prefill, generic decode, packed decode, and any new fused MTP decode path together so backend selection cannot silently change model semantics.

skipped on the NVIDIA implementation because deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py requires every DeepseekV4DecoderLayer to expose hc_pre and hc_post, but the actual decoder layer does not define those attributes. As a result, TileLang mHC kernels such as mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang may be JIT-compiled during the first real inference workload, causing a significant latency spike or request timeout. Environment vLLM version: 0.25.0 Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, downloaded from Hugging Face and served from a local directory Architecture resolved by vLLM: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM model_type: deepseek_v4 Tensor parallel size: 8 KV cache dtype: fp8_ds_mla Device: NVIDIA CUDA trust_remote_code=False Server command: python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --max-model-len 65537 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --port 8001 Expected behavior During engine initialization, vLLM should run the explicit DeepSeek V4 mHC warmup and print logs similar to: Warming up DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang kernels for token sizes: [...] DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang warmup finished in ... seconds. The relevant TileLang mHC kernels should not be compiled during real inference. Actual behavior The mHC warmup logs never appear. The subsequent DeepSeek V4 sparse-MLA warmup does run on all TP workers: Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16. I added diagnostics immediately before the silent return in deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py. The result was: Skipping DSV4 mHC warmup: no matching layer; model_class=DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, model_type='deepseek_v4', candidates=[ ( 'DeepseekV4DecoderLayer', [ 'hc_attn_fn', 'hc_attn_scale', 'hc_attn_base', 'hc_ffn_fn', 'hc_ffn_scale', 'hc_ffn_base' ] ), ... ] Every decoder layer has the expected mHC parameters, but none has hc_pre or hc_post. Suspected root cause _find_first_mhc_layer() in deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py requires the following attributes: ( "hc_pre", "hc_post", "hc_attn_fn", "hc_attn_scale", "hc_attn_base", "hc_ffn_fn", "hc_ffn_scale", "hc_ffn_base", ) The warmup later invokes: layer_input, post_mix, comb_mix = layer.hc_pre(...) layer.hc_post(...) However, the NVIDIA DeepseekV4DecoderLayer does not define self.hc_pre or self.hc_post. Its forward() directly invokes module-level TileLang functions: mhc_pre_tilelang(...) mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang(...) mhc_post_tilelang(...) This mismatch is also visible in the current main branch: Warmup implementation:https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py NVIDIA decoder implementation:https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py The same mismatch appears in the v0.25.0 NVIDIA model implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.25.0/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py Because _find_first_mhc_layer() returns None, deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup() exits silently before its first informational log. Impact The intended mHC warmup is effectively disabled for this model path. TileLang kernels can therefore be compiled after the API server has started accepting production inference traffic. In my deployment, this results in latency spikes and can cause model-service request timeouts when an uncompiled mHC kernel is first encountered. Suggested fix Adapt _warmup_layer_mhc() to exercise the same functions used by DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward(): mhc_pre_tilelang mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang mhc_post_tilelang The warmup should pass the real normalization parameters as the inference path does: layer.attn_norm.weight.data layer.attn_norm.variance_epsilon layer.ffn_norm.weight.data layer.ffn_norm.variance_epsilon This is necessary to cover kernels such as: mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang Simply removing hc_pre and hc_post from the attribute check is not sufficient, because _warmup_layer_mhc() would then fail with an AttributeError when it tries to call those missing members. It may also be useful to log the reason whenever the warmup is skipped, rather than returning silently. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
