signals.title: [Quantization] Remove the dead ocp_mx_scheme branch from moe_kernel_quantize_input
signals.text: ## Purpose Shortly, remove dead code. `moe_kernel_quantize_input()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py` carries an `ocp_mx_scheme: str | None = None` parameter and opens its body with a block that short-circuits `*_a_fp8` OCP MX schemes into `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` before the normal `quant_dtype` dispatch ever runs. Nothing reaches that block. This PR removes the parameter and the block. This is the follow-up @fxmarty-amd asked for when introduced the `quantization_emulation` path that superseded the block, in #46142 (`e368415daa`): > [r3452957212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3452957212): > "Yes I don't think this code block is needed" > [r3453008225](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3453008225): > "Let's address in an other PR." This is the left TODO: ```python # TODO: Remove this `ocp_mx_scheme is not None` block and rely solely # on `quantization_emulation`. ``` and reconfirmed the ask in review on #43983 ([review 4904664996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983#pullrequestreview-4904664996)), linking `utils.py#L288-L301` — exactly the lines removed here. ### Why deleting it changes no behavior The only arm with behavior was `.endswith("a_fp8")`, and the only **reachable** a_fp8 scheme is `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` — `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_fp8` and `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, both raise `NotImplementedError` earlier, in `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`. For `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` the two paths are identical: | | deleted arm | surviving dispatch | |---|---|---| | condition | `ocp_mx_scheme.endswith("a_fp8")` | `quant_dtype == current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and `quantization_emulation` | | action | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` takes only `A` and `A_scale`, so nothing else was being bypassed. `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts.__init__` sets both inputs (`quantization_emulation = True`, `_quant_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()`), and `TritonExperts.apply` forwards them. ## Test Plan ### Unit test ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -q python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -q pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py ``` ### End-to-end test Same as what tested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983 - ROCm, MI325 - Model: amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 - MXFP4 emulation MoE backend --moe-backend emulation ## Test Result Coming soon. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Own prepared B12x W4A16 weights
signals.text: ## Purpose Draft stacked PR for the vLLM half of the explicit FlashInfer B12x W4A16 prepared-weight lifecycle. Dependencies: - vLLM #43929 supplies the W4A16 B12x routing and wrapper configuration. - FlashInfer #4560 supplies `prepare_weights()` and `run_prepared()`. Because #43929 comes from another contributor's fork, GitHub cannot use its head branch as the base of an upstream vLLM PR. The current diff therefore temporarily contains the three #43929 commits not already absorbed by `main`. Reviewers should review only the top commit, `13fafd778c2e5e7d06435838df82d7bf85312464`. This branch will be rebased to a single commit after #43929 merges. The top commit makes `FlashInferB12xExperts` prepare W4A16 weights during `process_weights_after_loading()`, retain the caller-owned prepared object, reuse the checkpoint weight storage, and execute with `run_prepared()`. The W4A4 path keeps the existing `run()` behavior. This avoids relying on FlashInfer's process-global source-pointer cache and avoids retaining a second packed W1/W2 allocation. It addresses the ownership boundary described in #49031. This is not a duplicate of #43929, which establishes W4A16 routing, or #48698, which shares B12x workspace across layers. No other open PR using `run_prepared()` in vLLM was found. AI assistance was used to implement, test, and prepare this PR. The submitter is responsible for reviewing the final diff before this Draft is marked ready. ## Test Plan 1. Install FlashInfer from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4560. 2. Run the SM120 B12x SiLU and ReLU2 tests for both W4A4 and W4A16. 3. Verify that prepared W4A16 W1/W2 tensors retain the source `data_ptr()` values when `reuse_input_storage=True`. 4. Load `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` with the FlashInfer B12x backend on SM120, capture a PIECEWISE CUDA Graph, and generate a deterministic response. 5. Run pre-commit on the full rebased stack relative to `main`. Commands used: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_b12x_moe.py E2E_CUDAGRAPH=1 .venv/bin/python /workspace/run_vllm_w4a16_e2e.py uvx pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD ``` ## Test Result - Target hardware: one NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell, 48 GiB, SM120. - Targeted B12x SiLU and ReLU2 tests passed for the validated W4A16 path. - Prepared W1 and W2 pointer-identity assertions passed, confirming that the packed object reused the checkpoint allocations. - `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` loaded with `moe_backend="flashinfer_b12x"`, captured the PIECEWISE CUDA Graph at batch size 1, and completed deterministic generation with 16 output tokens. - The corresponding FlashInfer lifecycle suite passed with 30 tests; its targeted CUDA Graph test also passed. - FlashInfer's isolated ownership benchmark reduced preparation allocation delta from 108 MiB to 12 MiB for E=64, H=1024, I=1024. The 96 MiB difference equals the source W1 and W2 storage. - CUDA Graph validation covered 1, 8, 64, and 256 tokens. Prepared-weight, workspace, input, and output pointers remained stable; eager and replay outputs had zero maximum absolute difference. - All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the full rebased stack. No separate model-quality evaluation was run because this changes weight ownership and dispatches the same prepared W4A16 kernel. Numerical equivalence is covered by the kernel-reference and eager-versus-graph comparisons above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: fix(security): account for peak GPU usage in PyNvVideoCodec pool lease
signals.text: The PyNvVideoCodec decode path charged only one RGB batch (B = F*H*W*3) against the frontend GPU memory pool, but during the lease up to three batch-sized GPU allocations are simultaneously live: native DLPack frames, the torch.stack result, and the contiguous NHWC tensor from permute().contiguous(). This allowed a request to pass admission while its real transient GPU usage exceeded the reserved pool budget by ~2-3x. Apply a 3x multiplier to the pool lease to cover the measured peak transient GPU allocation, preventing CUDA OOM from requests that fit within the raw-frame budget but exceed actual device headroom.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill
signals.text: ## Purpose On ROCm, Kimi-K3's KDA prefill chunk path currently runs a pipeline of nine Triton kernels. This PR adds a fusion path for ROCm that fuses these operations based on the characteristics of their workloads: **Prologue**: The kernel that prepares the chunks leading up to the recurrent state update. It normalizes `q` and `k`, cumsum gate into `g` and `beta`, builds `Aqk` in each chunk, inverts the transition `Akk`, and produces w and u. Each 64-token chunk can be processed in parallel, so it is dispatched in `(chunk, head)` grids for parallelism. **Chunk recurrence**: This does the remaining recurrence state update. For each sequence, the state update is sequential, and dispatching workgroups on the number of sequences can lead to low CU occupancy. This path breaks a sequence down into groups of chunks where the number of groups is determined by device capability, and takes a two-pass approach to increase parallelism within sequences: - Pass 1: Each group walks a recurrence from a zero state and records how it transforms an incoming state - Perform a scan across groups from a sequence to recover each group's true initial state - Pass 2: Re-walks each group from the correct start to produce outputs The fusion chain is ~2x faster than the Triton chain, especially in the chunk recurrance stage. E2E tests shows this reduces TTFT by ~4%. | tokens / seqs | Triton chunk stage | fused chunk stage | speedup | Triton chain | fused chain | speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1024 / 1 | 117.4 µs | 60.7 µs | 1.93× | 139.2 µs | 79.1 µs | 1.76× | | 4096 / 1 | 301.1 µs | 113.7 µs | 2.65× | 330.5 µs | 143.0 µs | 2.31× | | 4096 / 2 | 232.7 µs | 110.0 µs | 2.12× | 278.0 µs | 154.7 µs | 1.80× | | 4096 / 8 | 192.5 µs | 84.5 µs | 2.28× | 256.6 µs | 145.2 µs | 1.77× | | 16384 / 1 | 1174.2 µs | 335.9 µs | 3.50× | 1232.4 µs | 393.5 µs | 3.13× | The fusion path is packed into two pytorch interfaces that serve as a replacement for the original Triton chain. An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported. The kernels have only been tested on gfx950 at the moment, so its build and dispatch is guarded on gfx950 for now. ## Test Plan Unit tests for the fused kernels lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X Server command ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --load-format auto \ --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kda-prefill-backend ["fused" | "triton"] ``` Benchmark ``` vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos ``` lm_eval ``` lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234 ``` ## signals.title: [Bugfix][CI] Release the shared ColBERT engine before `test_colbert_hf_comparison`
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes the four failing `test_colbert_hf_comparison` tests. The failure was introduced by #52570 (commit `53e211d29`), which replaced the per-test runners in `tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py` with a module-scoped `colbert_model` fixture. Error message: > ValueError: Memory of devices devices=[0] not free after dur_s=240.14 (threshold='device=0: max(0.00 GiB, 0.080)') A module-scoped fixture is only finalized at the end of the module, so the engine of the last parametrization is still alive when the four `test_colbert_hf_comparison` tests declared in the same module, start their own runner. The live engine holds `gpu_memory_utilization` (0.92 by default) of the device, while a starting engine requires that same fraction to be free, so the second engine can never come up. The condition is proportional, so device size does not help. These tests cannot simply share the fixture's engine: they compare against a HuggingFace reference at `rtol=atol=1e-2` and therefore need `float32` rather than the fixture's `half`, and each one pins `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER`. So instead of sharing, the six tests that do share an engine now live in a class and their fixtures are class-scoped. pytest finalizes class-scoped fixtures when the class ends, before moving on to module-level tests, so the engine is always gone by the time `test_colbert_hf_comparison` runs. The startup savings of #52570 are kept: still one engine per model instead of one per test. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py ``` ## Test Result | Run | Result | Duration | | --- | --- | --- | | Before, whole file | 4 failed, 24 passed | 17m22s | | Before, `test_colbert_hf_comparison` alone | 4 passed | 2m49s | | After, whole file | **28 passed** | 2m57s | The four failures reproduce deterministically before the fix and only when the file is run as a whole, which confirms the shared engine as the cause. The run is also much faster afterwards, since the four VRAM waits that ended in a timeout are gone. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: fix: propagate precompiled wheel variant lookup failure instead of falling back
signals.text: Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52544 ## Summary For Python-only builds, when the precompiled-wheel metadata lookup for the selected CUDA variant fails, `setup.py` fell back to the root/default variant index. Nothing downstream checks that the fallback wheel matches the CUDA variant that was selected (or auto-detected) — the issue reporter hit exactly this: PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, its metadata lookup failed, and the fallback picked a native artifact requiring CUDA 13. The fix propagates the variant lookup failure instead of retrying the root index: once a variant is selected, only that variant's metadata is fetched. A wrong-CUDA wheel is worse than an install failure, because it fails far from the config that caused it. ## Verification - `setup.py` parses cleanly (`ast.parse`). - No other code path depends on the removed `try_default`/`download_filename` initializer — `download_filename` is still assigned in the wheel-selection branches that follow.

signals.title: fix(anthropic): convert tool_reference items to template-safe text
signals.text: Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52489 ## Summary `AnthropicServingMessages._convert_user_tool_result` converted `text` and `image` items inside a `tool_result` block into template-safe OpenAI content, but passed `tool_reference` items through **raw** (`{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}`). That raw dict went straight into a `tool`-role message's `content`, and strict Jinja chat templates (e.g. Qwen3's) hit their catch-all `raise_exception` branch — so any conversation containing a `tool_reference` block (common with Claude Code + multiple MCP servers, where the API's dynamic-tool-discovery lets a result reference another tool by name) failed on every subsequent request. Changed `tool_reference` items to a template-safe `text` item — `{"type": "text", "text": "[tool reference: {name}]"}` — mirroring how `text`/`image` are already handled. ## Test Added `test_tool_result_tool_reference_becomes_text` to `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`, asserting the converted `tool` message content is `done\n[tool reference: search_web]`. Conversion logic verified standalone (vLLM's full test env needs torch, unavailable here).

signals.title: Fix for Issue 52413: causal_conv1d Alignment Specialization Race Condition
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes issue #52413: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs. **Problem:** - Triton kernels allowed alignment specialization on dynamic metadata pointers that change per-request - This caused unnecessary inference-time JIT recompiles - Concurrent JIT cache writes led to corrupted kernels producing silent all-NaN outputs (data corruption) **Solution:** Added dynamic metadata pointers to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` in both `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` decorators to prevent alignment-based specialization. ## Test Plan - [x] Added regression test `test_causal_conv1d_metadata_ptrs_not_alignment_specialized()` that validates kernel decorators keep metadata pointers in alignment exemption list - [x] Test command: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --noconftest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d_jit_metadata.py` - [x] Verified fix doesn't break existing kernel signatures or math - [ ] Full causal_conv1d test suite on Linux with CUDA (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py`) ## Test Results - [x] Regression test **PASSED**: `test_causal_conv1d_metadata_ptrs_not_alignment_specialized` - [x] No compile errors in modified files - [x] Code changes verified to be minimal and isolated to kernel specialization metadata only - [ ] Full functional test suite pending (requires Linux CUDA environment) --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][gpt-oss] Strip matched stop string from Harmony reasoning/content
signals.text: FIX #52599 ## Problem For a non-streaming GPT-OSS chat completion, when a client `stop` string is matched, `finish_reason=stop` / `stop_reason` are correctly reported, but with `include_stop_str_in_output=false` the matched stop string is still present in the returned `reasoning` (or `content`) text. Repro in #52599. ## Root cause `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` (`vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`) already excludes a matched stop string from the character-level `output_text` when `include_stop_str_in_output` is false — but it deliberately keeps the stop-matching token in `self.token_ids` (needed elsewhere for correct usage/logprobs accounting; see the `skipped_stop_token_id` bookkeeping in `update()`). The chat serving layer (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py`) passes those untruncated `token_ids` straight into `HarmonyParser.parse()`, which reconstructs `reasoning`/`content` purely from token IDs via the Harmony streamable parser and never consults the truncated `output_text` at all. So the character-level stop-string truncation that every non-Harmony (text-based) reasoning parser inherits for free never reaches whichever Harmony channel the stop string lands in — this affects `content` too, not just `reasoning`; the issue happened to reproduce on `reasoning` because these prompts finish mid-analysis with `content: null`. ## Fix `HarmonyParser.parse()` now reuses `check_stop_strings()` — the same matching/truncation function the detokenizer already uses — and applies it to `reasoning` and `content` after the Harmony channel split, so both channels honor `include_stop_str_in_output` the same way the plain-text path does. ## Testing Added two tests to `tests/parser/test_harmony.py`: - `test_stop_string_stripped_from_reasoning`: a stop string matched inside the `analysis` channel is stripped when `include_stop_str_in_output=False`. - `test_stop_string_kept_when_include_stop_str_in_output`: unchanged when the flag is `True`. I verified the core stop-matching/truncation logic standalone against vLLM's real, unmodified `check_stop_strings` (exercised the exact repro string from #52599, multi-stop earliest-match tie-breaking, and the `include_stop_str_in_output=True` passthrough case) — all correct. I was not able to run the full `tests/parser/test_harmony.py` suite in my environment (no network access to pull the `openai/gpt-oss-20b` tokenizer / `openai_harmony` / `xgrammar`), so the added tests are unverified against the real Harmony parser end-to-end — flagging this explicitly for review rather than claiming full green CI. ## Known limitation This is scoped to the non-streaming `parse()` path, matching the reported repro. Streaming (`parse_delta()`) needs the equivalent of the detokenizer's `stop_buffer_length` buffering to avoid emitting a partial stop string before it's known to complete without more truncation; left as a follow-up rather than attempted here. ## AI assistance This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code), based on tracing the actual vLLM 0.27.0 source after reproducing the issue on NIM and the official upstream image. Marked as draft pending review and a real test run.
signals.author: lamduong0

signals.title: [Refactor][kv_offload]: rename `block`→`chunk`
signals.text: ## Purpose The KV offloading framework has two granularities: **block** (GPU allocator unit, one block-table entry) and **chunk** (offloading transfer unit, one or more blocks grouped via `blocks_per_chunk`). The code conflated them because `blocks_per_chunk` was historically always 1. This PR fixes the naming so "block" only refers to GPU blocks, and "chunk" refers to the offloading/tiering unit. No behavioral changes. Key renames: - `BlockStatus`→`ChunkSlotStatus`, - `_num_blocks`→`_num_chunks`, - `batch_store_block`→`batch_store_chunks`, - `BLOCK_QUERIES`→`CHUNK_QUERIES`, - `TransferJob.block_ids`→`TransferJob.chunk_slot_ids` (these were CPU slot indices, not GPU block IDs — the rename makes that explicit). ## Breaking changes Unreleased APIs, no external consumers: - `TransferJob.block_ids` → `.chunk_slot_ids` - `BlockStatus` → `ChunkSlotStatus` - C extension: `batch_store_block`/`batch_load_block` → `batch_store_chunks`/`batch_load_chunks` - Metrics: `*_block_queries` → `*_chunk_queries`, `*_block_hits` → `*_chunk_hits` ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [CPU] Add AMX-only high-performance MLA backend for DeepSeek V2/V3/R1
signals.text: ## Purpose Add `AMXMLABackend`/`AMXMLAImpl`, a high-performance MLA attention backend for CPU, built on AMX decode/extend/bmm/qkv-proj kernels vendored under `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/`. It plugs into the same `MLACommonBackend`/ `MLACommonImpl` abstraction every other concrete MLA backend uses. This is a separate, opt-in-by-capability backend alongside the existing reference `CPUMLABackend` (#49453): that one targets any CPU/dtype at block_size=16 as a functional/CI reference, not performance. This backend requires AMX (bf16 only, block_size a multiple of 32) and is preferred automatically by the platform layer when the host supports it, falling back to the reference backend otherwise (or when explicitly requested). ## What's included - Vendored SGLang AMX kernels (`decode.cpp`, `extend.cpp`, `bmm.cpp`, `qkv_proj.cpp`) under `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/`, AMX-only build-gated. - `AMXMLABackend`/`AMXMLAImpl` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/amx_mla.py`): weight absorption for prefill via VNNI-packed `W_UK`/`W_UV` computed once at load time; `forward_mha` attends directly against the paged latent cache in one causal pass (fresh prefill + cached-prefix continuation together, no GPU-style decompress-then-dense-attend); `forward_mqa` reuses the existing generic decode-side absorption. Per-step-invariant metadata (block-table expansion, `req_pool_indices`, `num_kv_splits`, `query_start_loc` derivatives) is computed once in `AMXMLAMetadataBuilder.build`, not recomputed per layer. - Platform wiring: `CpuPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` selects `AMX_MLA` when `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()` and x86 (unless the reference backend is explicitly requested); block-size/chunked-prefill config forcing is scoped to exclude the AMX path, since the extend kernel handles arbitrary prefix length and block size natively. - Two small, genuine bugs fixed in shared MLA code, both applicable beyond this backend: (1) CPU's generic `Linear` weight-packing path was freeing `kv_b_proj`'s raw weight before `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` could read it to derive `W_UK`/`W_UV`; (2) `get_mla_prefill_backend()` unconditionally resolves the CUDA-only `FlashAttnPrefillBackend` when `device_capability` is `None`, which asserts at construction time on CPU — fixed via a minimal inert CPU prefill backend registration. - Correctness tests (`tests/kernels/attention/test_amx_mla.py`), gated on `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()`, wired into the x86 CPU CI job. ## Tests ``` pytest -x -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_amx_mla.py ``` 10 passed (stable across repeated runs). ``` pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py ``` 1585 passed, 990 skipped, 0 failed — no regression to the existing dense `CPU_ATTN` backend from the shared-code changes. Also verified directly: offline single/multi-prompt inference (coherent, correct output on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`); a forced mixed decode+prefill batch (confirmed via temporary instrumentation that `num_decodes>0 and num_prefills>0` in the same step, output unaffected); tensor parallelism at TP1/TP2/TP4 (correct output, no crashes, expected sub-linear throughput scaling from cross-socket all-reduce overhead). ## Model evaluation GSM8K via `lm_eval` (5-shot, full 1319-question test set, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_gen_toks=512`, TP4, `AMX_MLA` selected): | Filter | Accuracy | Stderr | |---|---|---| | strict-match | 38.44% | ±1.34% | | flexible-extract | 38.51% | ±1.34% | Cross-checked against an independent third-party measurement of the same base model (vllm-ascend's own accuracy report, same `lm_eval` harness): strict-match 38.13%, flexible-extract 38.36% — within noise of this run. DeepSeek's own published number for this model is 41.1% (different harness/shot-count, same ballpark). `vllm bench serve` (1000 prompts, `random` dataset, 1024in/256out, TP4): 1000/1000 successful, 0 failed, 816.9 tok/s output throughput, 4084.3 tok/s total. Throughput scaling across TP1→TP2→TP4 (100-question GSM8K): 196.0 → 295.2 → 407.8 tok/s.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable medium-skinny dispatch in RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel
signals.text: ## Purpose Before this change, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` routed a decode GEMM to the HIP `wvSplitK_int4_g` kernel only when the activation row count was at most five (`M <= 5`) and the total activation size satisfied `K * M <= 32768`. The existing C++ operator supports up to five activation rows (`N_in <= 5`) and accepts `K_in * N_in` up to `int(max_lds_len * 1.2)`. With `max_lds_len = 32768`, the effective upper limit is `39321` elements. Python `M` maps to C++ `N_in`. For inputs above the regular LDS capacity, the medium kernel keeps the activation prefix in LDS and reads the remaining elements from global memory. Consequently, supported shapes with `K * M` between `32768` and `39321` (exclusive of the lower bound and inclusive of the upper bound) fell back to Triton instead of using the existing HIP kernel. This PR aligns the Python dispatch limit with the C++ operator contract. It also adds dispatch-boundary tests and numerical correctness coverage for the newly enabled range. No C++ kernel is changed. ## Duplicate-work check Open PR searches for medium-skinny, wvSplitK W4A16, and RDNA hybrid W4A16 found no duplicate. Related PRs #46186, #51511, and #50618 do not modify this hybrid dispatch threshold. ## Test Plan Test environment: All tests were run locally on the following system: | Component | Value | | --- | --- | | GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S | | GPU architecture | gfx1151 | | Memory | 128 GB unified memory (96 GiB VRAM, 32 GiB host-visible) | | Operating system | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS | | ROCm | 7.2.3 | The end-to-end comparison covered the two medium-skinny `down_proj` shapes below: | Model | Batch | `down_proj` shape | `K * M` | Before this PR | With this PR | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | --- | | `Qwen3-8B-GPTQ-Int4` | 3 | `M=3, K=12288, N=4096` | 36864 | Triton | HIP medium | | `Qwen3-4B-GPTQ-Int4` | 4 | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 38912 | Triton | HIP medium | The end-to-end benchmark used identical settings before and after this change: - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` with the `ROCM_ATTN` backend; - eager execution (`enforce_eager=True`), with HIP Graph and `torch.compile` disabled; - prefix caching disabled; - fixed prompts and random seed; - 512 output tokens per request with `temperature=0` and `ignore_eos=True`; - one warmup followed by three measured runs. Functional validation included dispatch tests at the regular and medium boundaries, FP16 and BF16 medium-kernel comparisons against an FP32 reference, and the complete hybrid W4A16 test file. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` were also run on the changed files. ## Test Result ### End-to-end decode performance Qwen3-8B (`batch=3`, `K * M=36864`): | Metric | Before this PR | With this PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Aggregate decode throughput | 41.70 tok/s | 68.16 tok/s | +63.43% | | Per-request decode throughput | 13.90 tok/s | 22.72 tok/s | +63.43% | | Batch wall time | 36.92 s | 22.60 s | -38.79% | Qwen3-4B (`batch=4`, `K * M=38912`): | Metric | Before this PR | With this PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Aggregate decode throughput | 119.30 tok/s | 126.83 tok/s | +6.31% | | Per-request decode throughput | 29.83 tok/s | 31.71 tok/s | +6.31% | | Batch wall time | 17.19 s | 16.16 s | -5.99% | ### Direct kernel timing | Shape | Triton | HIP medium | Speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `M=3, K=12288, N=4096` | 0.643 ms | 0.388 ms | 1.66x | | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 0.136 ms | 0.071 ms | 1.93x | ### Correctness and lint - Focused tests: 8 passed, 83 deselected - Complete hybrid W4A16 test file: 91 passed, 14 warnings - Applicable pre-commit hooks: passed - `git diff --check`: passed ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with this change. I reviewed and understand every submitted line and ran the validation reported above. No user-facing API or configuration is changed, so no documentation update is required. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and affected dispatch range are documented. - [x] Duplicate open PRs were searched and related PRs were reviewed. - [x] Test coverage and results are included. - [x] End-to-end and direct-kernel performance results are included. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] AI assistance is disclosed. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix] Honor stop strings in beam search
signals.text: ## Purpose When `use_beam_search=True`, stop strings from the Chat Completions and Completions APIs were not propagated to `BeamSearchParams`. In addition, the beam-search loops only completed beams on EOS, so a requested stop string was ignored and generation continued until EOS or `max_tokens`. This PR: - propagates `stop` from both `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`; - adds stop-string support to the shared `BeamSearchParams` contract; - applies the same stop matching behavior to online and offline beam search; - reuses the existing stop-string selection semantics, including overlapping stop strings and matches spanning token boundaries; - supports stop strings that end inside a token; - preserves the triggering token IDs and logprobs while truncating only the returned text, matching the regular detokenizer contract; - preserves the existing offline contract where `BeamSearchSequence.text` includes the prompt; and - keeps the no-stop path free of candidate detokenization overhead. ### Behavior before and after For example, assume a beam decodes to `"answer STOP trailing text"` and the request specifies `stop=["STOP"]`. | Behavior | Before this PR | After this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Stop parameter | Dropped while building `BeamSearchParams` | Propagated to online and offline beam search | | Termination | Beam continues until EOS or `max_tokens` | Beam completes as soon as `STOP` is matched | | Text with `include_stop_str_in_output=False` | May contain `STOP` and text generated after it | Returns `"answer "` | | Text with `include_stop_str_in_output=True` | May contain text generated after `STOP` | Returns `"answer STOP"` | | `finish_reason` | Usually `"length"` or an unrelated EOS stop | `"stop"` | | `stop_reason` | `None` or an unrelated token ID | `"STOP"` | | Triggering token IDs and logprobs | Generation continues past the match | Preserved through the token that completes the match | The same behavior applies when a stop string spans multiple tokens or ends in the middle of a decoded token. Stop matching only examines generated text, so a matching string in the prompt does not terminate the beam. ### Duplicate-work check I searched the open issues and PRs using `beam search stop`, `beam_search stop`, `stop strings beam`, and `include_stop_str_in_output beam`. I did not find an open PR implementing this fix. #36285 also modifies online beam search, but it adds structured-output support and does not address stop strings, so this PR is not a duplicate. ## Test Plan The regression tests use fake renderers and engine clients. They do not load a model or require a GPU. `--confcutdir` keeps the focused unit-test run isolated from repository-wide model/GPU fixtures. ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -r requirements/cpu.txt pytest pytest-asyncio .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/samplers \ tests/samplers/test_beam_search_offline.py \ tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py -v ``` The tests cover: - online and offline stop-string termination; - stop strings spanning multiple tokens; - stop strings ending inside a token; - `include_stop_str_in_output=True` and `False`; - termination before `max_tokens`; - preservation of triggering token IDs; - `finish_reason` and `stop_reason`; and - propagation from both Chat Completions and Completions requests. Static checks were also run on all changed Python files: - `ruff check` - `ruff format --check` - the Python 3.12 mypy pre-commit hook - the typos pre-commit hook - Python AST parsing - `git diff --check` ## Test Result ```text ============================== 7 passed in 5.81s =============================== ``` All listed static checks passed. The original issue was also reproduced before the change and confirmed fixed after the change by the submitter in a GPU environment. The expected observable result is the before/after behavior documented above; model execution and beam scores before the stop match remain unchanged. ### Model evaluation No model-quality evaluation was run because this change does not modify model execution, logits, beam scores, or candidate token selection. Stop matching is performed after candidate logprobs have already been returned and only changes whether a candidate is moved to the completed-beam set. The affected output contract is covered by the CPU-only behavioral regression tests above. ### Documentation No documentation update is required. This restores the documented `stop` behavior for beam-search requests without introducing a new API.
signals.author: gakkiri

signals.title: [Bugfix] Return 4xx for client-caused errors in /detokenize
signals.text: ## Purpose `POST /detokenize` wraps `create_detokenize` in a blanket `except Exception` that reports every failure as HTTP 500. Its sibling `POST /tokenize` in the same file has no such wrapper, so its exceptions reach the global exception handlers registered by `init_exception_handler`, which map client-caused errors to 4xx (`VLLMValidationError` to 400, `VLLMNotFoundError` to 404, raw `ValueError`/`TypeError`/`OverflowError` to 400) and keep genuine server errors at 500. The two endpoints therefore disagree on identical client errors: | error raised by the serving layer | /tokenize | /detokenize before | /detokenize after | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `VLLMValidationError` | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `VLLMNotFoundError` | 404 | 500 | 404 | | `ValueError` | 400 | 500 | 400 | | `RuntimeError` (real server bug) | 500 | 500 | 500 | `create_detokenize` can surface client-caused errors in practice, for example through `_maybe_get_adapters` (bad LoRA adapter name) and `renderer.tokenize_prompt_async`. This is the same class of bug fixed for the Anthropic entrypoint in #52246: client-caused errors must be 4xx, never 500. The fix removes the wrapper so `/detokenize` takes the exact shape of `/tokenize`. Genuine server errors still return 500 through the global `Exception` safety-net handler, as the last table row shows. ### Why the `OverflowError` special case is dropped rather than kept The old code re-raised `OverflowError` as a `RequestValidationError`. Dropping it does not change the status code: - vLLM's `validation_exception_handler` returns 400 for `RequestValidationError`. - The global `OverflowError` fallback (`create_error_response`) also returns 400. Only the error body changes: the response now has the platform-standard shape (`type: "BadRequestError"` with the raw exception message) that `/tokenize` and every other endpoint produce, instead of a wrapped `1 validation error: ...` message with `type: "Bad Request"`. Fast tokenizers do raise `OverflowError` for out-of-range token ids, so the path is real, and the regression test pins its 400. ### Scope Other blanket `except Exception` handlers under `vllm/entrypoints/` are left alone deliberately: `serve/dev`, `serve/elastic_ep`, and `serve/fault_tolerance` are admin/dev endpoints rather than client-input surfaces, and `cohere/api_router.py` is annotated `# noqa: BLE001 - report as 500 for parity`, a deliberate choice. The `mode="before"` validator hardening from #52528 is already complete repo-wide, so nothing to do there. A search of open PRs for detokenize and tokenize router work found no overlapping PR. ## Test Plan New `TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses` in `tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_serving_tokenization.py`, mirroring `TestClientErrorResponses` from #52246. It builds the real router plus the real global exception handlers, mocks `ServingTokenization`, and asserts: - `VLLMValidationError` returns 400 with `param` propagated - `VLLMNotFoundError` returns 404 - `ValueError` returns 400 - `OverflowError` returns 400 (pins the status code of the removed special case) - `RuntimeError` still returns 500 - `/tokenize` and `/detokenize` return the same status for the same client error ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_serving_tokenization.py pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/ ``` ## Test Result New tests against the old handler (fix reverted): 6 failed, all 4xx cases came back as 500. ```text FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_vllm_validation_error_returns_bad_request FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_vllm_not_found_error_returns_not_found FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_value_error_returns_bad_request FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_overflow_error_returns_bad_request FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_server_error_still_returns_internal_server_error FAILED ...::TestDetokenizeClientErrorResponses::test_tokenize_and_detokenize_agree_on_client_errors 6 failed, 2 deselected ``` With the fix: ```text tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_serving_tokenization.py: 8 passed tests/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/: 39 passed ``` Live server check (`vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` on the CPU backend): ```text POST /tokenize {"prompt": "Hello world"} -> 200 POST /detokenize {"tokens": [9906, 1917]} -> 200 POST /detokenize {"tokens": [4611686018427387904]} -> 400 {"error": {"message": "out of range integral type conversion attempted", "type": "BadRequestError", ...}} POST /detokenize {"model": "no-such-model", ...} -> 404 NotFoundError ``` The third case is the real OverflowError path: a token id inside the protocol's int64 bound but beyond the fast tokenizer's range keeps its 400 through the global handler. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both changed files, and mypy (CI configuration via `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`) reports no issues. This change was developed with AI assistance; I reviewed and tested every line.

signals.title: fix: fix ovis2_5 multimodal tokens
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix multimodal tokens for ovis 2_5 processor ## Test Plan vllm serve ATH-MaaS/Ovis2.5-2B --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 1, "image": 0}' --enforce-eager 2>&1 | tee /results/ovis_video_server.log curl --retry-connrefused --retry 60 --retry-delay 10 -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model": "ATH-MaaS/Ovis2.5-2B", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What'\''s in this video? answer in english"}, {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/raushan-testing-hf/videos-test/resolve/main/sample_demo_1.mp4"}}]}], "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0}' | tee /results/ovis_video_query.log ## Test Result Logs after changes: [ovis_video_query.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31142606/ovis_video_query.log) [ovis_video_server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31142610/ovis_video_server.log) Without the modification, vllm raises: File "/workspace/local/vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py", line 286, in call_hf_processor output = hf_processor(**data, **allowed_kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/workspace/local/vllm/transformers_utils/processors/ovis2_5.py", line 219, in __call__ tokenized_batched_text = self._tokenize_with_visual_symbol(text) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/workspace/local/vllm/transformers_utils/processors/ovis2_5.py", line 292, in _tokenize_with_visual_symbol return torch.tensor(batch_token_ids, dtype=torch.long) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer --- <details> Pr #47298 after refactor did not fully fix ovis models, due to ` self.tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(token_name)` referencing an tokenizer unmodified by `self.tokenizer.add_tokens()`. This alleviated the `"Can not find {token_name}", but the returned token ids were `None`, which caused further problems. This pr uses `self.tokenizer.get_added_vocab()` gets tokens from different source, which is affected by `self.tokenizer.add_tokens()`. signals.title: [Helm] Support custom affinity configuration
signals.text:
Assisted-by: Codex ## Purpose Fixes #38308. The Helm chart previously supported scheduling only through `gpuModels` , which renders a GPU-product-specific `nodeAffinity`. This prevented users from configuring generic `nodeAffinity`, `podAffinity`, or `podAntiAffinity` without selecting a GPU product label. This PR adds a first-class `affinity` value. A non-empty custom affinity is rendered as-is and takes precedence over `gpuModels`. When `affinity` is empty, the existing `gpuModels` fallback remains available for deployments with positive NVIDIA GPU requests and limits. This does not duplicate an open PR. No open PR was found for #38308 or Helm affinity configuration. #38310 addressed the same issue but was closed because of merge conflicts. Compared with #38310, this PR: - Updates the implementation for the current `examples/deployment/chart-helm` layout. - Adds `affinity` to the values schema and documents its precedence and legacy fallback behavior. - Keeps `runtimeClassName: nvidia` independent of affinity selection. - Adds regression coverage for custom-affinity precedence, legacy fallback, CPU-only custom affinity, and GPU request/limit edge cases. ## Test Plan - Run pre-commit on all changed files. - Run Helm lint and unit tests. - Run `git diff --check`. - Manually validate scheduling on a three-node CPU-only Kubernetes cluster with the same custom `nodeAffinity` and `podAntiAffinity` values before and after the change. ## Test Result - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files ` - Passed - `helm lint examples/deployment/chart-helm` - Passed (one informational icon recommendation) - `helm unittest examples/deployment/chart-helm` - Passed: 5 test suites, 16 tests - `git diff --check` - Passed ### Kubernetes scheduling validation The attached before/after screenshot was captured on a three-node CPU-only Kubernetes cluster: #### Before #### After - Before: the legacy chart ignored custom affinity; the peer Pod and vLLM Pod were both scheduled on `k8s-worker1`. - After: the peer Pod remained on `k8s-worker1`, while the vLLM Pod was scheduled on `k8s-worker2`. - All displayed Pods were `Running`. ## Model Evaluation N/A — this is a Kubernetes scheduling/chart configuration change. It does not change model output, accuracy, or the vLLM serving runtime. ## AI Assistance AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation and test development. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the validation commands listed above. ---

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4 mHC broadcast buffer for weight sync
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix Stale broadcast weights after refit. finalize_mhc_broadcast_weights() rebound layer.hc_attn_fn_broadcast to a freshly-allocated tensor on every call. CUDA graphs captured against the original tensor's address keep replaying with the old pointer, so a weight refit (repeat load_weights() after capture, e.g. RL weight sync) left captured graphs reading stale broadcast weights. Fixed by allocating only when the buffer is None and otherwise copy_()-ing in place, keeping the address stable. ## Test Plan Two unit tests added to tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py: 1. test_deepseek_v4_mhc_broadcast_finalize_sums_hc_streams — first finalize allocates the buffer with the stream-summed values. 2. test_deepseek_v4_mhc_broadcast_refit_refreshes_in_place — after mutating hc_attn_fn and re-finalizing, the buffer is the same tensor object with updated values (the refit contract). pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -k mhc_broadcast -v pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py -k "hc_head_tilelang or mhc_broadcast" End to end tests on verl side with DSV4 training ## Test Result - -k mhc_broadcast: 2 passed. - Combined with the tilelang hc_head kernel tests (which flip torch.set_default_device to CUDA earlier in the file): 10 passed. - Full file collects all 53 tests cleanly. - Mutation check: with the model.py fix reverted to HEAD, the refit test fails on the buffer-identity assertion and the sums test still passes — the pair pins both the pre-existing semantics and the new in-place contract. - End to end tests on verl side with DSV4 training returned to normal training inference mismatch. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [X] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [X] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [X] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [ROCm] Enable fused AR draft metadata updates for DeepSeek V4
signals.text: Builds on vLLM PR #46849, which restores fused multi-step draft decode graphs for autoregressive speculative decoding when every attention backend can update step-dependent draft metadata in place. That PR left DeepSeek V4 ROCm sparse SWA disabled because the AMD path also materializes ROCm-specific ragged SWA indices and indptrs. Enable the ROCm DeepSeek V4 AITER SparseSWA metadata builder for fused draft decode by refreshing its ragged SWA representation after the generic dense SWA update. The refresh writes directly into the persistent metadata buffers returned by build(), avoiding temporary ragged flat/indptr allocations so captured HIPGraph replay keeps stable tensor storage addresses. Add focused tests for the direct-to-buffer helper and in-place metadata update. Validation used TP4 on MI355X against patched and control images built from vllm/main@c4e9692. Runtime logs confirmed the patched image used the fused speculator graph path, while control logged fallback because DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA did not support fused multi-step draft decode metadata updates. Smoke, GSM8K, c16, and c128 runs completed with no HIPGraph/cudagraph replay errors, illegal memory access, stale metadata symptoms, or failed benchmark requests. Serve command shape: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --attention_backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN"}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --max_model_len 4096 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max_num_seqs 256 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --trust-remote-code Accuracy command shape: lm_eval --model local-completions \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 8 \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:<PORT>/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False Accuracy results, full GSM8K 8-shot, no limit: patched flexible/strict: 0.9492 / 0.9500 control flexible/strict: 0.9416 / 0.9424 Benchmark command shapes: vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --temperature 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 16 \ --num-prompts 160 \ --num-warmups 16 vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --temperature 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 128 \ --num-prompts 1024 \ --num-warmups 128 Performance results, output throughput: c16 patched/control: 2000.58 / 1958.82 tok/s (+2.13%) c128 patched/control: 7852.55 / 7751.43 tok/s (+1.30%)

signals.title: [Test] Add a prefix-caching x tool-calling gate
signals.text: ## Purpose Agentic deployments run prefix caching and tool calling together — repeated system prompts and tool definitions are exactly the prefix a cache is meant to reuse — yet no test exercises the combination: the per-parser tests never boot an engine, and the tool-calling e2e tests never enable prefix caching. A regression that only appears when the cache engages is invisible today. Adds `tests/tool_use/test_prefix_cache_tool_calling.py`, which boots the same tool-calling server with prefix caching off and on and asserts (1) a well-formed, schema-conformant tool call in both configurations, and (2) that under the caching configuration the cache was *actually exercised* (`vllm:prefix_cache_queries` and `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` non-zero, and zero in the control arm). Assertion 2 keeps the gate honest: a cache that never engaged would pass while proving nothing. Test-only; requires a GPU and a small model, so it suits a nightly or opt-in tier rather than a blocking gate. ## Test Plan Run on 1 GPU: `pytest tests/tool_use/test_prefix_cache_tool_calling.py -v` ## Test Result | Run | Result | |---|---| | As filed (GB200, recent dev build, Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) | 3 passed, 1 skipped (control-arm skip by design) | | Planted defect — caching arm secretly booted with caching disabled | exactly 1 failed: the cache-engagement assertion; tool-calling assertions stayed green | Counter helper probed against 6 synthetic expositions (with/without `_total`, multi-engine labels summed, `_created` ignored, absent series -> 0, trailing timestamp not misread): 6/6. ruff 0.14.0 (`check` + `format --check`) clean. Searched open PRs and the tree for existing prefix-caching x tool-calling coverage: none found. Written with AI assistance (Claude); I have reviewed and validated every line. Model evaluation results: N/A (test-only change).

signals.title: [Bugfix] DeepEP-V2: expert_tokens_meta must be None on the decode/cudagraph path (empty recv_expert_num_tokens)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix a deterministic startup crash in graph-enabled (default-compilation) serving with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`. In `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize._receiver`, `expert_tokens_meta` was built unconditionally via `mk.ExpertTokensMetadata.make_from_list(recv_expert_num_tokens, ...)`. On the decode/cudagraph path, `do_cpu_sync = not self.use_cudagraph` (this file) intentionally skips the CPU sync, leaving `recv_expert_num_tokens` **empty** — so the call builds a **present-but-empty** `ExpertTokensMetadata`. That violates the decode-mode contract documented at the top of this file (`expert_tokens_meta` must be `None` when counts are absent), and downstream it crashes DeepEP's `combine` during startup `profile_run`. Measured, two independent reproductions of the same call path (`profile_run → finalize_async → DeepEP elastic.py combine`): - H200/B200, EP16 (DP16, 2 nodes over EFA, NCCL-GIN CPU proxy): Triton illegal-memory-access at `deepep_v2.py` combine, 12+/16 ranks, deterministic ~48 s into startup, 2/2 repro (Xid 43, ECC clean). - Independently reproduced by AWS on B300, EP16, DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16: `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (719)` raised from DeepEP's JIT handle at the same phase — one root cause surfacing at different synchronization points. `--enforce-eager` avoids the crash (the sync happens); this guard makes default compilation safe. ## Changes One guard: return `expert_tokens_meta = None` when `recv_expert_num_tokens` is empty (the decode/cudagraph path), matching the documented contract; the prefill path (`do_cpu_sync=True`) is unchanged. ## Test Plan / Validation - With the guard applied at `e2f993dc4`-era pins: graph-enabled `vllm serve` (no `--enforce-eager`) on EP16/DP16 across 2 nodes over EFA completes CUDA-graph capture, reaches `Application startup complete`, and serves: 153/153 HTTP 200 across a 1/8/16/32/64 concurrency sweep (previously: deterministic crash in `profile_run` before startup completed). - Eager path unaffected (guard only changes the empty-list case).

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix no-op num_blocks division in get_moe_wna16_block_config
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52590. In `get_moe_wna16_block_config` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`), the 256-branch reassigns `block_size_k` to `256` *before* using it as the divisor: ```python if size_k % 256 == 0 and num_blocks >= 256 and block_size_k < 256: block_size_k = 256 num_blocks = num_blocks // (256 // block_size_k) # 256 // 256 == 1, always a no-op ``` Since `block_size_k` is already `256` by the time it's used as the divisor, `256 // block_size_k` is always `1`, so `num_blocks` never actually shrinks. The very next branch in the same function does this correctly — it divides using the pre-doubling block size before doubling it: ```python if (num_m_blocks <= 16 and ... and num_blocks >= 512): block_size_k = block_size_k * 2 num_blocks = num_blocks // 2 ``` This PR reorders the two statements in the 256-branch to match that pattern, so the division actually uses the old `block_size_k` (128, the common initial default): ```python if size_k % 256 == 0 and num_blocks >= 256 and block_size_k < 256: num_blocks = num_blocks // (256 // block_size_k) block_size_k = 256 ``` An artificially-inflated `num_blocks` can stay above the `num_blocks > 1024` threshold a few lines later when it shouldn't, which flips `BLOCK_SIZE_N` to `1024` instead of `256` for shapes that should cross that boundary — i.e. this silently picks the wrong CUDA MoE WNA16 kernel tiling for affected shapes. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Checked `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open` against `get_moe_wna16_block_config`, `moe_wna16 block_size_k`, and the issue number in-body. Four open PRs touch this function or file but none touches this specific no-op-division defect: - #40547 / #48751 — both remove a *duplicated* `if` condition elsewhere in the same function (a redundant repeated check, not this divisor bug). - #44563 — clamps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` so `BLOCK_SIZE_K // group_size` stays in `{1,2,4,8}`; a different, unrelated constraint on the final block size. - #52577 — fixes an out-of-bounds weight load in the Triton `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` kernel and a scale-indexing bug in `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm`; neither touches `get_moe_wna16_block_config`. None of these change the 256-branch's divisor calculation, so this is not duplicate work. ## Test commands run and results ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_wna16_block_config.py -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_wna16_block_config.py::test_get_moe_wna16_block_config_256_branch_actually_halves_num_blocks PASSED tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_wna16_block_config.py::test_get_moe_wna16_block_config_256_branch_affects_block_size_n PASSED 2 passed in 0.80s ``` Added `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_wna16_block_config.py`, a new pure-Python (no GPU required) regression test covering `get_moe_wna16_block_config` directly. The second test's shape was chosen so the bug and fix diverge not just internally but in the returned `BLOCK_SIZE_N` (`1024` under the bug vs. `256` under the fix) — verified by temporarily reverting the fix locally and confirming both tests fail against the unfixed code with exactly that mismatch (`assert 1024 == 256`). Also ran, with no regressions: ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -v # 1 skipped (CUDA-gated, expected on this CPU-only macOS box) $ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_wna16_block_config.py # ruff check/format, typos, mypy: all Passed $ pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py --hook-stage manual # Passed ``` Built vLLM from source for CPU on macOS/arm64 per `.github/workflows/macos-smoke-test.yml` (`uv pip install -r requirements/build/cpu.txt && uv pip install -r requirements/cpu.txt && uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`) to run the above against the real package; `import vllm` succeeds afterward. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance (Claude) was used to locate, diagnose, and fix this bug, and to write the regression test. I reviewed the diff line-by-line, independently hand-derived and cross-checked the arithmetic for both test shapes against the function's actual branch order (including the `_ensure_block_size_k_divisible` post-processing step), and verified the test fails against the unfixed code before submitting.

signals.title: [ROCm][MoRI][BugFix] Fix combine() using dispatched topk_ids instead of original
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes a correctness bug in vLLM's MoRI (`--all2all-backend mori_high_throughput` / `mori_low_latency`) expert-parallel integration that causes garbled/incoherent output at higher expert-parallel degree (confirmed broken at EP32 across 4 nodes; confirmed correct at EP8 and EP16, model-dependent — see Test plan). `MoriPrepareAndFinalize.finalize()` calls `mori_op.combine()` with the `topk_ids` argument it is passed by `modular_kernel.py`'s `forward()`. By the time `finalize()` runs, that variable has already been overwritten with the **dispatched** (post-`prepare()`) `topk_ids` returned by `mori_op.dispatch()` — correct for driving the local expert GEMM, but wrong for `combine()`. MoRI's combine kernel uses these ids (via `tokenIndices`) to decide, for each of *this* rank's own tokens, which remote nodes' partial expert outputs to gather and sum. The dispatched ids instead describe the routing of *other* ranks' tokens that were routed to this rank's local experts — not the original routing of this rank's own tokens — so `combine()` ends up gathering from the wrong set of nodes. The resulting corruption gets worse as expert-parallel degree increases (more tokens routed to remote ranks), which matches the observed EP8/EP16-clean, EP32-broken pattern. ## Test Plan Verified against Qwen3-30B-A3B (non-disaggregated) - **Qwen3-30B-A3B** (Qwen3MoeForCausalLM) across three expert-parallel degrees (EP8 = 1 node, EP16 = 2 nodes, EP32 = 4 nodes, 8 GPUs/node). Two accuracy checks per configuration: 1. **10-prompt known-answer probe** (greedy, temp=0) — checks the exact expected answer appears and flags degenerate/repeated-token output. 2. **GSM8K, full 1319-question test set**, 5-shot, greedy (temp=0), via vLLM's own `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against the live server. ## Test Result | Config | Nodes | Probe (before fix) | GSM8K-1319 (before fix) | Probe (after fix) | GSM8K-1319 (after fix) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | EP8 | 1 | 10/10, 0 degenerate | 89.31% (0.00% invalid) | 10/10, 0 degenerate | 88.70% (0.00% invalid) | | EP16 | 2 | 10/10, 0 degenerate | 88.78% (0.00% invalid) | 10/10, 0 degenerate | 89.23% (0.00% invalid) | | EP32 | 4 | **3/10, 2 degenerate** | **18.95% (0.53% invalid)** | 10/10, 0 degenerate | **89.31% (0.00% invalid)** | - EP8 and EP16 are unaffected by the bug either way — GSM8K accuracy is ~88-89% both before and after the fix, confirming the fix does not regress already-working configurations. - EP32 before the fix collapses to 18.95% GSM8K accuracy (vs. the ~89% every other configuration achieves) — a large-magnitude, quantitative confirmation of the failure, not just visibly garbled text. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [EPLB] Add contention-aware expert migration batching
signals.text: Partially addresses #31671. This PR implements a focused part of the EPLB execution optimization proposed in #31671: scheduling expert-migration instructions to reduce communication contention. The batching strategy is inspired by the greedy instruction-scheduling approach referenced in Omni/OmniInfer, adapted to vLLM's existing EPLB communicator and migration paths. ## Purpose EPLB currently submits every remote expert transfer in one communicator execution. When a rank communicates with several peers, those flows contend for the same NIC and can interfere with inference during asynchronous rebalancing. This PR adds an opt-in `enable_migration_batching` setting. It builds the global migration graph deterministically and greedily groups directed rank-pair flows so that each rank communicates with at most one peer in a batch. Transfers for the same rank pair remain coalesced. Batches execute sequentially, reducing instantaneous network contention while preserving the existing transfer path when the setting is disabled. The implementation supports both synchronous and asynchronous EPLB and uses the current communicator interface, including resetting per-transfer context for every batch (required by communicators such as NIXL that clear their context after `execute()`). This PR focuses only on the instruction-scheduling part of #31671. It does not implement the other proposed components such as topology-aware expert placement, custom initialization, or the C++ scheduling backend. AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. The human submitter reviewed every changed line before marking it ready for review and is responsible for understanding and defending the implementation. ## Test Plan Unit tests cover: - opt-in configuration behavior; - deterministic, rank-pair-disjoint batching; - coalescing transfers for the same directed rank pair; - complete coverage of randomized migration graphs; - local-copy exclusion and balanced source selection; - repeated communicator context setup across batches; and - duplicate-expert receive-buffer selection. Commands: ~~~bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/config/parallel.py \ vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py \ vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py \ vllm/distributed/eplb/migration_scheduler.py \ vllm/distributed/eplb/rebalance_execute.py \ tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py ~~~ Serving evaluation used four Quadro RTX 6000 24 GB GPUs (one GPU per node), `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, TP=4, expert parallelism, 16 redundant experts, an EPLB window of 50 steps, a 100-step rearrangement interval, and prefix caching enabled. Synchronous runs used `torch_nccl`; asynchronous runs used `torch_gloo`. Each configuration started a fresh server. Two cache-on workloads were tested: 1. 200 random requests, 300 shared-prefix tokens, 200 random input tokens, 100 output tokens, concurrency 32. 2. 256 ordered English requests in eight 32-request domain phases (CUDA, literature, mathematics, biomedical, repeated twice), with a shared prefix, 100 output tokens, concurrency 32, and shuffling disabled. This caused 8–9 rebalancing triggers during a run. NIC values are not emitted by `vllm bench serve`. They are the sum of receive and transmit byte-rate samples from the head node's data interface at one-second intervals, cropped to the benchmark time window. ## Test Results - Unit tests: `8 passed`. - All pre-commit hooks for the changed files passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, configuration validation, and forbidden-import checks. - All serving requests completed successfully with zero failures. ### Random workload, prefix cache enabled | Mode | Batching | Duration (s) | Output (tok/s) | E2EL P99 (ms) | NIC P99 (MB/s) | NIC peak (MB/s) | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | sync | off | 988.94 | 20.22 | 186001.25 | 1852.22 | 1930.67 | | sync | on | 1067.07 | 18.74 | 200128.55 | 1153.45 | 1210.99 | | async | off | 889.51 | 22.48 | 162839.73 | 707.21 | 802.06 | | async | on | 875.30 | 22.85 | 161767.77 | 649.08 | 701.98 | | Mode | Batching | TTFT P50 (ms) | TTFT P99 (ms) | TPOT P50 (ms) | TPOT P99 (ms) | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | sync | off | 40131.95 | 84048.68 | 1095.51 | 1478.92 | | sync | on | 40319.07 | 85214.08 | 1209.60 | 1593.21 | | async | off | 40601.85 | 81621.22 | 942.43 | 1347.07 | | async | on | 40392.90 | 82462.42 | 929.03 | 1328.39 | For the primary async comparison, batching improved output throughput by **1.6%**, reduced NIC P99 by **8.2%**, and reduced peak NIC rate by **12.5%**. ### Phased English workload, prefix cache enabled | Mode | Batching | Duration (s) | Output (tok/s) | E2EL P99 (ms) | NIC P99 (MB/s) | NIC peak (MB/s) | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | sync | off | 952.94 | 26.86 | 134590.88 | 1829.08 | 1982.54 | | sync | on | 1052.99 | 24.31 | 156878.38 | 1161.40 | 1208.52 | | async | off | 845.10 | 30.29 | 108864.96 | 799.65 | 914.92 | | async | on | 815.56 | 31.39 | 104369.71 | 705.32 | 770.31 | | Mode | Batching | TTFT P50 (ms) | TTFT P99 (ms) | TPOT P50 (ms) | TPOT P99 (ms) | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | sync | off | 38503.30 | 67659.84 | 795.31 | 1129.39 | | sync | on | 38687.32 | 80047.90 | 921.92 | 1259.57 | | async | off | 38197.97 | 58619.07 | 693.25 | 1033.79 | | async | on | 38335.24 | 59520.39 | 653.61 | 998.35 | For the primary async comparison, batching improved output throughput by **3.6%**, reduced E2EL P99 by **4.1%**, reduced NIC P99 by **11.8%**, and reduced peak NIC rate by **15.8%**. The synchronous results show the expected tradeoff: sequential batches reduce network peaks substantially but increase stop-the-world migration time. The intended use is asynchronous EPLB, where lower migration-induced network contention improves serving throughput and tail latency in both tested workloads. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is explained. - [x] The related RFC / issue is documented. - [x] The test commands are provided. - [x] Unit and serving results are included. - [x] No documentation update is required because the setting is an EPLB config field with inline documentation. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

signals.title: [Bugfix] Encode special tokens found in text for MistralCommonBackend in multimodal processors
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #50706 vLLM crashes at engine startup for Mistral3/Pixtral "dual-format" checkpoints (repos shipping both HF tokenizer files and Mistral-native `tekken.json`/`params.json`, e.g. `nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4`, `mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B`). Under transformers 5.x, `AutoTokenizer` resolves these to `MistralCommonBackend`, which never encodes special tokens (e.g. `"[IMG]"`) found in plain text. During dummy multimodal input profiling (run at engine startup to size the encoder budget), `PixtralProcessor` counts a mismatch between the placeholder in the templated text and the encoded ids and raises: ``` ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1]. ValueError: Failed to apply PixtralProcessor on data={'text': '[IMG]'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'} ``` `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` now swaps in a `MistralCommonBackend` subclass (`with_placeholder_token_support`) that resolves known special-token strings found in text back to their ids, scoped only to the tokenizer instance handed to HF processors — never used for general/user-prompt tokenization. Conceptually related to but independently derived from: - #50752 — fixes the same root cause on the default tokenizer-mode path (currently blocked on the contributor-gate CI check, not real test failures) - #45525 — fixes the sibling issue (#45289) for `--tokenizer-mode mistral` ## Test Plan - Unit tests: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py -q` — 8 new tests against a real `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` tokenizer, covering: bug repro (stock backend doesn't encode `[IMG]`), fix correctness, memoization/idempotency, plain-text passthrough (unaffected by the change), placeholder-prefix disambiguation (`[IMG]` vs `[IMG_BREAK]`/`[IMG_END]`), and `add_special_tokens` behavior. - Manual end-to-end repro against a real dual-format checkpoint, exercising the same code path as engine-startup profiling: ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY model_config = ModelConfig( "unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", tokenizer="unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", tokenizer_revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", max_model_len=8192, ) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) mm_inputs = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.get_dummy_mm_inputs( model_config, mm_counts={"image": 1}, processor=processor, ) ``` - `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/utils/mistral.py vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py` ## Test Result - `tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py`: **69 passed, 2 skipped** (pre-existing, unrelated skips) - Manual end-to-end repro against `unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506` (dual-format checkpoint): dummy multimodal input generation **crashes** with the exact `ValueError: Mismatch in image token count...` shown above **before** this fix (verified via `git stash`), and **succeeds** after. - `pre-commit run` on all changed files: **clean** (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden-imports check, SPDX headers, typos, etc.)
