signal.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description When deploying DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `MooncakeStoreConnector` + MTP speculative decoding (`speculative_config.method='mtp'`), the external KV cache save path is completely broken: no `save_exists`/`save_put` operations are ever recorded, and the `External prefix cache hit rate` stays at 0.0% indefinitely. **Disabling MTP resolves the issue.** ## Environment - vLLM version: v0.23.0 - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash - Deployment: single-node, 8x H100-80G, TP=8, EP=8 - KV connector: `MooncakeStoreConnector` with `standalone-store` mode - Speculative decoding: MTP (`Eagle3`) with `num_speculative_tokens=1` Relevant config: ``` tensor_parallel_size: 8 enable_expert_parallel: True block_size: 256 enable_prefix_caching: True speculative_config: {method: mtp, num_speculative_tokens: 1} kv_transfer_config: kv_connector: MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role: kv_both ``` ## Symptoms 1. **Metrics only show `lookup_exists`**, never `save_exists` / `save_put` / `load_get`: ``` KV Transfer metrics: lookup_exists_count=5, lookup_exists_avg_ms=40.884, ... (save_exists, save_put, load_get never appear) ``` 2. **External prefix cache hit rate always 0.0%** (internal cache hits work fine): ``` Engine 000: ..., Prefix cache hit rate: 5.5%, External prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% ``` 3. **All 8 workers show `Completed send: 0` every step**: ``` (Worker_TP*_EP*) DEBUG [worker.py:1291] Completed send: 0, recv: 0, tp_rank: [0-7] ``` 4. **Zero send thread activity**: no `Storing KV cache` log, no error, no crash — the `KVCacheStoreSendingThread._handle_request()` is simply never reached. ## Root Cause Analysis The scheduler-side connector correctly builds `ReqMeta` with `can_save=True`: ``` (EngineCore) DEBUG [data.py:260] request:chatcmpl-xxx, meta save spec:True, meta load spec:None ``` However, the worker-side `worker.get_finished()` receives `meta.requests` as either empty or with all `can_save` fields lost, so the save loop at never adds any requests to the send queue. The likely cause is a **serialization incompatibility** in `ReqMeta` (defined in `data.py`). When MTP Eagle3 is active, the model has 5 KV cache groups with mixed `block_size` values (256 for MLA groups, 64 for drafting layers). This produces `ReqMeta` objects with: - `block_ids: tuple[list[int], ...]` — per-group block id lists (5 groups) - `block_hashes: list[BlockHash]` — `BlockHash = NewType("BlockHash", bytes)`, finer granularity due to `hash_block_size=64` - `can_save: bool` These nested typed structures appear to not survive the pickle-based shared memory broadcast (`shm_broadcast.py`) from EngineCore to workers in this specific multi-group + MTP configuration. ## Workaround Disable MTP speculative decoding when using `MooncakeStoreConnector`: ```bash # Remove --speculative-config entirely ``` ## Expected Behavior `MooncakeStoreConnector` should correctly save KV cache blocks to the external Mooncake store even when MTP speculative decoding is enabled, so that subsequent requests can benefit from external prefix cache hits. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Mamba] Add FlashInfer ReplaySSM backend
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds FlashInfer as an optional ReplaySSM backend for Mamba2. It calls FlashInfer's native `checkpointing_ssu` API, shares replay trackers per KV-cache group, and autotunes a maximum-batch decode through the existing FlashInfer warmup flow before CUDA-graph capture. FlashInfer ReplaySSM supports Model Runner V1 and V2; Triton ReplaySSM remains V1-only. ## Blocked on FlashInfer > [!IMPORTANT] > This PR is blocked by [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4545](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4545), which adds native ReplaySSM autotuning. Do not merge this PR until #4545 is available in a compatible FlashInfer release and vLLM's package and Docker pins are updated together. Older FlashInfer versions fail capability validation rather than silently using a non-native tuning path. ## Validation Validation used `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4` on H100 GPUs with MTP disabled. ### GSM8K Matched 5-shot GSM8K over all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, and `max_num_seqs=64`: | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | FlashInfer ReplaySSM | 1117/1319 | 84.685% | 0 | | Triton ReplaySSM | 1119/1319 | 84.837% | 0 | The paired exact test gives `p=0.913`, so the observed accuracy difference is not statistically significant. ### Throughput Matched TP=1 fixed-length decode benchmark: 512 decode steps, 128 warmup steps, five measured repeats, and ReplaySSM buffer length 16. | Batch | FlashInfer TPS | Triton TPS | FlashInfer delta | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 366.22 | 360.17 | +1.68% | | 16 | 2774.93 | 2901.00 | -4.35% | | 64 | 6630.05 | 6725.68 | -1.42% | | 128 | 9368.32 | 9452.60 | -0.89% | FlashInfer is faster at batch size 1; Triton remains faster at the larger tested batch sizes. Additional coverage: V1 and V2 smokes, two-node TP=2 and PP=2 smokes, focused H100 unit/integration tests

signal.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fail closed on HMA receive errors
signal.text: ## Summary NIXL receive failures are currently propagated through flat block IDs. That works for uniform KV caches, but HMA block IDs are scoped to independent pools, so the worker intentionally omits them. The failed request is then reported as finished receiving without any failure signal, allowing decode to continue with invalid KV. This change: - propagates unrecoverable HMA receive failures by request ID; - aggregates that signal across workers until the receive is complete; - applies the same aggregation to uniprocess execution so failure and completion notifications cannot be split across scheduler steps; and - fails the request before consuming any sampled tokens, regardless of the block-recovery policy. Uniform-cache failures keep the existing block-level fail/recompute behavior. ## Duplicate-work check This is not duplicated by an open PR: - #40364 fixed handshake-failure recovery through `invalid_block_ids`, but explicitly left HMA failure handling as a TODO because its block IDs are not group-qualified. - #50754 reports push-side write-posting failures to the decode worker; it still relies on the downstream receive-failure path fixed here. - #50494 and #48263 extend supported HMA layouts rather than propagating failed receives to the scheduler. ## Tests ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_error_propagation.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py -q # 8 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_handshake_failure_returns_finished -q # 2 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_hma_failed_transfer_reports_request_error -q # 1 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py \ -k uniproc_executor_pairs_receive_failure_with_completion -v # 2 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py -v # 3 passed pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py \ tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py # all file-scoped hooks passed ``` Linux validation used a vllm-development-platform environment on the `vllm-envs` PVC and Kueue-managed Jobs: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_error_propagation.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_hma_failed_transfer_reports_request_error -q # 9 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_handshake_failure_returns_finished -q # 2 passed (B200) ``` The serving regression was reproduced with Gemma-4-26B FP8, NIXL HMA, prefill block size 128, and decode block size 64. Both runs used the same Manifesto-rendered PD topology and EPP always-disaggregated routing: - current main `71b0da7c4e`: the compatibility hash passed, the NIXL handshake then raised the heterogeneous-block-size assertion, and the API returned HTTP 200 with 64 tokens of gibberish despite zero successful KV transfers; - this change `9e80dac9eb`: the identical handshake failure logged `Failing 1 request(s) due to unrecoverable KV receive failure` and the API returned HTTP 500 with only an error object—no choices, content, usage, or generated tokens. No model-quality evaluation is applicable: successful KV transfer and model output paths are unchanged. The serving validation targets the changed failure path and asserts that no generated tokens escape. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines before marking the PR ready.

### 🐛 Describe the bug PR [#36787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36787) moved Gemma's `sqrt(hidden_size)` normalization from `forward()` into text-only `embed_input_ids()`, but PaliGemma retained the inverse scale that previously compensated for the old common forward multiplication. Current vLLM consequently feeds projected image features into Gemma at `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of their intended magnitude. Before #36787, the operations were balanced: ```text text: embed_tokens ------------------------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) image: projector / sqrt(H) -> merge --------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) ``` After #36787, current vLLM scales only text: ```text text: embed_tokens * sqrt(H) -> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged image: projector / sqrt(H) ----> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged ``` Current `main` scales text in [`gemma.py:284-308`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma.py#L284-L308), but still inverse-scales images in [`paligemma.py:376-383`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/paligemma.py#L376-L383). Multimodal merge only replaces placeholder rows, and `GemmaModel.forward(inputs_embeds=...)` applies no compensating scale. Transformers changed both halves atomically in [`0e7cb4e3`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/0e7cb4e3ea3daaeef626148522f80b751e9559bd): Gemma text lookup gained `sqrt(H)` scaling and PaliGemma stopped dividing projected image features. Transformers 5.14.1 directly inserts raw projected image features into the already-scaled text embeddings. For ColPali's `hidden_size=2048`, the contract reduction is: ```python import math hidden_size = 2048 raw_projected_image = 1.0 print( "before #36787:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5 * math.sqrt(hidden_size), ) print("current vLLM:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5) print("expected:", raw_projected_image) ``` ```text before #36787: 1.0 current vLLM: 0.022097086912079608 expected: 1.0 ``` The stale factor is therefore about `0.0221`: projected image features enter Gemma at about 2.21% of their intended magnitude. Controlled one-variable A/B against the pinned Transformers reference: | Variant | Text cosine mean | Image cosine mean | Image p01 | Image minimum | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Current stale inverse scale | 0.999797 | 0.903149 | 0.430221 | 0.225688 | | Inverse scale removed only | 0.999797 | 0.987502 | 0.726556 | 0.436249 | The request, preprocessing, checkpoint, plugin SHA, and reference were held constant; only `vision_embeddings *= hidden_size**-0.5` was removed. The remaining image mismatch is a separately measured Neuron eager-vision drift, so this one-line change should not be represented as fixing all ColPali parity issues. Full ColPali command used for validation: ```bash vllm serve vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --revision 7d3c8ab1c1908b32d701308fb1dfb2968d150c67 \ --served-model-name vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --trust-remote-code \ --runner pooling \ --convert none \ --pooler-config.task token_embed \ --port 20000 ``` Expected behavior: PaliGemma should return raw projected image features from `embed_multimodal()`, matching Transformers' scaled-text/raw-image contract. Suggested fix: ```diff def embed_multimodal(self, **kwargs: object) -> MultiModalEmbeddings: image_input = self._parse_and_validate_image_input(**kwargs) if image_input is None: return [] vision_embeddings = self._process_image_input(image_input) - vision_embeddings = vision_embeddings * (self.config.hidden_size**-0.5) return vision_embeddings ``` Suggested tests: pass known projected `image_embeds` to PaliGemma and assert they are returned unchanged; add one fixed-image Transformers parity test that compares first-step logits or top-k probabilities. Current ColPali tests verify shape, L2 normalization, and weak relevance ordering, which cannot detect this pre-language-model scaling error. The final downstream ColPali branch passes with pristine vLLM only because its host-vision path supplies raw projected features and bypasses `PaliGemma.embed_multimodal()`. The one-line patch is not part of that final plugin apply set, and the pristine pass does not validate the stale upstream method. This regression was introduced by #36787 (`65986db6ba71abf4cf0639c5fd1477b0d8df8f5e`). Searches for PaliGemma image scaling, inverse scaling, `sqrt(hidden_size)`, `hidden_size**-0.5`, and #36787 found no matching issue or follow-up fix. Severity: major silent correctness regression. The source contract is confirmed; broad current-main CUDA generation impact has not yet been quantified. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0 PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug vLLM applies Dynamic NTK context-extension scaling even when a Nomic model is served below its trained context length. `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` is validly served here with `--max-model-len 512`, while its `max_trained_positions` is 2048. Current vLLM computes a negative scaling term, creates a complex RoPE cache with values near `1.86e38`, casts that cache to a real dtype, and ultimately returns NaN embeddings. Current `main` passes the served maximum and trained maximum separately in [`config.py:717-732`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/config.py#L717-L732), then applies this formula unconditionally in [`dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py:53-66`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py#L53-L66): ```text inner = factor * served_max / trained_max - (factor - 1) = 2 * 512 / 2048 - 1 = -0.5 base = 1000 * (-0.5) ** (64 / 62) = approximately (-486.44 - 49.47j) ``` Minimal CPU reproduction: ```python import torch from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding.dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope import ( DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding, ) served, trained, factor, base, dim = 512, 2048, 2.0, 1000.0, 64 inner = factor * served / trained - (factor - 1) effective_base = base * inner ** (dim / (dim - 2)) rope = DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding( head_size=64, rotary_dim=64, max_position_embeddings=served, max_trained_positions=trained, base=base, is_neox_style=True, scaling_factor=factor, dtype=torch.float32, ) precast = rope._compute_cos_sin_cache() print("inner_factor:", inner) print("effective_base:", effective_base) print("precast:", precast.dtype, precast.is_complex()) print("precast_abs_max:", precast.abs().max().item()) print("registered_abs_max:", rope.cos_sin_cache.abs().max().item()) ``` Observed: ```text inner_factor: -0.5 effective_base: (-486.4356532483613-49.46567115590085j) precast: torch.complex64 True precast_abs_max: 1.859551754043404e+38 registered_abs_max: approximately 1.859551754043404e+38 UserWarning: Casting complex values to real discards the imaginary part ``` Full serving reproduction: ```bash vllm serve nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1 \ --revision 3ac47f125a41961d13b397d0332866be2f9152e1 \ --served-model-name nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-model-len 512 \ --trust-remote-code \ --runner pooling \ --convert embed \ --port 20000 ``` On the measured float32 path, inputs of 35 tokens and longer return HTTP 400 because the embedding contains NaNs: ```text ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan ``` This is not an invalid serving configuration. Reducing the served maximum below the checkpoint's trained maximum is ordinary truncation, and the pinned Nomic reference implementation keeps the original RoPE base until the sequence length exceeds 2048. The verified fix is to skip Dynamic NTK scaling at or below the trained maximum: ```diff def _compute_cos_sin_cache(self) -> torch.Tensor: - base = self.base * ( - ( - self.scaling_factor - * self.max_position_embeddings - / self.max_trained_positions - ) - - (self.scaling_factor - 1) - ) ** (self.rotary_dim / (self.rotary_dim - 2)) + if self.max_position_embeddings <= self.max_trained_positions: + base = self.base + else: + base = self.base * ( + ( + self.scaling_factor + * self.max_position_embeddings + / self.max_trained_positions + ) + - (self.scaling_factor - 1) + ) ** (self.rotary_dim / (self.rotary_dim - 2)) ``` With only this guard changed, the cache is real float32, finite, and bounded by `[-1, 1]`. The original model configuration then passed 100/100 requests at batch 1 and batch 4, and float32 CPU/accelerator embedding cosine returned to approximately 1.0. Expected behavior: when `max_position_embeddings <= max_trained_positions`, Dynamic NTK should use the original RoPE base. At equality the existing formula already evaluates to the original base, and above the trained maximum the existing context-extension behavior should remain unchanged. Suggested regression tests: compare Dynamic NTK caches at served maxima 512 and 2048 against ordinary RoPE, asserting real and finite values bounded by one; add a 4096 case proving extension behavior is unchanged. This is not a duplicate of [#41236](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41236). That issue reported the previous constant-scaling formula and was closed by [#41277](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41277), which introduced the current below-training-length regression. Open PR [#41301](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41301) predates #41277 and its current head only changes indentation, so it does not add this guard. Searches for `max_trained_positions`, `below training length`, `negative base`, and Dynamic NTK NaNs found no matching report. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bug]: FP8 on RDNA3/gfx1100 exceeds the 600 s engine-ready timeout on first start — no AMD_Radeon_Graphics tuned configs shipped
signal.text:
### TL;DR - The official FP8 checkpoint (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) **loads and serves fine on a consumer RDNA3 card** (gfx1100, Radeon W7900 48 GB, `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723` on ROCm). There is no architecture refusal — community trackers currently report FP8 as "does not run on RDNA3", but it does. - The out-of-the-box failure is a **startup timeout**: for `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` the wheel ships **zero** tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs (of 218 device-keyed configs it ships 76 for AMD Instinct and 142 for NVIDIA devices), so the default config is used and warmup **JIT-compiles the Triton GEMM kernels shape by shape**. First engine init measured **1474.26 s** — 2.5x the 600 s default of `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` — and the APIServer aborts. - The abort message says the timeout is "**often caused by slow weight loading**". Our weights loaded in **16.33 s**; the 23+ minutes between kernel warnings were CPU-side Triton compilation with the GPU idle. - `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800` makes it start. Once the on-disk Triton cache is warm, engine init is **49 s** and every later start is ~2 min — the cost is one-time per host (until `~/.triton/cache` is cleared). - **Asks:** (1) ship tuned W8A8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` (mirroring the MI300X/MI325 sets); (2) cheap: mention cold-start JIT/config warmup as a cause in the engine-ready timeout error or the env-var docs; (3) secondary observation: the **first inference** triggers a further ~43 min of JIT staging that `/health` does not reflect. - **I have the hardware** and am happy to run whatever tuning/profiling procedure you point at and PR the resulting `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` JSONs, and to test any RC on gfx1100. ### Your current environment
Output of python -m vllm.collect_env (venv used for all runs below) ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : N/A ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.2.53211 XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Mar 3 2026, 12:15:18) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-79-generic-x86_64-with-glibc-2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : Could not collect CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU models and configuration : AMD Radeon Graphics (gfx1100) Nvidia driver version : Could not collect cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : 7.2.53211 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.1 Is XNNPACK available : True ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : 7.2.53211-e1a6bc5663 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: single GPU, NUMA node 0 ============================== Environment Variables ============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root ``` Install (per the ROCm install docs): `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` → `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723`; `transformers==5.15.0`; host ROCm userspace 7.2.1. CPU: 2x AMD EPYC 9334 (full `lscpu` flags and the rocm-smi topology table omitted for brevity; available on request).
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Expected:** `vllm serve` (or `api_server`) with an official FP8 checkpoint on gfx1100 either starts within the default engine-ready budget, or fails with a message pointing at the real cost. **Actual (measured on Radeon W7900D, gfx1100, 48 GB):** | Run | `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` | Triton cache | Result | |---|---|---|---| | cold serve | 600 (default) | cold | `TimeoutError` at 600 s mid-warmup; weights had loaded in 16.33 s | | cold serve | 1800 | cold | engine init **1474.26 s**, then `/health` 200, serving OK | | warm re-run | 1800 | warm | engine init **49.01 s** | | later starts (x3) | 1800 | warm | 49.10 / 49.11 / 49.19 s, server up in ~2 min | After unlock, serving works end-to-end (105/105 benchmark requests OK) — at untuned-config performance; see measured results below. #### Reproduce without hardware (2 minutes) Anyone with the wheel installed can verify the config gap that drives the cold-start cost: ```bash CFG=$(python -c "import vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils as m, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(m.__file__),'configs'))") ls "$CFG" | wc -l # 219 (218 device-keyed JSONs + README.md) ls "$CFG" | grep -c MI300X # 28 (+ 24 MI325X + 24 MI325_OAM = 76 Instinct) ls "$CFG" | grep -ci radeon # 0 ls "$CFG" | grep -c 'N=16384,K=5120' # 0 — not shipped for ANY device ``` The engine-side lookup is a plain file-exists check in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` (0.27.1, ~line 830): the filename is built from `get_device_name_as_file_name()` — which on RDNA3 consumer cards is literally the torch device name `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and when the JSON is missing the code logs the warning below and **returns `None` (default config)**. Nothing is ever written back to that directory, so the cost recurs for every fresh host/venv. #### Reproduce on gfx1100 (~35 min, needs a 24 GB+ RDNA3 card) ```bash # fresh venv — a warm ~/.triton/cache hides the bug (init drops to ~49 s) uv venv /root/venv-fp8 && VIRTUAL_ENV=/root/venv-fp8 uv pip install vllm \ --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/ # 0.27.1+rocm723 # model: official FP8 checkpoint, ~28.7 GiB # HF: huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # (we used ModelScope: modelscope download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) SNAP=/path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # 1) default timeout → aborts at 600 s: /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 # 2) unlocked: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 ``` (All measurements above were taken with `--enforce-eager` added to skip torch.compile/CUDA-graph capture; the cold abort also reproduces without it, with `torch.compile took 67.53 s` interleaved.) #### Verbatim evidence
1) Cold run, default timeout — aborts while weights were long done ```text (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 16.33 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [gpu_model_runner.py:5405] Model loading took 29.38 GiB memory and 17.353099 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:44:23 [monitor.py:53] torch.compile took 67.53 s in total (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 01:44:23 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 02:07:49 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=5120,K=6144,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (APIServer pid=279547) TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. This is often caused by slow weight loading for large models. Waited 600s (configured by VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S). To increase the timeout, set the environment variable: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S= ``` Note the **23 m 26 s gap between the two fp8_utils warnings** — that is one Triton GEMM kernel compiling (single CPU core pinned, GPU idle), not weight loading.
2) Same wheel, timeout raised — starts, and the cost is visible ```text (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:07:37 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:31:17 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=34816,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) INFO 08-17 08:31:42 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 1474.26 s (APIServer pid=371094) INFO: 127.0.0.1:33878 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The warmup pass walks five GEMM shapes for this model (N=16384/K=5120, N=5120/K=6144, N=34816/K=5120, N=5120/K=17408, N=14336/K=5120); none has a shipped config.
3) Warm Triton cache — the whole cliff disappears ```text (EngineCore pid=378832) INFO 08-17 08:38:28 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 49.01 s (APIServer pid=378511) INFO 08-17 08:38:45 [api_server.py:682] Starting vLLM server on http://0.0.0.0:8199 (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: Application startup complete. (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: 127.0.0.1:46230 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ```
4) Secondary: first-INFERENCE JIT staging (~43 min), invisible to /health Even after a healthy start, the first completion request triggers more JIT compiles; the server answers `/health` 200 the whole time and a default-timeout client (ours: 300 s) just times out. Verbatim from the first served request on a cache-warm-start server: ```text (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:34:18 [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _causal_conv1d_update_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel. ... (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: layer_norm_fwd_kernel. ... ``` The very first request (13:34:18) outlived the client's 300 s ceiling; the first fully-served response landed at ~14:17:41 — **43 min after the first request was sent** (the request that completed was issued 14:07:52 and took `total_s=608.536757`). Subsequent traffic is normal: a 16-request warmup burst after this returned all 200 in ~26–28 s.
### Root cause (as far as the code shows) 1. `fp8_utils.py` builds the tuned-config filename from the torch device name — on RDNA3 consumer cards that is `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and the wheel ships **no** JSONs for that name (the entire AMD set is Instinct-only). Missing file → warning → `return None` → default W8A8 config. 2. With the default config, `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` JIT-compiles its Triton kernel for each distinct (N, K) shape during engine warmup. On this host each big compile takes ~20+ min of single-threaded CPU (GPU idle); the shape-by-shape walk (first warning 08:07:37 → init done 08:31:42) accounts for essentially all of the 1474.26 s engine init. 3. The APIServer's engine-ready deadline (default 600 s, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, consumed in the v1 engine core client) expires mid-warmup, and the error names "slow weight loading" as the likely cause. 4. The Triton disk cache (`~/.triton/cache`) makes every subsequent start fast, and nothing writes tuned JSONs back — so the cliff is a **per-host one-time cost that looks like a hard failure** the first time. ### Proposed fixes (ranked) 1. **Ship tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics`** (gfx1100 at minimum), mirroring the shipped MI300X/MI325 sets. This is what the runtime warning already asks for, it removes the "sub-optimal default" path entirely, and it is the lever for the performance gap below. I have a W7900 and am glad to run the config-generation/benchmark procedure on it and open a PR with the resulting JSONs if you can point me at the tooling. 2. **Cheap message/docs improvement:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` is documented, but the timeout error's cause list ("often caused by slow weight loading") sends users down the wrong path when the real cost is JIT/config warmup on an untuned device (weights: 16.33 s here). One extra sentence in the error string or in the env-var docs — "first-start JIT compilation of untuned kernels can take tens of minutes on newly-supported platforms; raise the timeout or pre-warm" — would have saved us hours. 3. **Secondary observation** (same platform gap, different surface): the first inference after a cold start triggers ~43 min more of Triton JIT that `/health` does not reflect (details block 4). If preferred I'll split this into its own issue — keeping it here because it shares the root cause (no RDNA3 tuning artifacts shipped). ### Measured results after unlock (context for prioritization, not a complaint) `--enforce-eager`, temp 0, fixed 100-token prompt, 128-token generations, 5 reps per cell, non-streaming: | concurrency | aggregate decode tok/s | requests OK | p50 request wall | |---|---:|---|---:| | 1 | 0.612 | 5/5 | 209.2 s | | 4 | 2.301 | 20/20 | 222.4 s | | 16 | 8.730 | 80/80 | 234.5 s | For scale on the same GPU, llama.cpp with a Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model does 28.6 tok/s single-stream and 164.4 tok/s aggregate at c=32 — so FP8-on-RDNA3 today is ~47x slower per stream, which the tuned-config gap plausibly explains a large part of. Capacity is not the issue: 29.38 GiB of FP8 weights on the 48 GB card with ~19 GiB headroom. ### Related issues (searched; not duplicates) - #51136 — AITER not enabled on RDNA3 (gfx1100): same GPU class, different mechanism (INT8/Quark + AITER gating vs FP8 W8A8 Triton path here); complementary data point. - #35547, #32116 — same engine-ready timeout symptom class on NVIDIA (slow weight loading / DeepGEMM warmup). This issue adds the RDNA3/FP8 instance where the dominant cost is per-shape Triton JIT under a missing tuned config, plus the configs gap itself. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues (linked above) and found no report of FP8-on-RDNA3 failing startup via untuned-config JIT with this mechanism. - [x] `collect_env` output attached. - [x] Repro is self-contained; the configs-gap part needs no hardware. Happy to contribute: tuning runs on gfx1100 → `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` config PR, and RC testing on this card.

signal.title: [Feature]: Add torch.compile support for SiglipEmbeddingModel
signal.text: ## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Please add vLLM `torch.compile` support for the standalone `SiglipEmbeddingModel`. As of main commit [`8878ebd8`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd) [Aug 17th], the class has no `@support_torch_compile` decorator. vLLM 0.24.0 consequently emitted its explicit "`torch.compile` is turned on, but the model ... does not support it" warning. This is a compile-support request, not a regression in supported eager serving. The main compile blocker we found is [`_flip_sequences_by_position_ids()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd/vllm/model_executor/models/siglip.py#L985-L1028). The released implementation introduced by [#28365](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28365) creates a compact boundary tensor with one-argument `torch.where`, then uses its value-dependent length in `repeat_interleave`. On a backend requiring static fullgraph compilation, vLLM 0.24.0 produced an unbacked `sym_sum` (`u0 + 1`) and failed during startup: ```text torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='neuron' raised: RuntimeError: Unimplemented call_function: target=<function sym_sum ...> File "vllm/model_executor/models/siglip.py", line 1108 len(lengths), device=features.device from_node: sym_sum val: u0 + 1 ``` We validated a fixed-shape replacement that avoids compact tensors and keeps every intermediate dimension tied to the input token count: ```python def _flip_sequences_by_position_ids( self, features: torch.Tensor, position_ids: torch.Tensor, ) -> torch.Tensor: if len(features) == 1: return features num_tokens = features.shape[0] token_indices = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=features.device) boundary_mask = position_ids[1:] <= position_ids[:-1] segment_starts = torch.cat( ( torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=features.device), boundary_mask, ) ) segment_ends = torch.cat( ( boundary_mask, torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=features.device), ) ) rows = token_indices[:, None] columns = token_indices[None, :] starts = torch.where( segment_starts[None, :] & (columns <= rows), columns, 0 ).amax(dim=1) ends = torch.where( segment_ends[None, :] & (columns >= rows), columns, token_indices[-1], ).amin(dim=1) flip_indices = starts + ends - token_indices return features[flip_indices] ``` This implementation matched the existing eager behavior exactly for 6,400 generated packed and padded cases covering token lengths 1 through 64. With the other required Neuron/plugin fixes held constant, replacing this helper allowed fullgraph warmup to pass at batch 1 and batch 4 on AWS Trainium2; text serving completed 100/100 requests at both batch sizes, and the complete text/image test reported `2 passed`. The temporary is `O(T^2)`, but the tested SigLIP text length is 64; a more efficient fixed-shape implementation would also satisfy the request. Suggested acceptance criteria: - Replace the value-dependent reversal with a compile-safe implementation that preserves packed and padded sequence semantics. - Add exhaustive small-boundary and randomized length-64 equivalence tests. - Add a test that exercises SigLIP text embeddings without `--enforce-eager`. - Add `@support_torch_compile` once the complete model path passes vLLM's compile tests. Current main changed the helper in [#43107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43107) to perform the dynamic boundary calculation on CPU. It still has value-dependent boundary cardinality and the model still lacks `@support_torch_compile`. We have not run current main on Neuron and are not claiming that current main fails; the hardware validation above is against vLLM 0.24.0, so the proposed implementation must be adapted and tested against current main. ### Alternatives - Continue serving SigLIP with `--enforce-eager`. This is the upstream-tested path from #28365, but it does not serve backends that require static fullgraph compilation. - Carry the validated replacement as a downstream compatibility patch. This works, but duplicates model logic downstream and must be version-guarded. - Insert a graph break around the dynamic reversal. This may help partial-compilation backends but does not provide fullgraph support and is unsuitable for static ahead-of-time backends. ### Additional context - Latest release checked: v0.27.1. - Current main inspected: `8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd`, 2026-08-17. - Hardware validation: `trn2.48xlarge`, vLLM 0.24.0, torch 2.11.0, torch-neuronx `2.12.3.0.26429+3f245a2.dev`, neuronx-cc `2.0.273779.0a0+c78bd1dd`, Python 3.12.11. - Model validated: `google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384` at revision `9fdffc58afc957d1a03a25b10dba0329ab15c2a3`. - Duplicate searches for `SigLIP torch.compile`, `SigLIP dynamic shape`, and `_flip_sequences_by_position_ids` found no matching issue on 2026-08-17. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Feature]: Optional content fallback policy for length-truncated reasoning responses
signal.text: #### Summary When a DeepSeek V4 generation reaches `max_tokens` before its reasoning block closes, the Chat Completions response has `finish_reason: "length"`, `message.content: null`, and non-empty `message.reasoning`. vLLM preserves the generated text, so this is not token loss. However, OpenAI-compatible clients that read only `content` present an empty assistant response. Could vLLM provide a documented, explicit opt-in policy for deployments that prefer non-empty standard content on this path? The default behavior can remain unchanged. An opt-in is important because copying incomplete reasoning into content can expose chain-of-thought text and can misrepresent an unfinished analysis as a final answer. #### Relationship to existing work - #48645 covers naturally completed replies that omit `</think>` and are misclassified as reasoning. - #50753 proposes `force_nonempty_content` for that natural-stop case and deliberately excludes streaming responses with `finish_reason: "length"`. - This request concerns whether deployments should have a separate explicit compatibility policy for the length-truncated case. #### Environment - Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` - vLLM release: `0.27.1` - vLLM nightly: `0.27.2rc1.dev122+g8efa13b70`, commit `8efa13b700f1836657699cae2503dc2feab27fa0` - Hardware: Linux arm64, 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs - Endpoint: `/v1/chat/completions` - Parser: `deepseek_v4` - Direct `vllm serve`, with no proxy or separate response assembler Material server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --max-num-seqs 36 \ --trust-remote-code ``` #### Reproduction ```bash curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Rank these by acidity and justify each comparison from first principles, considering inductive effects, resonance stabilisation, and hybridisation: phenol, ethanol, acetic acid, water, trifluoroacetic acid. Think step by step, then finish with \"the answer is (X)\"." } ], "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0, "chat_template_kwargs": { "enable_thinking": true } }' \ | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason,content:.message.content,reasoning:.message.reasoning}' ``` Observed response shape: ```json { "finish_reason": "length", "content": null, "reasoning": "<non-empty generated text>" } ``` #### Results For vLLM 0.27.1, all 48 requests capped at 256 through 2,048 tokens ended inside reasoning, returned null content, and returned non-empty reasoning. For nightly `8efa13b70`, all 60 requests capped at 256 through 4,096 tokens had the same result. At 4,096 tokens on vLLM 0.27.1, every response crossed the reasoning boundary and produced non-empty content. Ten later ended by length and two stopped normally. This shows that the condition is truncation inside reasoning, not any response with `finish_reason: "length"`. Streaming reproduced the split in both builds. At 256 tokens, 12 of 12 streams per build emitted non-empty reasoning deltas and no non-empty content delta. With thinking disabled on nightly, 12 of 12 requests at 256 tokens returned non-empty content and empty reasoning. #### Requested behavior Please consider one of these outcomes: 1. Document that length-truncated reasoning is available only in `reasoning`, and document that content-only clients must handle this response shape. 2. Add an explicit opt-in compatibility policy that copies or moves length-truncated reasoning into `content`. 3. Expose a terminal indicator that lets clients distinguish an empty answer from a response whose entire generation remains in the reasoning channel. The option must behave consistently for streaming and non-streaming responses. It must not silently expose incomplete reasoning by default. #### Duplicate check I searched the current issue tracker. #48645 and #50753 are related but focus on naturally completed replies that omit the reasoning close marker. This request is limited to an explicit compatibility policy for responses that end by length while still reasoning.

signal.title: [Documentation]: Clarify FileStore vs TCPStore security behavior by executor and version
signal.text: ### Description The current vLLM security guidance warns that PyTorch distributed TCP initialization can create a TCPStore listener on all interfaces, including in single-host deployments, and appropriately recommends firewall and network isolation: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/usage/security/#notes-on-pytorch-distributed That warning is important, but the documentation no longer makes the configuration and version boundary clear after these changes: - #50999 switched local `MultiprocExecutor` and `UniProcExecutor` rendezvous to `file://` / `torch.distributed.FileStore`, eliminating the TCP rendezvous listener for those paths. - #51635 retains TCPStore when ROCm AITER custom all-reduce is enabled because that integration currently requires it. - Multi-node and ordinary data-parallel configurations continue to use TCP rendezvous. Released versions from before #50999, including v0.27.1, still construct a `tcp://<loopback>:<port>` rendezvous URI for local executors. A loopback address in that URI should not be taken as proof that the TCPStore server is bound only to loopback; operators can still observe a wildcard listener on the selected port. Could the security and distributed-deployment documentation add a concise version/configuration matrix covering: 1. The default store for local `UniProcExecutor` and `MultiprocExecutor`. 2. The store used for multi-node and data-parallel deployments. 3. The ROCm AITER custom all-reduce exception. 4. The first vLLM release containing #50999. 5. Whether `VLLM_HOST_IP`, `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`, or `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` affect the TCPStore server's bind scope. 6. Firewall or network-namespace requirements for configurations that still use TCPStore. 7. A simple log indicator or verification command operators can use to identify the active rendezvous/store. This would help operators distinguish configurations fixed by FileStore from those that still require network containment, and avoid assuming that a loopback `tcp://` URI proves a loopback-only listener. ### Alternatives - Keep the current generic warning. This remains conservative, but it does not explain which current configurations no longer open a TCP rendezvous listener or which exceptions still do. - Document the behavior only in release notes and pull requests. Those details are difficult for operators to discover during security review. - Add a user-selectable store setting. That could be useful separately, but operators would still need documentation for defaults, compatibility, and exceptions. ### Additional context Related upstream work: - #15987 reported the wildcard TCPStore listener behavior. - #50999 implemented FileStore rendezvous for single-node executors. - #51635 documented and implemented the ROCm AITER TCPStore exception. - Current security guidance: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/usage/security/#notes-on-pytorch-distributed This is a documentation and deployment-hardening request, not a report of a new undisclosed vulnerability. ### Before submitting a new issue - [x] I searched existing and past issues for this documentation gap. - [x] I reviewed the current security documentation and the related merged pull requests.

signal.title: [Performance][ROCm] shared_expert_gate ([1, K] weight) misses every skinny-GEMM path and costs 13.7% of the decode step
signal.text: ## Summary On ROCm, `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` dispatches on `m = weight.shape[0]`. Its two skinny-GEMM branches cover `m > 8` (wvSplitK) and `m % 4 == 0` (LLMM1), so for `m <= 8` only `m ∈ {4, 8}` are covered — **`m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` falls through** to `torch.nn.functional.linear` → rocBLAS. (The `n` conditions also differ: wvSplitK takes `0 < n <= 5`, LLMM1 only `n == 1`.) `m == 1` is not a rare shape. In transformers today, `self.shared_expert_gate = torch.nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1, bias=False)` — i.e. a `[1, hidden]` weight — appears in **`qwen2_moe`, `qwen3_next`, and `qwen3_5_moe`**, invoked once per layer per token to produce the scalar that gates the shared expert's contribution. (`qwen3_moe` and `qwen3_vl_moe` have no shared expert, so they are unaffected; `glm4_moe` has a shared expert but no gate.) Because `bias=False` there, `bias is None` always holds for this call. For a `1×2048 @ 2048×1` product, rocBLAS selects `Cijk_Ailk_Bljk_BBS_BH_MT128x32x16_..._GSU1_...` — a **128×32 macro-tile with no split-K**. That is one workgroup on a 40-CU GPU serially walking `k=2048`: **~140 µs to move 4 KiB of weights**, against **~7.9 µs** for every width the skinny ladder does cover. Measured on a Qwen3.5-MoE 35B-A3B (40 layers, hidden 2048, 256 experts, 8 active), batch-1 decode, gfx1151: | | | |---|---| | cost per call | 137 µs | | calls per decode step | 40 (one per layer) | | **total** | **5.48 ms of a 40.06 ms step = 13.7%** | | decode after fixing it | 40.06 → 34.79 ms/step, **24.53 → 28.32 tok/s (+15.5%)** | ## Environment - gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo), ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 - vLLM 0.27.1 (the same dispatch conditions are present on `main` today) - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` at its default (`True`) ## Where `vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py`, in `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`: ```python if use_skinny: x_view = x.reshape(-1, x.size(-1)).contiguous() if m > 8 and 0 < n <= 5: # m == 1 fails ... elif m % 4 == 0 and n == 1 and k <= 8192 and bias is None: # 1 % 4 != 0, fails ... if rocm_aiter_ops.is_tgemm_enabled(): ... return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias) # <-- m == 1 lands here ``` Note `is_tgemm_enabled()` requires `on_gfx950()`, and `use_aiter_triton_gemm()` matches only a hardcoded shape whitelist, so on gfx11xx there is no other path to catch this. ## Reproducer Standalone, no checkpoint needed. Part A needs only torch; Part B additionally needs vLLM: https://gist.github.com/wenis/ea2a42350797771304a2d8ea8c7848f7 Output on the environment above, **stock vLLM**, `--k 2048 --iters 200`: ``` device : AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics torch : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 shape : x[1, 2048] @ w[m, 2048].T (batch-1 decode), bfloat16 === Part A: torch.nn.functional.linear (vLLM's fallback path) === m us/call GiB/s note 1 141.17 0.03 <- shared_expert_gate; 4 KiB of weights 2 37.45 0.20 3 40.33 0.28 4 37.82 0.40 8 39.65 0.77 12 38.00 1.20 16 39.09 1.56 32 40.12 3.04 64 37.81 6.46 m=1 as a reduction (x * w).sum(-1) : 5.47 us m=1 via F.linear : 141.17 us (25.8x slower) === Part B: vLLM's rocm_unquantized_gemm dispatch === m us/call expected path 1 139.93 *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback *** 2 37.16 *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback *** 3 38.82 *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback *** 4 7.90 LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1) 8 7.88 LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1) 12 7.99 wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5) 16 7.95 wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5) 32 8.01 wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5) 64 7.96 wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5) ``` Two separate things show up here, and I think only the first is vLLM's to fix: 1. **The dispatch gap.** `m = 1` costs **139.93 µs** against **~7.9 µs** for every covered width — **17.7x** — while moving *less* data than any of them. 2. **rocBLAS is additionally pathological at `m == 1` specifically.** In Part A, which never touches vLLM's ladder, `m = 1` costs **141 µs** while `m ∈ {2, 3, 4, 8, ..., 64}` all sit at **37–40 µs**. So `m = 2` and `m = 3` miss the skinny ladder too, but cost ~3.7x less than `m = 1` does. The degenerate single-row output is its own kernel-selection problem, independent of vLLM. ## Attribution The 137 µs in the table above was measured on the full model and then traced, not inferred from reading the guard: 1. vLLM's own torch profiler (`--profiler-config.profiler=torch`), 51 decode steps under representative serving flags with CUDA graphs **on**. Kernel `Cijk_..._MT128x32x16_..._GSU1` appeared at **137.5 µs × 39.2 calls/step**. An `--enforce-eager` run agreed at 137.06 µs × 40 calls, so it is not a graph-capture artifact. 2. Call-chain attribution on the eager trace resolved it to `aten::mm < aten::matmul < aten::linear < vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm < vllm::moe_forward_shared`. 3. Dispatch counts for the step were exactly **271 = 231 `wvSplitK` + 40 fallback**, with `LLMM1` never taken — i.e. exactly one linear per layer misses the ladder. 4. `shared_expert_gate.weight [1, 2048]` is the **only** 2-D weight in the model with `shape[0] == 1`, so the 40 fallbacks are fully accounted for. ## Proposed fix A `[1, K]` weight is a dot product. Adding it as a third branch in the existing ladder: ```python elif m == 1: out = (x_view * weight.reshape(-1)).sum(-1, keepdim=True) if bias is not None: out = out + bias return out.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0]) ``` With that mounted over the container's copy, Part B's `m = 1` row goes **139.93 µs → 6.82 µs (20.5x)**, and every other row is unchanged within noise (7.88–8.08 µs). End-to-end on the model above: **+15.5% decode**, with the `Cijk` kernel gone from the profile entirely and `wvSplitK` untouched (17.58 vs 17.54 ms/step), i.e. nothing else moved. The `bias is not None` arm is defensive only — transformers builds this layer with `bias=False`. Relaxing the `LLMM1` branch to accept `m < 4` looks unattractive: it passes a hardcoded split factor of 4, and the `m % 4 == 0` guard appears to be a vectorization requirement. The patch deliberately fixes only `m == 1`; `m ∈ {2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` remain uncovered, and I have no model that exercises them, so I would rather not widen it speculatively. Happy to restructure however maintainers prefer. ## Numerics — please read before taking the patch as-is **The output is not bitwise identical to `F.linear`, and the difference is not only summation order.** `x_view * weight.reshape(-1)` is a bf16 × bf16 product, so **each of the K element products is rounded to bf16 before it is summed**. `F.linear` accumulates the products in fp32 without rounding the intermediates. `torch.sum` then accumulates those bf16 values in fp32, so the reduction step itself is fine — it is the elementwise product that loses precision the GEMM keeps. Measured on random bf16 vectors at K=2048, max absolute difference was **3.1e-02 to 2.5e-01** across runs, on dot products of order ~45 — a small number of bf16 ulps, but a real and systematic difference rather than pure reordering. If that matters, the safer formulation is to widen before multiplying: ```python out = (x_view.float() * weight.reshape(-1).float()).sum(-1, keepdim=True).to(x.dtype) ``` which should keep the fp32 intermediates the GEMM has. **I have not benchmarked that variant** — it adds two small casts to a 4 KiB operand, so I would expect it to stay far ahead of 140 µs, but I would not want that assumption in the patch without a maintainer confirming which trade-off is wanted. Padding `m` to 16 and slicing the result is a third option that would stay exact and keep it a GEMM. For what it is worth on end-to-end behaviour with the bf16-product version applied: greedy decode matched the unpatched baseline for 794 of 1028 characters (~200 identical tokens) before diverging at a near-tie between two equally plausible continuations, and across 400 tool-calling benchmark problems there were **zero malformed tool calls**. That is evidence the patched model is healthy in absolute terms; it is **not** a controlled A/B, since I do not have an unpatched run of the same benchmark. A maintainer wanting a strict before/after should ask for one. vLLM already selects different kernels by shape, so bitwise stability across shapes does not appear to be a property it currently guarantees — flagging it explicitly in case that changes which fix is preferred. ## Relationship to existing work on this call site **#43187** proposes a Triton fusion for the *same* call site — collapsing the gate's skinny GEMM, sigmoid and broadcast-multiply into a single kernel, measured on MI355x. I believe the two are complementary rather than competing, because they attack different layers: - #43187 removes **kernel-launch count and intermediate tensors** in `models/qwen2_moe.py`. - This issue is that `layers/utils.py`'s dispatch ladder **never offers that GEMM a skinny path at all**, so it lands on a rocBLAS kernel measured at 17.7× the cost of the ones the ladder does select for neighbouring widths. If #43187 lands, its fused kernel replaces this call site for the models it covers, and this fix still applies to every *other* `m == 1` linear reaching `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`. If it doesn't, this fix helps the call site on its own. Fixing the dispatch also makes the un-fused path a fairer baseline to measure a fusion against. **#39280** (merged) added AITER Fused Shared Experts, which bypasses the call site at MoE-block level — but it is opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`, default `False`) and requires AITER. **#37800**, which would have enabled it by default on ROCm, was closed. So on a default ROCm configuration, and on any configuration running with AITER off (as gfx1151 is here), the unfused path is what executes. ## Related - #15830 introduced this dispatch (and, per its history, the `n <= 5` bound for spec decode). - Point 2 under the reproducer may deserve a separate rocBLAS/hipBLASLt report: selecting a 128×32 tile with `GSU1` for a degenerate 1-row output is a poor heuristic regardless of what vLLM hands it.

signal.title: [Performance]: ~18% pooling throughput regression starting with torch 2.11 (vLLM v0.20.0+)
signal.text: ## Your current environment ``` GPU: 1× NVIDIA H100 PCIe 80GB (no tensor parallelism, no data parallelism) Driver: 595.71.05, CUDA 13.2 Host: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic, 64 cores, 2 TB RAM Runtime: Docker, images vllm/vllm-openai at tags v0.14.1, v0.17.1, v0.19.0, v0.21.0, v0.26.0, v0.27.1 (torch versions bundled: 2.9.1, 2.10.0, 2.10.0, 2.11.0, 2.11.0, 2.13.0) Note: the GPU is shared with unrelated services occupying ~28 GB; all runs below were made sequentially on the same card with the same neighbours, so the comparison between versions is apples-to-apples. ``` ## Describe the bug Embedding throughput of pooling models drops by ~18% (encoder model) and ~13% (decoder model) starting with the vLLM releases that bundle **torch 2.11** — that is v0.20.0 and later. Releases on torch 2.9 and torch 2.10 are consistently fast. The regression is reproducible across four later releases and is **independent** of the API-server frontend bottleneck described at the end. Retrieval quality is unaffected — only throughput. NDCG@10 on the same dataset is 0.7426 on v0.27.1 and 0.7436 on SGLang v0.5.17, i.e. within noise, so this is purely a performance issue. ## Models used | Model | Type | Pooling | Flags | |---|---|---|---| | [`BAAI/bge-m3`](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3) | encoder (XLM-RoBERTa, 568M) | CLS | `--runner pooling` | | [`Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B) | decoder-only (4B) | last token | `--runner pooling --max-model-len 8192 --quantization fp8` | `bge-m3` is the primary reproducer: it is small enough that the model itself is not the bottleneck, so engine-side overhead is clearly visible. `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` is included to show the regression is not encoder-specific. ## Benchmark methodology Dataset: **RuBQ 2.0 retrieval corpus** (as packaged in [`mteb/RuBQRetrieval`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mteb/RuBQRetrieval)) — Russian Wikipedia paragraphs, 56 826 documents total. Each run embeds the **first 4096 documents**, average length 493 characters (~120 tokens), which keeps a single run at a few seconds and avoids drift from GPU thermals. Client: a small asyncio script issuing `POST /v1/embeddings` with 32 documents per request, sweeping client concurrency over 16 / 32 / 64. One warmup pass (4 batches) precedes every measurement so that compilation and CUDA-graph capture never land inside the timed window — this is the artifact that made [#42520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42520) a false positive, and we deliberately avoided it. Reported number is the best (plateau) throughput across the concurrency sweep; the median of per-request latencies is recorded too. Server command (bge-m3, only the version tag changes between runs): ```bash docker run -d --network host --gpus '"device=7"' \ -v /data/models:/data/models:ro \ vllm/vllm-openai:<TAG> /data/models/bge-m3 \ --served-model-name bge --runner pooling --port 8043 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.10 --api-server-count 8 --api-key "$KEY" ``` Each version got a fresh container; compile caches were not shared between versions. ## Results ### BAAI/bge-m3, `--api-server-count 8` | vLLM | torch | plateau, texts/s | at concurrency | |---|---|---|---| | v0.14.1 | 2.9.1 | 3079 | 32 | | **v0.19.0** | **2.10.0** | **3092** | 32 | | v0.21.0 | 2.11.0 | 2537 (−18%) | 32 | | v0.27.1 | 2.13.0 | 2458 (−20%) | 32 | ### BAAI/bge-m3, default `--api-server-count 1` Included because it was our starting point and shows the same shape: | vLLM | torch | plateau, texts/s | at concurrency | |---|---|---|---| | v0.14.1 | 2.9.1 | 1582 | 16 | | v0.17.1 | 2.10.0 | 1592 | 32 | | v0.21.0 | 2.11.0 | 1115 | 32 | | v0.26.0 | 2.11.0 | 1095 | 32 | | v0.27.1 | 2.13.0 | 1169 | 8 | ### Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B, `--quantization fp8` | vLLM | torch | plateau, texts/s | |---|---|---| | v0.14.1 | 2.9.1 | 391 | | v0.19.0 | 2.10.0 | 382 | | v0.27.1 | 2.13.0 | 341 (−13%) | So the regression is milder on a compute-bound model, as one would expect, but present. ## What we ruled out - **Async scheduling.** [#39592](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39592) disables it by default for pooling models from v0.20.0 on, which correlates with the regression window. But forcing `--async-scheduling` on v0.27.1 yields **1101** texts/s — worse than the 1169 default, consistent with that PR's own rationale. Not the cause. - **`assume_32_bit_indexing`.** Its default flipped True→False in [#33113](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33113). However v0.17.1 already has `False` and is fast; and forcing `--compilation-config '{"dynamic_shapes_config":{"assume_32_bit_indexing":true}}'` on v0.27.1 yields **1050** — also worse. Not the cause. - **Client batch size.** 64 documents per request instead of 32 gives 1077 vs 1169 on v0.27.1. - **Frontend process count.** The regression is present at both 1 and 8 API-server processes, so it is not the serialization path. - **Config drift.** Startup configs of v0.14.1 and v0.27.1 were diffed: `enable_chunked_prefill=False`, `enable_prefix_caching=False`, `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, `enforce_eager=False` and the selected attention backend (`FLASH_ATTN`) are identical in both. The bisect points at the **torch 2.10 → 2.11 boundary**, i.e. between v0.19.1 and v0.20.0. We did not attempt to swap torch inside an image to confirm, and we have not narrowed it to a specific commit — happy to run further tests on this hardware if that would help. ## Separate finding: `--api-server-count 1` is a hard bottleneck for small pooling models Not a regression, but possibly worth documenting. With a lightweight embedder the single frontend process cannot serialize embeddings as fast as the GPU produces them: | `--api-server-count` | bge-m3, texts/s | host RAM used | |---|---|---| | 1 (default) | 1590 | 2.5 GiB | | 2 | 2661 | 4.0 GiB | | 4 | 3023 | 5.8 GiB | | 8 | **3079** | 9.4 GiB | | 16 | 3058 | 16.5 GiB | That is **+94% from a single flag**, with VRAM usage unchanged (one engine, one copy of weights). On the compute-bound `Qwen3-Embedding-4B` the same flag gives only +4.5%, as expected. A note in the pooling-models documentation that small embedders need more than one API-server process would have saved us a while. ## Before submitting a new issue - [x] Searched existing issues. [#42520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42520) is CPU-only with a different root cause (model compilation landing inside the benchmark window, fixed by [#42709](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42709)) — the reporter of that issue also re-measured on NVIDIA and found no regression. [#41390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41390) is about general pooling overhead versus HF Transformers and is still open. Neither covers this. - [x] Bisected across six releases to localize the change. - [x] Ruled out the obvious configuration and scheduling differences. - [x] Verified quality is unaffected, so this is throughput only.

signal.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 silent output corruption with MooncakeStoreConnector + MultiConnector; NIXL-only PD is stable
signal.text: ### Summary I am seeing intermittent silent output corruption / garbled generation when serving Kimi-K3 with TP=8 in a 1P1D disaggregated Prefill/Decode deployment using MooncakeStoreConnector together with NixlConnector through MultiConnector. The important A/B observation is: - **NIXL-only PD**: stable, no garbled output observed. - **NIXL + MooncakeStoreConnector through MultiConnector**: garbled output reproducibly appears under sustained load. - **Mooncake enabled + DSpark/speculative decoding disabled**: corruption still reproduces. - **Mooncake disabled**: corruption has not reproduced in my testing. Therefore speculative decoding does not appear to be required to trigger the corruption. The corrupted requests can generate long sequences of nonsensical mixed-language/repeated tokens, for example repeated words such as `Effective/effective` mixed with unrelated English/Chinese fragments. Some affected streams eventually surface at the application layer as HTTP 502 / `7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED`. This looks like a correctness issue rather than a crash-only issue: the engine can continue running while individual outputs are already corrupted. ### Deployment topology Two-node 1P1D deployment: ``` Prefill node Kimi-K3 TP=8 | | NIXL PD transfer v Decode node Kimi-K3 TP=8 ``` Failing configuration additionally uses: ``` Prefill | +-- MultiConnector | +-- NixlConnector | kv_role=kv_producer | +-- MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role=kv_both load_async=true lookup_async=true ``` The Decode node remains a NixlConnector consumer. ### Environment - **Model**: Kimi-K3 - **Tensor parallel size**: 8 - **PD topology**: 1 Prefill + 1 Decode - **KV transfer**: NIXL - **Prefix caching**: enabled - **KV cache dtype**: fp8 - **MLA prefill backend**: FLASHINFER - **VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT**: DS - **vLLM version**: Latest main / nightly - **vLLM commit**: Latest main - **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA B300 - **CUDA**: CUDA 12.8 - **OS / container image**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 / Container) Relevant upstream fixes included: - #48425: yes (tested on latest main) - #49499: yes (tested on latest main) - #49502: yes (tested on latest main) - #50344: yes (tested on latest main) ### Failing Prefill configuration Relevant environment: ```bash export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=4608 ``` KV connector: ```json KV='{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }, { "kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "load_async": true, "lookup_async": true } } ] } }' ``` Relevant server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enforce-eager \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --kv-transfer-config "$KV" ``` *(For minimal reproduction, run without `--speculative-config`, as the corruption reproduces without DSpark).* ### Decode configuration The Decode side uses NIXL only: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \ --compilation-config \ '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 ``` ### Stable control configuration If I remove `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `MultiConnector` and use only: ```json --kv-transfer-config \ '{ "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }' ``` on the Prefill side, the same Kimi-K3 TP8 PD setup is stable in my testing. The control setup still uses: - Kimi-K3 - TP=8 - prefix caching enabled - FP8 KV cache - FLASHINFER MLA prefill - NIXL PD transfer I have also tested DSpark/speculative decoding in the NIXL-only configuration without observing the same corruption. ### Reproduction A minimal A/B reproduction: 1. **Test A — Control**: - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Prefill with NixlConnector only. - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Decode with NixlConnector. - Enable prefix caching. - Run sustained concurrent traffic, including repeated/shared prefixes. - Confirm prefix-cache activity. - **Result**: No corrupted output observed. 2. **Test B — Failing**: - Keep the same model and PD topology, but replace the Prefill connector with `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`). - Run the same traffic and make sure Mooncake external cache hits are occurring. - **Result**: Intermittent silent output corruption / garbled text. 3. **Test C — DSpark disabled**: - Repeat Test B without any `--speculative-config`. - **Result**: Corruption still reproduces. (Speculative decoding is not the primary trigger). ### Actual behavior Affected generations suddenly degrade into nonsensical output containing repeated and unrelated multilingual tokens. Example pattern: ``` ... effective ... Effective ... effective ... ... random unrelated English words ... ... Chinese fragments ... ... repeated/degenerate text ... ``` The server does not necessarily crash immediately. At the upper service layer, affected streams can end as: ``` HTTP 502 7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED ``` ### Attachments I can provide: - screenshot of a corrupted generation; - Prometheus graphs from the failing run; - Prometheus graphs from the stable/control run; - complete Prefill/Decode logs around an affected request; - Mooncake hit/load metrics; - exact request ID / prompt and response if needed. ### Additional observation about speculative decoding When DSpark is enabled, I have also observed abnormal MTP/spec-decode acceptance behavior during some bad runs. However, I currently consider this a secondary symptom, because the output corruption can still reproduce after DSpark is completely disabled. Therefore this report is specifically about the Mooncake/external hybrid-cache path, rather than the DSpark rejection sampler. ### Expected behavior Loading a prefix from MooncakeStore should be correctness-equivalent to either: 1. recomputing the prefix, or 2. serving the same prefix from local GPU prefix cache. For Kimi-K3, all cache/state groups required to resume generation should represent the same safe token boundary. Enabling Mooncake external caching should not change model output correctness. ### Suspected area The A/B result suggests the issue is somewhere in the interaction between: - Kimi-K3 hybrid cache - `MooncakeStoreConnector` + `MultiConnector` - external prefix cache lookup/load - KDA recurrent state / attention KV reconciliation A possible failure mode would be a resume boundary where the attention KV and KDA recurrent state do not correspond to the same token position. I am particularly interested in whether the following invariant is always guaranteed for Mooncake external hits: ``` reported reusable prefix <= safe Full-Attention/MLA prefix <= valid boundary with corresponding KDA recurrent state ``` and whether all hybrid cache groups are invalidated/reconciled together if one external group is unavailable or has a shorter valid hit. ### Possibly related issues / PRs - #48425 — per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid models with KV connector - #49499 — Mooncake TP-sharded Mamba/linear-attention state corruption - #49502 — reliable partial-tail KV offload for sub-block prompts - #50344 — divergent hybrid cache hits scoped to capable connectors / MultiConnector behavior - #47812 — group-aware recovery for KV load failures on hybrid models - #50630 — hybrid recurrent-cache correctness / hit-boundary coordination discussion If my commit already contains them, this may indicate a remaining Kimi-K3-specific or MooncakeStore/MultiConnector-specific correctness path.
