### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description Using `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding together with the `xgrammar` structured-output backend causes valid concurrent structured-output requests to fail with HTTP 500. A single request using the same model, prompt, JSON schema, and server configuration succeeds. However, when 24 requests are sent with concurrency 8, most requests fail. On vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` The server logs report: ```text Failed to advance FSM ... Please file an issue. Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [...] Terminating request. Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The identical workload without speculative decoding succeeds 24/24. This was also reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. ## Environment ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.15.0 xgrammar: 0.2.3 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Maximum model length: 768 Maximum sequences: 16 Maximum batched tokens: 768 ``` Only one L40S GPU is required. ## Reproduction script The complete standalone reproduction script is attached as: [repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143661/repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py) The script does not depend on an external test framework. It automatically: 1. Starts vLLM with `ngram_gpu` and `xgrammar`. 2. Sends one structured request. 3. Sends 24 structured requests at concurrency 8. 4. Records the HTTP responses and relevant server errors. 5. Confirms that the server remains healthy. 6. Stops the server. 7. Starts an otherwise identical server without speculative decoding. 8. Repeats the same single and concurrent requests. 9. Writes all results to `result.json`. Run it with: ```bash python repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py \ --gpu 0 \ --out-dir ngram_gpu_xgrammar_repro ``` A `bug_reproduced` result intentionally exits with status 1. ## Failing server configuration The failing phase starts the server with: ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 768 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 \ --disable-log-stats \ --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram_gpu","num_speculative_tokens":4,"prompt_lookup_min":1,"prompt_lookup_max":4}' ``` ## JSON schema Every request uses the following schema: ```json { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } ``` ## Request input For request index `N`, the prompt is constructed as: ```python prefix = ( "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. " "Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. " ) * 6 prompt = ( f"{prefix}\nRequest id {N}. Return a JSON object with " '"status":"ok", "items":[1,2,3], and "request_id":' f"{N}." ) ``` The complete OpenAI-compatible request is: ```json { "model": "veritas-model", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. [repeated six times]\nRequest id 0. Return a JSON object with \"status\":\"ok\", \"items\":[1,2,3], and \"request_id\":0." } ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 80, "stream": false, "structured_outputs": { "json": { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } } } ``` ## Single-request result Before applying concurrent load, the script sends one request. Observed response: ```text HTTP 200 ``` The returned content is valid and satisfies the schema: ```json { "status": "ok", "items": [1, 2, 3], "request_id": 0 } ``` This confirms that: - The model is loaded correctly. - The request format is valid. - The schema is accepted. - xgrammar can compile and enforce the schema. - `ngram_gpu` can complete at least one structured request. ## Concurrent-load result The script sends: ```text Request count: 24 Concurrency: 8 ``` Observed result with vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Successful valid JSON responses: 3 HTTP 500 responses: 21 Invalid HTTP 200 responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Timeouts: 0 ``` The failed requests return: ```json { "error": { "code": 500, "message": "Internal server error", "param": null, "type": "InternalServerError" } } ``` ## Server log errors Representative server log output: ```text ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request ... for tokens 151667. Please file an issue. ``` ```text ERROR [scheduler.py:1835] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [151667] for request ... Terminating request. ``` Other rejected token IDs observed in the same run include: ```text 22335 630 ``` The API server subsequently reports: ```text Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The following log markers were all present: ```json { "failed_to_advance_fsm": true, "please_file_issue": true, "grammar_rejected_tokens": true, "internal_generation_error": true } ``` ## Server health after the failures After the 21 HTTP 500 responses, the script calls: ```text GET /v1/models ``` Observed result: ```text HTTP 200 ``` Therefore, this is a per-request internal generation failure rather than a complete server crash. ## Control without speculative decoding The script stops the failing server and starts an otherwise identical server without: ```text --speculative-config ``` The following settings remain unchanged: ```text Model Model dtype xgrammar backend JSON schema Prompts Request count Concurrency Maximum model length Maximum sequences Maximum batched tokens GPU ``` Control result: ```text Single request: HTTP 200, valid JSON Concurrent successful responses: 24 Concurrent HTTP 500 responses: 0 Invalid JSON responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` This isolates the failure to the interaction involving `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding. ## Reproduction on vLLM 0.26.0 The same interaction was previously reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. One run produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 ``` A separate run with asynchronous scheduling produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 2 HTTP 200, 22 HTTP 500 ``` The same server-side FSM and rejected-token errors were observed. The failure therefore reproduces on both: ```text vLLM 0.26.0 vLLM 0.27.1 ``` ## Expected behavior All valid concurrent structured-output requests should complete successfully. Speculative decoding may change performance, but it should not cause xgrammar to reject tokens that have already been accepted or committed by the scheduler. Expected result: ```text 24 HTTP 200 responses 24 valid JSON outputs 0 HTTP 500 responses ``` ## Actual behavior With `ngram_gpu` enabled: ```text 3 HTTP 200 responses 21 HTTP 500 responses ``` The structured-output FSM rejects generated tokens, the affected requests are terminated, and clients receive an internal server error. ## Reproducibility summary | Configuration | Single request | Concurrent result | Server after test | |---|---:|---:|---:| | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar without speculative decoding | Pass | 24/24 pass | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu, separate scheduling run | Pass | 2/24 pass, 22 HTTP 500 | Healthy | ## Attached evidence [result.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143667/result.json) [ngram_gpu_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143672/ngram_gpu_stdout.log) [ngram_gpu_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143685/ngram_gpu_stderr.log) [no_spec_control_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143690/no_spec_control_stdout.log) [no_spec_control_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143699/no_spec_control_stderr.log) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary LMCache prefill/decode disaggregation returns incorrect generation results after an apparently successful remote KV-cache transfer. The prefill and decode servers both: - Start successfully. - Return HTTP 200. - Remain healthy after the requests. - Report that LMCache P/D mode is enabled. - Report that the NIXL/UCX transfer channel is active. - Report complete prompt KV-cache hits on the decode receiver. Despite this, the P/D generation diverges from an equivalent monolithic vLLM server starting at generated token 0. The incorrect output frequently begins by reproducing tokens from inside the repeated prompt body: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ... ``` The monolithic server instead begins answering the instruction at the end of the prompt: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence ... ``` This is a silent correctness failure. It is not a startup failure, HTTP failure, missing-transfer failure, or unhealthy-engine failure. The issue was reproduced locally: - 6/6 comparisons failed across two independent vLLM 0.26.0 runs. - 3/3 comparisons failed in a separate vLLM 0.27.1 run. - Total: 9/9 LMCache P/D versus monolithic comparisons failed. - Native NIXL and Mooncake passed the identical monolithic-equivalence oracle. ## Environment Primary reproduction environment: ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S Prefill: 1 × L40S Decode: 1 × independent L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.26.0 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.14.1 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager Transfer channel: NIXL NIXL backend: UCX ``` The same failure was independently reproduced with: ```text Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.13.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B GPU: NVIDIA L40S Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager ``` ## LMCache prefill configuration Save as `lmcache_prefill.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "sender" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_proxy_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_proxy_port: 37413 pd_skip_proxy_notification: true ``` ## LMCache decode configuration Save as `lmcache_decode.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "receiver" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_peer_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_peer_init_port: [37413] pd_peer_alloc_port: [42727] ``` The exact port numbers can be replaced with any two unused local ports. The values above are taken from one representative reproduction. ## Common environment variables Run the following before starting the servers: ```bash export LMCACHE_USE_EXPERIMENTAL=True export PYTHONHASHSEED=123 export UCX_TLS=cuda_ipc,cuda_copy,tcp export VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=1 export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 ``` ## Start the prefill server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_prefill.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8100 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-prefill"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Start the decode server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_decode.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8200 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-decode"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Input Three independent prompts are generated. Each prompt contains a unique random request marker to prevent accidental reuse between repetitions. ```python import uuid repeat = 0 marker = f"VERITAS_PD_{repeat}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}" prompt = ( f"Request marker {marker}. " + "alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta " * 96 + " Summarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets." ) request_id = f"veritas-pd-{repeat}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}" ``` Depending on how the random marker is tokenized, the complete prompt contains approximately 895–898 tokens. The same exact `prompt` and `request_id` are used for the corresponding prefill and decode requests. ## Prefill request ```python import requests prefill_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "stream": False, "max_tokens": 1, "kv_transfer_params": { "disagg_spec": { "req_id": request_id, "receiver_host": "127.0.0.1", "receiver_init_port": [37413], "receiver_alloc_port": [42727], } }, } prefill_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/completions", json=prefill_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("prefill status:", prefill_response.status_code) print("prefill body:", prefill_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text prefill status: 200 ``` ## Decode request After the prefill request finishes, send the same prompt and request ID to the decode receiver: ```python decode_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } decode_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/completions", json=decode_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("decode status:", decode_response.status_code) print("decode body:", decode_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text decode status: 200 ``` Repeat this process three times with three independently generated markers and request IDs. ## Monolithic control After recording the P/D outputs, stop both the prefill and decode servers. Start a monolithic server without LMCache or any other KV connector: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8300 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager ``` Replay each previously recorded prompt byte-for-byte: ```python monolithic_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } monolithic_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8300/v1/completions", json=monolithic_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": f"mono-{request_id}"}, timeout=180, ) print("monolithic status:", monolithic_response.status_code) print("monolithic body:", monolithic_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text monolithic status: 200 ``` ## Comparison oracle For every prompt, compare the P/D result with the monolithic result using: 1. Generated token strings. 2. Generated text. 3. Selected-token log probabilities. 4. Top-5 token overlap at each generated position. The equivalence requirements are: ```text Generated tokens must be identical. Generated text must be identical. Maximum selected-token logprob absolute difference must be <= 0.25. Minimum top-5 overlap across generated positions must be >= 0.80. ``` The following inputs are identical between the P/D decode and monolithic control: ```text Prompt bytes Model Model dtype Execution mode Temperature Seed Maximum generated tokens Requested logprob count Prefix-caching setting ``` ## LMCache transfer evidence In a representative vLLM 0.26.0 run, the LMCache decode receiver logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` In the vLLM 0.27.1 confirmation run, the receiver similarly logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` The connector evidence collected from the server logs was: ```json { "lmcache_initialized": true, "pd_enabled": true, "nixl_channel": true, "cache_retrieval": true, "healthy_engine": true } ``` ## Representative output mismatch For one vLLM 0.26.0 repetition, the LMCache P/D output began with: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " alpha", " beta", " gamma", " delta", " epsilon", " z", "eta", " eta", " theta", " alpha", " beta", " gamma" ] ``` For the identical prompt, the monolithic output began with: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets. ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " ", "The", " problem", " is", " to", " summarize", " the", " operational", " sequence", " in", " exactly", " three" ] ``` The P/D and monolithic generations therefore diverged at generated token 0. A second prompt produced the following P/D output: ```text alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. ``` The monolithic server instead produced: ```text The first step is to identify the key elements of the system. The second step is to determine the appropriate tools and methods to achieve the goal. The third step is to implement the solution. ``` ## vLLM 0.26.0 results ### Independent run 1 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4423 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6104 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3309 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` ### Independent run 2 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3705 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4516 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3782 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 6/6 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All six comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## vLLM 0.27.1 results ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6067 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6052 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 2.5831 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 3/3 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All three comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## Native NIXL control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were run using the native vLLM NIXL connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0479 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0893 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0621 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Native NIXL verdict: ```text pass ``` ## Mooncake control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were also run using the Mooncake connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0942 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.1162 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0640 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Mooncake verdict: ```text pass ``` These controls use the same: ```text Model Prompt generation Prompt lengths GPU type BF16 dtype Temperature Seed Maximum generated token count Logprob count Monolithic-equivalence oracle ``` ## Reproducibility summary | Runtime | Connector | Comparisons | Result | |---|---|---:|---| | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 1 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 2 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.27.1 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Native NIXL | 3 | 3 equivalent | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Mooncake | 3 | 3 equivalent | Overall LMCache result: ```text 9/9 P/D versus monolithic comparisons mismatched. ``` ## Expected behavior When the LMCache receiver reports that the complete prompt KV cache was retrieved, decoding should be semantically equivalent to running the same prompt on a monolithic server with the same model and sampling configuration. In particular: - The first generated token should match. - The complete generated token sequence should match. - The generated text should match. - Token log probabilities should remain within normal BF16 numerical tolerance. - Top-k distributions should retain substantial overlap. ## Actual behavior The LMCache receiver reports a complete KV-cache hit and returns HTTP 200, but: - The first generated token differs from the monolithic result. - The complete 64-token output differs. - Generated text differs. - Minimum top-5 overlap reaches 0.0. - Maximum selected-token logprob differences reach approximately 2.58–3.61. - Output frequently begins with tokens taken from inside the repeated prompt body. - Both servers remain healthy. - No explicit runtime error is returned to the client. ## Classification This appears to be a remote KV restoration correctness failure rather than a transfer availability failure. The evidence shows that: - LMCache initializes successfully. - P/D mode is enabled. - The NIXL/UCX transfer path is active. - The receiver reports complete cache hits. - The inference engine reports zero computed prompt tokens. - Prefill and decode requests both return HTTP 200. - Both engines remain healthy. - The restored KV state does not preserve the expected next-token semantics. ## Reproduce * The full reproduction script can be seen here [repro_lmcache_pd.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31142926/repro_lmcache_pd.py). * Run it with 2 separate GPUs. `.../miniconda3/envs/vllm_0260/bin/python repro_lmcache_pd.py --prefill-gpu 0 --decode-gpu 1 --out-dir artifacts` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description The `lm-format-enforcer` structured-output backend fails with vLLM 0.26.0 because `lm-format-enforcer==0.11.3` imports `MistralTokenizer` from a module path that no longer exists. The affected import in `lm-format-enforcer==0.11.3` is: ```python from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer ``` In vLLM 0.26.0, `MistralTokenizer` is instead available at: ```python from vllm.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer ``` This causes two observable failures: 1. Importing `lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm` directly fails. 2. An OpenAI-compatible structured-output request returns HTTP 500 when the server uses the `lm-format-enforcer` backend. This bug is also reproduced on the latest vLLM 0.27.1. ## Package versions ```text vllm: 0.26.0 lm-format-enforcer: 0.11.3 torch: 2.11.0+cu130 python: 3.12.13 ``` vLLM 0.26.0 lists `lm-format-enforcer==0.11.3` in its requirements: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.26.0/requirements/common.txt#L22-L23 ## Minimal reproduction ```python from importlib.metadata import version print("vllm:", version("vllm"), flush=True) print("lm-format-enforcer:", version("lm-format-enforcer"), flush=True) from vllm.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer print("new path:", MistralTokenizer, flush=True) import lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm ``` Run it with: ```bash python repro_lmfe_import.py ``` ## Minimal reproduction output ```text vllm: 0.26.0 lm-format-enforcer: 0.11.3 new path: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/miniconda3/envs/vllm_veritas_0260/lib/python3.12/site-packages/lmformatenforcer/integrations/vllm.py", line 4, in from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer' During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/project/llm/vllm-veritas/artifacts/lmfe_bug_report_local/repro_lmfe_import.py", line 10, in import lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm File "/miniconda3/envs/vllm_veritas_0260/lib/python3.12/site-packages/lmformatenforcer/integrations/vllm.py", line 7, in raise ImportError('vllm is not installed. Please install it with "pip install vllm"') ImportError: vllm is not installed. Please install it with "pip install vllm" ``` The final error message is misleading: vLLM is installed, but the internal module path imported by LMFE no longer exists. ## End-to-end server reproduction Start the server: ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 512 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --disable-log-stats \ --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"lm-format-enforcer"}' ``` First, send a normal request: ```bash curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "veritas-model", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK." } ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 4 }' ``` The normal request succeeds with HTTP 200. Then send a structured JSON request: ```bash curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "veritas-model", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Return a JSON object with status ok, items [1,2,3], and request_id 0. Do not add prose." } ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 80, "stream": false, "structured_outputs": { "json": { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } } }' ``` ## Actual HTTP response The structured-output request returns HTTP 500: ```json { "error": { "code": 500, "message": "Internal server error", "param": null, "type": "InternalServerError" } } ``` The complete request sequence was: ```text Server startup: OK GET /v1/models: HTTP 200 Normal chat request before: HTTP 200 Structured JSON request: HTTP 500 GET /v1/models after: HTTP 200 Normal chat request after: HTTP 200 ``` The model and server therefore remain operational. The failure is specifically triggered when the LMFE structured-output backend is initialized. ## Server-side traceback ```text Unexpected error pre-processing request Traceback (most recent call last): File "/miniconda3/envs/vllm_veritas_0260/lib/python3.12/site-packages/lmformatenforcer/integrations/vllm.py", line 4, in from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer' During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "/miniconda3/envs/vllm_veritas_0260/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_lm_format_enforcer.py", line 38, in _cached_build_vllm_token_enforcer_tokenizer_data return lmfe_vllm.build_vllm_token_enforcer_tokenizer_data( ... File "/miniconda3/envs/vllm_veritas_0260/lib/python3.12/site-packages/lmformatenforcer/integrations/vllm.py", line 7, in raise ImportError('vllm is not installed. Please install it with "pip install vllm"') ImportError: vllm is not installed. Please install it with "pip install vllm" ``` ## Actual behavior - vLLM installs and starts successfully. - Normal inference works. - The first request that initializes the LMFE backend fails with HTTP 500. - The exception incorrectly reports that vLLM is not installed. - Repeated structured-output requests fail for the same reason. - Normal requests continue to work after the structured-output failure. ## Root cause `lm-format-enforcer==0.11.3` imports: ```python from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer ``` Source: https://github.com/noamgat/lm-format-enforcer/blob/v0.11.3/lmformatenforcer/integrations/vllm.py#L1-L7 However, vLLM 0.26.0 defines `MistralTokenizer` under: ```python vllm.tokenizers.mistral.MistralTokenizer ``` Source: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.26.0/vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py#L207 The failure therefore occurs while the LMFE tokenizer integration is imported, before structured decoding begins. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 (MXFP8) streaming: generation stops (empty delta, finish_reason=stop) right after reasoning closes, whenever a tool call should follow — non-streaming with identical payload succeeds
signal.text: ### Your current environment `collect_env.py` could not be run on this host — no outbound internet access (air-gapped deployment). Manually collected equivalent below. **Versions** - vLLM: `0.27.0` (build `vllm-0.27.0-tp4-41db7380`) - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu129` - Transformers: `5.15.0` - GPU: 4x NVIDIA H200 (143771 MiB), driver `595.58.03` **Model** - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` - Quantization: `mxfp8` (NVIDIA ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoint, `weight_block_size=[1,32]`, MoE via `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`/`MARLIN` backend) — vLLM's own startup log flags this format as *"experimental and could change in future"* **Launch command** ```bash vllm serve /model --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \ --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug With `stream: true` and `tools` provided, for requests where the model's reasoning is longer / more hedging before deciding to call a tool, the SSE stream **stops immediately after the reasoning block closes**: the next chunk has an empty `delta` and `finish_reason: "stop"`. Nothing is generated after that — no content, no `tool_calls`. This is not a parsing failure; generation itself halts. The byte-identical payload sent with `"stream": false` succeeds reliably (tested 6/6). > **Note:** only reproduced so far on an MXFP8-quantized checkpoint (NVIDIA ModelOpt format). Untested whether an unquantized bf16 checkpoint is also affected. **Minimal repro** Flat 2-field tool schema — confirmed tool schema complexity/count is not the trigger (fails the same way with 1 tool or 5 tools): ```python import requests payload = { "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", "stream": True, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "сделай docx с названием test и текстом привет"}], "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "generate_docx_report", "description": "Generate a Word document from content.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "filename": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["filename", "content"], }, }, }], "tool_choice": "auto", } r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, stream=True) for line in r.iter_lines(): if line: print(line.decode()) ``` **Expected** Reasoning closes, then either visible content or a populated `tool_calls` delta follows — same as the non-streaming response to the identical payload (`"stream": False` above). **Observed** After the last reasoning chunk, the stream emits one more chunk with an empty delta and `finish_reason: "stop"`, then ends. Nothing else is generated. **Ruled out** - Tool schema size — reproduces with both a minimal flat 2-field schema and a real ~2KB docstring-heavy schema - Tool count — 1 tool vs 5 tools, same result - Payload size in general — byte-identical payloads, only `stream` differs **Correlation observed (not confirmed causal)** Requests where the model's own reasoning is short/decisive stream through fine. Requests where reasoning is longer with self-correction (*"But I should check... Actually... Let me reconsider..."*) reliably hit the halt. **Current workaround** Routing tool-decision through a separate non-streaming call instead of native streaming tool-calling (application-level, not a real fix — costs 2x LLM calls per turn). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Doc]: vLLM's default NIXL connector is ~100× slower than the push connector on non-RDMA hardware, and the fix is undocumented
signal.text: ### 📚 The doc issue [cuda_ipc_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139915/cuda_ipc_probe.py) [nixl_bench.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139914/nixl_bench.py) [nixl-bench-pods.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139913/nixl-bench-pods.yaml) ## Summary On hardware without RDMA, where prefill and decode share a node, vLLM's `NixlConnector` transfers KV cache at **0.5 GB/s**. Switching a single config value to `NixlPushConnector` gives **49 GB/s** on the same hardware, same pods, same NIXL and UCX build — a **~100× difference** that matches raw CUDA peer-copy bandwidth. Cause: **NIXL/UCX `cuda_ipc` serves remote PUT at full speed but falls back to TCP for remote GET.** vLLM's `pull_worker.py` issues `make_prepped_xfer("READ", ...)`, and `NixlConnector` is a backward-compatible **alias for `NixlPullConnector`**, so the familiar connector name silently selects the slow direction. This is defensible design for the hardware NIXL targets: on InfiniBand or RoCE, RDMA READ and RDMA WRITE are symmetric at line rate, so a pull-based connector costs nothing and arguably reads better, since the consumer controls when it fetches. The asymmetry only appears on `cuda_ipc`, which is only reachable for same-node transfers without RDMA. Anyone deploying on an RDMA fabric would never see this. The problem is discoverability. `NixlPushConnector` does not appear in vLLM's NixlConnector documentation, and a web search for the name returns no results. A user on commodity GPU nodes therefore hits a 100× regression with no indication that a supported fix exists. --- ## Environment | item | value | |---|---| | Host | Google Cloud `g4-standard-96` (also reproduced on `g4-standard-384`) | | GPUs | 2 × NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), 96 GB | | Interconnect | **PCIe P2P, no NVLink, no RDMA.** `nvidia-smi topo -m` = `PIX`, `can_device_access_peer(0,1) = True` | | Driver | 580 | | Image | `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` | | NIXL | vendored 1.3.1/1.3.2; **also reproduced with 1.4.0** installed via pip | | Orchestration | reproduced both on GKE and on a bare VM with Docker | --- ## Measurements ### 1. The asymmetry, isolated from vLLM `bench/nixl_bench.py` calls `nixl._api` directly — no vLLM, no model, no KV cache. Two processes, one GPU each, 2.15 GB per transfer: | op | API | descriptors | Gbit/s | |---|---|---|---| | WRITE | `initialize_xfer` | 1 | 383.92 | | WRITE | `initialize_xfer` | 614 | 370.67 | | WRITE | `make_prepped_xfer` | 1 | 413.99 | | WRITE | `make_prepped_xfer` | 614 | 414.33 | | **READ** | `initialize_xfer` | 1 | **3.91** | | **READ** | `initialize_xfer` | 614 | **4.19** | | **READ** | `make_prepped_xfer` | 1 | **4.20** | | **READ** | `make_prepped_xfer` | 614 | **4.21** | The operation is the only variable that matters. The prepped-descriptor API versus `initialize_xfer` makes no difference, and descriptor count makes none either, so this is not batching or launch overhead. ### 2. The same asymmetry through vLLM Identical pods, identical settings, only `kv_connector` changed. Single request with a 30,067-token prompt, measured from `vllm:nixl_bytes_transferred_sum` and `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds_sum`: | `kv_connector` | bytes | time | bandwidth | |---|---|---|---| | `NixlConnector` (= `NixlPullConnector`, READ) | 2158 MB | 4.354 s | **0.50 GB/s** | | `NixlPushConnector` (WRITE) | 2158 MB | 0.044 s | **49.04 GB/s** | 49 GB/s matches raw CUDA peer copy on this host (48–51 GB/s), so the push path reaches full hardware bandwidth. ### 3. Reference bandwidths on the same host | path | bandwidth | |---|---| | Raw CUDA peer copy GPU0→GPU1 | 48–51 GB/s | | Raw CUDA IPC peer copy, two processes | 55.4 GB/s | | `iperf3` TCP loopback, single stream | 12 GB/s | | `iperf3` pod-to-pod, same node | 8.2 GB/s | | `iperf3` pod-to-pod, **cross-node** | 4.7 GB/s (37.5 Gbit/s); 21.6 GB/s with 8 streams | | NIXL READ path | 0.5 GB/s | Note the READ path is slower than plain TCP loopback by 24×, so it is not simply "falling back to the network"; it is well under what the network itself delivers. --- ## What was ruled out Each tested individually, with a redeploy and measurement: 1. **Kubernetes.** Reproduced on a bare VM with Docker and no CNI. 2. **Network bandwidth and latency.** 65.5 Gbit/s pod-to-pod, 0.016 ms RTT. 3. **Descriptor batching.** Flat from 1 to 2048 descriptors. 4. **NIXL version.** 1.4.0 behaves identically to 1.3.x. 5. **`--enable-cumem-allocator`.** vLLM's NixlConnector guide states the KV cache must be registered as VMM via this flag or NIXL "can only use RDMA/TCP". Removing it changed nothing measurable here. Worth reviewing: CUDA VMM allocations are not exportable via `cudaIpcGetMemHandle`, so the guidance may be counterproductive for the CUDA IPC path it describes. 6. **`UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y`**, also from that guide. On non-MNNVL hardware it logs `cuda_ipc_md.c:562 UCX ERROR multi-node NVLINK support is requested but not supported`. Removing it did not restore bandwidth, but the error suggests the flag should be conditional on MNNVL hardware. 7. **`UCX_TLS` list and `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE`.** No material effect. 8. **Privileges.** Both processes run as root with `CAP_IPC_LOCK`. --- ## Deployment preconditions found along the way These are not the bug, but they are undocumented and each silently costs the fast path. On GKE all of the following were required before `cuda_ipc` could be selected between pods at all: | setting | symptom when missing | |---|---| | `privileged: true` | The NVIDIA device plugin restricts GPUs through the cgroup device controller. `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` alone still leaves `nvidia-smi -L` showing one GPU even though `/dev/nvidia0..7` are mounted. | | `hostPID: true` | `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` returns `invalid device context (201)` | | `hostIPC: true` | necessary, not sufficient alone | | peer GPU visible to the importing container | `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` returns `invalid argument (1)` | `hostNetwork` is **not** required; it also collides on ports, since both llm-d roles bind 8000 and 5600. Note the security cost: privileged plus host PID/IPC makes Kubernetes GPU isolation advisory. That trade-off deserves to be stated in any guide that recommends same-node disaggregation. --- ## Suggested asks 1. **Document `NixlPushConnector`.** It currently appears nowhere in the NixlConnector usage guide and is not web-searchable. 2. **State the direction trade-off.** Recommend push on non-RDMA hardware and explain that pull is intended for fabrics where READ and WRITE are symmetric. 3. **Warn at runtime.** When a NIXL agent connects to a co-located peer and the selected transport for the transfer direction is not `cuda_ipc`, log a warning naming the transport. Today the degradation is silent and only discoverable by measuring. 4. **Revisit `--enable-cumem-allocator` and `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL` guidance**, which appear to be written for MNNVL systems and are at best inert, at worst counterproductive, elsewhere. 5. **Upstream to `ai-dynamo/nixl`:** is the PUT/GET asymmetry on `cuda_ipc` expected, or is remote GET simply not implemented for that transport? If expected, NIXL could surface it so callers can choose direction accordingly. --- ## Reproducers - `nixl_bench.py` — NIXL transfer benchmark, sweeps READ/WRITE × simple/prepped × descriptor count. No vLLM, no model. - `cuda_ipc_probe.py` — raw `cudaIpcGetMemHandle`/`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` across an arbitrary boundary, with a same-container control. - `nixl-bench-pods.yaml` — runs the benchmark as two GKE pods. Two implementation notes for anyone adapting these. The CUDA IPC handle must be carried as `c_ubyte[64]`; `c_char[64]` truncates it at the first NUL and yields a false negative. And the metadata-exchange directory must be wiped between runs, or the target sees a stale done-flag, exits immediately, and the initiator fails with `NIXL_ERR_BACKEND` against dead agent metadata. --- ## Related upstream material - [vllm-project/vllm#26382](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26382) — NIXL slowness on CUDA_IPC, attributed to transmission time and fixed with patched builds adding batching. Our descriptor sweep shows batching is not the mechanism; direction is. - [ai-dynamo/nixl#791](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/791) — low saturated bandwidth via the UCX backend. - [ai-dynamo/nixl#1614](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/1614) — `NIXL_ERR_BACKEND` cross-node, `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL` discussion. - [NVIDIA Dynamo disaggregated communication guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kubernetes-deployment/operate/disagg-communication) — describes `cuda_ipc` as "same-node, same-pod" and notes NVLink P2P needs a single process. Dynamo also uses NIXL, so the same asymmetry should be expected there on non-RDMA hardware. - [vLLM NixlConnector usage guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/nixl_connector_usage/) — the page that should mention `NixlPushConnector` and does not. --- AI assistance was used in this project. ### Suggest a potential alternative/fix _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bug]: GPT-OSS reasoning retains matched stop string when include_stop_str_in_output=false
signal.text: ### Your current environment ```text vLLM version: 0.27.0 Model: openai/gpt-oss-20b Precision: MXFP4 TP/PP: 1/1 Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions Streaming: false ``` This was observed in a downstream deployment based on vLLM v0.27.0. I have not yet reproduced it with the official upstream container. ### Describe the bug For a non-streaming GPT-OSS chat completion, vLLM detects a stop string in the reasoning output but returns that same stop string even when `include_stop_str_in_output` is `false`. Request: ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Can you write me a song?"} ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 500, "min_tokens": 0, "stop": ["song", "verse", "chorus", "bridge", "stanza", "melody"], "include_stop_str_in_output": false }' ``` The response had `content=null`, `finish_reason="stop"`, and `stop_reason="song"`. The returned `reasoning` text still ended with `song`, so the matched stop string remained in the response. ### Expected behavior With `include_stop_str_in_output=false`, the matched stop string should not be present in returned output. In this case, reasoning should end before `song`, or the API contract should explicitly document that reasoning is exempt from stop-string removal. The current `SamplingParams.stop` documentation says that returned output will not contain stop strings. `include_stop_str_in_output` is also documented as controlling whether stop strings are included in output text. ### Why this matters Reasoning models can stop before producing final content, leaving `content=null`. A client cannot validate stop-string exclusion by checking only `content`; the only returned model text is in `reasoning`. This also makes it unclear whether the problem is in engine stop-string truncation or in the GPT-OSS reasoning parser after the generated text is split into reasoning and content. ### Related issues - #51641 covers a streaming Qwen3 stop-buffer desynchronization. This report is non-streaming and uses the GPT-OSS reasoning parser. - #38789 reported another streaming reasoning-parser interaction with stop sequences. ### Before submitting a new issue - [x] I searched open and closed issues for `include_stop_str_in_output`, GPT-OSS, stop strings, and reasoning parser behavior.

signal.title: [Bug]: muse_glimmer cannot combine reasoning with structured outputs — schema is silently skipped when enable_in_reasoning=False
signal.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-29-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition Nvidia driver version : 595.84 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 24 Model name: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 285 Core(s) per socket: 24 Socket(s): 1 NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] nvidia-cudnn-cu13==9.20.0.48 [pip3] nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.15.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [conda] Could not collect ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d (git sha: 99a10304d) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-23 0 N/A ============================== Environment Variables ============================== VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 CUDA_VERSION=13.0.2 NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=0 TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0 VLLM_USAGE_SOURCE=production-docker-image VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT=99a10304dce8945119bd0b1a072297803c52a749 VLLM_IMAGE_TAG=vllm/vllm-openai:v99a10304dce8945119bd0b1a072297803c52a749-ubuntu2404 PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Build note.** I am on the commit-pinned muse_glimmer image (`vllm/vllm-openai:v99a10304dce8945119bd0b1a072297803c52a749-ubuntu2404`, reported by `collect_env.py` as `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d`). The published v0.27.0 and v0.27.1 releases do not include Muse Glimmer support, so I cannot retest on a tagged release yet. #51655 merged two days ago, and `vllm/reasoning/muse_glimmer_reasoning_parser.py` in this image is byte-identical to the file now on `main`, so what follows is not an artefact of the pre-merge build. **With `--reasoning-parser muse_glimmer`, asking for a JSON schema forces a trade-off: depending on `structured_outputs.enable_in_reasoning`, you can have reasoning or an enforced schema, but never both.** | `enable_in_reasoning` | `message.reasoning` | JSON schema | |---|---|---| | `True` | ❌ empty — the grammar masks from token 0, so the model never gets to open a `to=self` channel | ✅ enforced | | `False` (default) | ✅ correct | ❌ **silently not enforced** | With `enable_in_reasoning=False` the request returns 200, but nothing comes back in the requested JSON schema. ### Why it happens `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser` reports a reasoning end only when a **tool** channel opens. The decode-time predicate delegates straight to the tool-only one (`vllm/reasoning/muse_glimmer_reasoning_parser.py`, current `main`): ````python def is_reasoning_end_streaming( self, input_ids: Sequence[int], delta_ids: Iterable[int] ) -> bool: return self.is_reasoning_end(list(input_ids)) ```` and its docstring states the tool-only rule is deliberate: > A `to=user` answer is NOT a reason to leave the reasoning phase -- this parser > surfaces that content itself. Only a real tool channel switches the > `DelegatingParser` phase machine over to the tool parser. **That looks reasonable.** Muse Glimmer runs with `skip_special_tokens=False`, so framing markers survive into the decoded text. When no schema is involved the parser splits the `to=self` and `to=user` bodies itself and emits them clean. If it reported a reasoning end at `to=user`, the serving phase machine would hand a plain prose answer to the ATEM tool parser, which would see a bare `<|message|>`, misclassify it as the content channel, and leak framing into content. That said, `to=user` is where the model starts answering the user. Other reasoning parsers treat exactly that boundary as the end of reasoning: for a ``-style model, everything after `` is the user-facing answer, and that is where the grammar is allowed to start. Muse Glimmer's `to=user` channel is the same boundary expressed in a different framing, so it is reasonable to expect structured outputs to behave the same way here. With the current code base, however, structured outputs cannot follow that same boundary. A **second** consumer reads the same predicate to answer a **different** question: | Consumer | Question it asks | |---|---| | `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` | When should the stream go to the tool parser? | | `vllm/v1/structured_output/` | When may the grammar bitmask start being filled? | For a ``-style parser both questions share one answer, so the overload is invisible. Muse Glimmer has a separate answer channel and tool channel, and the two consumers want different answers at the same moment — which is why no single return value satisfies both, and why better detection alone cannot fix it. On a plain answer turn no tool channel is ever opened, so `reasoning_ended` never becomes `True`, `should_fill_bitmask()` keeps returning `False`, and the bitmask is never filled. The schema is never applied. ### Reproduce ````bash # stock image, no parser modifications vllm serve \ --reasoning-parser muse_glimmer \ --tool-call-parser muse_glimmer \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_strength":"low"}' # structured_outputs.enable_in_reasoning is left at its default (False) ```` ````bash curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this in the given schema."}], "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "name": "s", "schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"scenario": {"type": "string"}, "confidence": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["scenario", "confidence"], "additionalProperties": false}}}, "max_tokens": 8192 }' ```` The schema is requested per-request through `response_format` on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, not through a server-side flag — so vLLM does receive a well-formed schema request on the supported path. - **Observed:** the schema is not enforced. `message.content` comes back as free-form prose bearing no relation to the schema, with no error and no warning — every downstream node that parses these responses fell through to its deterministic fallback. `message.reasoning` is populated correctly. - **Expected:** `message.content` validates against the schema, and `message.reasoning` carries the `to=self` channel. Channel splitting itself is fine — `extract_reasoning` separates the bodies correctly. The only thing that fails is grammar activation. ### Proposed change Report the reasoning end at the `to=user` header, but **only in `is_reasoning_end_streaming()`** — the predicate the engine consults during decoding. The grammar then starts on the first token of the answer body, leaving the `to=self` channel unconstrained. Leave `is_reasoning_end()` tool-only. Every caller of that overload evaluates it against **prompt** token-ids, where a generated `to=user` header cannot appear, so widening it buys no decode-time behaviour; and since `_current_assistant_turn()` falls back to the whole text when there is no `<|start|>assistant`, an assistant-prefill or `continue_final_message` request would enter the tool phase at token 0. We have been running this patched parser in production, and both fields come back correctly: unconstrained reasoning in `message.reasoning`, and a schema-conformant object in `message.content`. **Existing behaviour is preserved.** We ran the patched parser against the current one on the same inputs: `_classify_bodies` and `extract_reasoning` produce byte-identical output, and the tool-handoff path is untouched. This adds a capability rather than trading one off. One complication remains: the serving phase machine calls the same streaming predicate and must **not** flip at `to=user`. In our deployment we gate the new branch on the instance never having been used as a streaming extractor — `parse_delta` calls `extract_reasoning_streaming()` before `is_reasoning_end_streaming()`, while the structured-output gate never calls the extractors at all. It works, but it couples the parser to an undocumented call ordering, so I would not propose shipping it as-is. Cleaner directions, in rough order of preference: 1. A separate predicate for the structured-output gate (e.g. `is_grammar_start_allowed()`) whose default delegates to the existing one, so no current parser changes behaviour. 2. Pass the consuming role to the reasoning parser at construction time. 3. At minimum, log a warning when a structured-output request finishes with the bitmask never having been filled, so this stops being a silent failure. Related: #39130 was the same symptom on `gemma4` with a different cause — there the end marker was absent from the prompt, and #45553 / #45588 fixed it by pre-initialising the parser engine from prompt state. Gemma 4 has a single boundary (everything after the channel close is content), so one predicate suffices there. I have a patch and unit tests for the parser-local version, and am happy to open a PR in whichever direction maintainers prefer. cc @xianbaoqian @jeejeelee ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bug]: two logger calls have mismatched %-args, so the log record is dropped
signal.text: Two `logger` calls pass arguments that don't match their format string. When either one fires, the logging module raises internally and the message you wanted is replaced by a `--- Logging error ---` traceback on stderr. The first is in `vllm/v1/engine/tensor_ipc.py` at lines 151 to 153: ```python logger.warning( "Discarding %d stale tensors from sender %s", sender_id, ) ``` Two placeholders and one argument, so this raises `TypeError: not enough arguments for format string`. There's a second problem in the same call: `sender_id` is annotated `str` at line 135, so it can't fill the `%d` slot regardless of ordering, and putting it first instead gives `TypeError: %d format: a number is required, not str`. The count that `%d` is asking for looks like it should come from the dict popped just above it, given that `_Sender.tensors` is `dict[int, dict[int, torch.Tensor]]` at line 111. The second is in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` at lines 1501 to 1504: ```python logger.debug( "MoRIIO handshake listener received done recv for req", req_id.decode(), ) ``` No placeholder at all and one argument, which gives `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting`, so the request id never makes it into the log. This one is debug level so it matters less, but it's the same mistake. I reproduced both of these with plain `logging` on a stock interpreter to confirm the record really is dropped rather than just formatted oddly. There was a third instance of this in `quick_all_reduce.py`, but #39127 is already open for it so I've left it alone.

signal.title: [Bug]: num_blocks division is a no-op in get_moe_wna16_block_config because block_size_k is reassigned first
signal.text: In `get_moe_wna16_block_config` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`, this block at lines 1250 to 1252 never actually changes `num_blocks`: ```python if size_k % 256 == 0 and num_blocks >= 256 and block_size_k < 256: block_size_k = 256 num_blocks = num_blocks // (256 // block_size_k) ``` `block_size_k` is set to 256 on the first line, so by the time the second line runs, `256 // block_size_k` is `256 // 256`, which is 1, and dividing by 1 leaves `num_blocks` untouched. The branch is guarded by `block_size_k < 256`, so the value being clobbered is 32, 64 or 128 depending on `group_size`, which means the divisor was presumably meant to be 8, 4 or 2. The block immediately below does the equivalent thing in the order that works, doubling `block_size_k` and then dividing `num_blocks` by 2. The effect is that `num_blocks` stays larger than it should be, and it gets compared against thresholds three more times before the function returns (`num_blocks >= 512` at line 1259, `num_blocks > 1024` at line 1264, `num_blocks >= 1024` at line 1269), so the inflated value pushes the heuristic toward bigger tiles than were intended. To get a sense of how often it matters I pulled the function out and ran it as written against the same function with those two lines in the other order, sweeping shapes for a few 4-bit MoE models (Mixtral 8x7B and 8x22B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2) over group_size 32/64/128, top_k 2/6/8, and token counts inside the `num_valid_tokens / num_experts <= 6` limit that `should_moe_wna16_use_cuda` enforces. 90 of 504 combinations came back with a different config. As one example, Mixtral-8x7B `w2` with group_size 128 and a single token gives `BLOCK_SIZE_N=256, BLOCK_SIZE_K=512` as written, versus `BLOCK_SIZE_N=128, BLOCK_SIZE_K=512` with the order swapped. Worth being clear about the blast radius: everything the function returns is still a legal config, and the divisibility guard at line 1277 still runs, so this looks like it costs performance on wna16 MoE rather than producing wrong output. I have not measured it on a GPU. Separately, the duplicated `size_k % (block_size_k * 2) == 0` term in the `if` a few lines down already has PRs open at #40547 and #48751. I checked both diffs and neither touches the lines above, so this is a different problem.

signal.title: [Performance][ROCm] gfx1100 long-prefill: unified attention BLOCK_M=16 default leaves ~2x on the table; BLOCK_M=64 gives 1.1-1.3x TTFT on latest main
signal.text: ## Summary On RDNA3 (gfx1100 / RX 7900 XTX), the unified Triton attention kernel (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`, TRITON_ATTN backend) is configured with `BLOCK_M=16` for every GQA model with `num_queries_per_kv <= 16`. For long prefill (8k tokens) this leaves the kernel at roughly half its achievable throughput. Raising the query block to `BLOCK_M=64` (`BLOCK_Q=8` for `nq_per_kv=7`, `BLOCK_Q=16` for `nq_per_kv=4`) improves prefill TTFT by **1.1-1.3x** across 4 models and 3 quantization regimes on latest main, with bitwise-identical outputs and no decode regression. ## Environment - GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 96 CU, 960 GB/s) - vLLM: **main @ 53e211d (2026-08-17), built from source as a ROCm wheel** (torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14, triton 3.7.1, ROCm 7.2.4 toolchain) - Backend: `attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN"`, eager mode, single sequence - Measured at in=8192 tokens (the regime where attention is 30-65% of wall) ## Data (in=8192, same-process interleaved A/B, min of 2 reps, greedy first-token correctness) | Model | Quant | nq/kv | wall baseline (BLOCK_M=16) | wall BQ=8 | speedup | correctness | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | Qwen2.5-7B | int4 GPTQ | 28/4 | 2305 ms | 1921 ms | **1.20x** | identical | | Llama-3-8B | bf16 | 32/8 | 2731 ms | 2458 ms | **1.11x** | identical | | Qwen3-4B | bf16 | 32/8 | 1912 ms | 1597 ms | **1.20x** | identical | | Llama-3-8B | fp8 KV (fp8_e4m3) | 32/8 | 3884 ms | 2995 ms | **1.30x** | identical | - Attention-kernel time: 1.26-2.18x faster with `BLOCK_M=64` (Qwen2.5-7B: 43 -> 93 TFLOPS on the fp16 path; rocBLAS fp16 GEMM wall on this GPU is ~107 TFLOPS). - Decode TPOT: unchanged (interleaved 3x, all within noise). - Output tokens identical for every config/model at 512/2048/8192. ## Sweep context (what we tried and why BLOCK_M=64 is the sweet spot on gfx1100) Single-model sweep (Qwen2.5-7B, in=8192): | BLOCK_Q (BLOCK_M) | wall speedup vs default | |---|---:| | 2 (16) — default | 1.00x | | 4 (32) | 1.13x | | **8 (64)** | **1.24x** | | 16 (128) | 1.16x | | 32 (256) | 0.77x (register spilling, bimodal) | - `num_warps=8` at BLOCK_M=64 is much worse than 4 warps (2x slower). - `TILE_SIZE_PREFILL=64` hurts; 128 exceeds the gfx1100 64KB LDS limit (K+V tiles alone need 64KB). - split-KV prefill (reusing the 3D decode path) is numerically correct but neutral at 8k tokens — the prefill grid is already large (thousands of CTAs), so extra parallelism has nothing to buy. - KV cache `block_size` 16 -> 64: neutral at BLOCK_M=64. ## Why this looks like a config-selection bug, not a kernel bug The wrapper hardcodes: ```python BLOCK_M = 16 if num_queries_per_kv <= 16 else triton.next_power_of_2(num_queries_per_kv) BLOCK_Q = BLOCK_M // num_queries_per_kv ``` `BLOCK_M=16` was chosen for the decode-shaped workload (1 query row per CTA). At long prefill the same CTA iterates 256+ KV tiles, and the 16-row Q tile makes each `tl.dot` tiny and the loop latency-bound; `BLOCK_M=64` raises the arithmetic intensity per KV byte 4x and cuts the grid from ~16k to ~4k CTAs. Notably, main already ships a precedent for platform/regime-conditional tuning of this exact kernel (`tuned_large_head`: head=256 prefill on Blackwell -> BLOCK_M=32, 8 warps, TILE=128), and an AMD gfx1100-specific tile heuristic was accepted for `triton_scaled_mm` (#34275) — but no gfx11 config exists for this kernel. ## Suggested fix direction Follow the `tuned_large_head` pattern and add a gfx11 (RDNA3) long-prefill launch config, e.g. `max_seqlen_q > 1 and num_queries_per_kv <= 16` on gfx11 -> `BLOCK_M=64`, 4 warps, TILE=32. Alternatively feed this data into the platform block-size autotune (per the 2026 Triton-backend deep dive). If a global default change is preferred, it needs CUDA A/B — we have no NVIDIA numbers and `BLOCK_M=16` may be deliberate there. ## Repro The change is a single launch-parameter override; the experiment scripts and full data are in `experiments/vllm-rdna3-w4a16-kernel-test/` (`attn_multimodel_bench.py` + `EXPERIMENT_RECORD_BLOCK_Q8.md`). Happy to turn the sweep into a minimal patch (BLOCK_M selection + a gfx11 conditional) if maintainers want it. ## Notes / caveats - fp8 WEIGHTS could not be exercised on gfx1100: vLLM ROCm's fp8 GEMM uses `torch._scaled_mm`, which requires MI300+. fp8 coverage here is via an fp8_e4m3 KV cache (bf16 weights), i.e. the fp8 attention path. - bf16 attention is noticeably slower than fp16 on RDNA3 (captured real llama3 q/KV are bf16) — separate observation, not required for this fix.

signal.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix PEFT 0.18+ target_parameters LoRA loading for 3D MoE experts
signal.text: # [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix PEFT 0.18+ target_parameters LoRA loading for 3D MoE experts ## Problem PEFT 0.18+ can train a LoRA against a fused 3D MoE expert parameter via `target_parameters` (e.g. `mlp.experts.gate_up_proj` / `down_proj`), reading it `[E, dim1, dim2]` as `[E, in, out]`. vLLM's `add_lora_w13` / `add_lora_w2` punica kernels use the opposite `nn.Linear` `[out, in]` convention, so per expert `ΔW_vllm = ΔW_peft^T`. On stock vLLM, `_stack_moe_lora_weights` reshapes with the wrong semantics and `set_lora` raises a shape mismatch that drops the adapter (e.g. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B `down_proj`: `512 vs 2048`). ## Fix - `peft_helper.py`: parse `target_parameters` from `adapter_config.json`. - `lora_model.py`: propagate it onto `LoRAModel` (ctor, `clone()`, `from_lora_tensors`). - `model_manager.py`: in `_stack_moe_lora_weights`, detect the PEFT 3D layout and swap `lora_A`/`lora_B` + transpose the trailing two dims **after** the EP-aware expert slicing. Detection is required, not assumed: `create_dummy_lora_weights` builds dummies in the native layout with the same flat shape, so an unconditional transpose would corrupt them. Primary signal is `target_parameters` naming a fused expert weight; fallback is `lora_a` trailing dim != `hidden_size`. ## Testing ``` python -m pytest -v \ tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py::test_peft_helper_target_parameters_direct \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_target_parameters_indicates_3d_lora \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_from_lora_tensors_propagates_target_parameters \ tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py::test_peft_helper_pass \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_from_lora_tensors ``` → **10 passed** (the discriminator test is parametrized over 6 cases). **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B expert LoRA).** The raw PEFT adapter crashes the unpatched loader with the `512 vs 2048` error. With the fix, the directly-loaded adapter is **bit-identical** (chosen-token logprobs, 32 tokens × 5 prompts) to an independent offline-converted oracle that self-checks `max|ΔW_vllm − ΔW_peft^T| = 0` over 320 experts, while both shift logits measurably vs base — so the adapter takes effect and the in-loader transpose matches the verified transform. Logprobs, not decoded text: for an experts-only (8-of-256, rank-32) adapter, greedy text is a false-negative trap since the adapter shifts logits without always flipping the argmax on short prompts. ## Latency impact None expected. The transpose runs inside `_stack_moe_lora_weights` — the adapter-load path, once per adapter (two `.transpose(-2, -1).contiguous()` per fused expert weight). The per-forward hot path (`add_lora_w13` / `add_lora_w2`) is not touched. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used to author this change. A human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.
signal.author: darrenpeng-amazon

signal.title: [Kernel] Skip padding rows in SiTU activation for DeepEP v2 decode
signal.text: ## Purpose Skip padding rows in the SiTU (SituGLU) activation kernel during DeepEP v2 decode. With DeepEP v2, the receive buffer is worst-case allocated (`num_max_tokens_per_rank * world_size`), but during decode only a fraction of rows hold valid tokens. The `situ_and_mul` kernel was launching one block per row over the whole buffer, so for typical decode batches most of that compute was spent on padding (roughly 87% wasted for the batch sizes we measured on Kimi-K3). This threads the device-side `psum_recv_per_rank` count from DeepEP v2 through `ExpertTokensMetadata` -> `HummingIndexedExperts` -> `apply_moe_activation` -> the `situ_and_mul` CUDA op, and adds an early-exit so blocks past the valid row count return immediately. The count is read through a device pointer inside the kernel, so it stays CUDA-graph safe (no host sync, value resolved at launch time). ## Changes - `situ_and_mul` gains an optional `valid_rows` tensor argument (`Tensor? valid_rows=None`); the kernel returns early when `row >= *valid_rows_ptr`. `valid_rows=None` preserves the previous full-buffer behavior for every other caller. - `ExpertTokensMetadata` carries an optional `psum_recv_per_rank`; DeepEP v2 populates it only in cudagraph (decode) mode. - `HummingIndexedExperts.apply()` derives `valid_rows = psum_recv_per_rank[-1] * topk` and forwards it to the activation. Non-Humming activations and the prefill path are unaffected: `psum_recv_per_rank` stays `None`, so `valid_rows` is `None`. ## Test Plan Correctness is covered by the existing GSM8K humming configs (the padded rows contain no valid tokens, so masking them cannot change output). The win is a decode-time reduction in blocks launched by the SiTU kernel; benchmark numbers on H200 to follow. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Perf] Add adaptive sync-less DeepEP v2 prefill dispatch
signal.text: ## Summary - Add an opt-in `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_MAX_SYNCLESS_TOKENS` threshold, disabled by default. - Select sync-less eager prefill dispatch from the maximum post-sequence-parallel token count across DP ranks. - Reconstruct aligned expert counts and expert IDs from DeepEP GPU prefix sums, avoiding the host count poll. - Keep synchronized dispatch for larger prefills and preserve the existing cudagraph/decode path. - Zero unused expanded rows before non-block input quantization. ## DeepEP behavior This follows the linked ElasticBuffer implementation at https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/blob/01dc3aaac82068020353dce2c302e38153c0bfaa/csrc/elastic/buffer.hpp#L1065-L1071. With `do_cpu_sync=False`, DeepEP allocates the rank/top-k worst case plus per-expert alignment padding. Its GPU prefix sums encode each real expert count as `psum[i] - align(psum[i - 1], expert_alignment)`, so vLLM can rebuild expert metadata without reading routing counts on the CPU. ## Duplicate-work check I searched open PRs for DeepEP v2 sync-less dispatch, `do_cpu_sync`, and ElasticBuffer prefill dispatch. This is not a duplicate of #50511: that draft fixes padding and metadata handling in existing contiguous-layout decode paths. This PR adds a new adaptive eager-prefill mode and intentionally leaves the baseline decode behavior unchanged. ## Testing Passed in the managed PR worktree environment: - `chg run -g 2 --timeout 30m -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py::test_deep_ep_v2_moe[world_dp_size0-6-32-32-256-1024-64-dtype0] tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py::test_deep_ep_v2_moe[world_dp_size0-6-32-32-256-1024-64-dtype1] -vv -s` — 2 passed in 54.01s on two B300 GPUs - The two cases exercise BF16 and FP8 expert weights with `m=32` and sync-less threshold `64`, comparing DeepEP dispatch, expert execution, and combine against the PyTorch reference - A separate two-rank smoke invocation of the same reference-comparison worker with `use_fp8_dispatch=True`, BF16 expert weights, `m=32`, and threshold `64` — passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py --collect-only -q` — 15 tests collected; the existing end-to-end matrix includes sync-less prefill without adding test cases - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_envs.py -q` — 54 passed - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py` — passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, and environment-default checks - Static hot-path sync audit — no new GPU-to-CPU conversion or explicit barrier - CUDA synchronization debug check for the GPU metadata builder on the earlier equivalent implementation — passed The GPU runs emitted the existing default-MoE-config and ElasticBuffer teardown warnings; output correctness passed in all cases. No model evaluation was run because the feature is opt-in and does not change model semantics. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to inspect DeepEP, develop the implementation and tests, run validation, and draft this PR. Before this draft is marked ready, the human submitter must review every changed line and understand and be able to defend the change end-to-end.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Bound draft max_model_len by the target before logging
signal.text: Fixes #29945 ## The bug With MTP or any other in-checkpoint drafter, startup prints two different max model lengths for the same run: ``` [model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration [model.py:1684] Using max model len 131072 [model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP [model.py:1684] Using max model len 262144 ``` Users read the second line as the drafter being sized for a longer context than the target and reasonably conclude that KV cache is being over-allocated. The issue has collected repeat reports on Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and GLM-4.5-Air since December, including cases where an explicit `--max-model-len 8192` still printed `Using max model len 262144` for the draft. @benchislett investigated twice and confirmed there is no over-allocation, since `SpeculativeConfig._maybe_override_draft_max_model_len` clamps the draft to the target immediately after the model config is built, and invited a PR to fix the log. ## Root cause `ModelConfig` for the draft is constructed with `spec_target_max_model_len=target_model_config.max_model_len`, but `_get_and_verify_max_len` only consults that argument inside the `derived_max_model_len == inf` branch, which is the fallback for checkpoints that declare no length key at all. Every real MTP or EAGLE checkpoint does declare one, so the argument is dead in practice and the draft resolves to its own declared length, logs it, and is only corrected one step later by the clamp in `SpeculativeConfig`. So the bound exists twice, in two different places, and the value that gets logged is the one from before the bound is applied. ## The fix Apply `spec_target_max_model_len` as an upper bound in `_get_and_verify_max_len` whenever the length is being derived, so the draft resolves and logs the value it will actually run with. The later clamp in `SpeculativeConfig` becomes a no-op, which also stops its `Overriding draft model max model len` line from firing on a config that was never wrong. The bound is applied only when the caller did not pass an explicit length. An explicit `speculative_config.max_model_len` keeps flowing through `_maybe_override_draft_max_model_len` and its existing validation, so the `speculative_max_model_len cannot be larger than target_max_model_len` error and the `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN` escape hatch behave exactly as before. `spec_target_max_model_len` is set on exactly one `ModelConfig` in the tree, the speculative draft one, so the blast radius is the drafter and nothing else. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "29945 in:body"` and `--search "spec_target_max_model_len"` both return nothing, and the issue has no PR cross-references. The open PRs matching "draft max model len" are unrelated: #43049 caps per-request ngram drafts, #47272 reserves the KV null block during `max_model_len` validation, #44954 fixes a DP drafter hang. None of them touch how the draft `ModelConfig` resolves its length. ## Testing Added `test_get_and_verify_max_len_bounds_draft_by_target` to `tests/test_config.py`, next to the existing `test_get_and_verify_max_len`. It drives `_get_and_verify_max_len` directly with a stub arch config, so it needs no network and no accelerator, and covers draft longer than target, equal, and draft shorter than target. ``` pytest tests/test_config.py -k get_and_verify_max_len -q ``` I do not have a GPU, so I verified the behavior change by extracting the real `_get_and_verify_max_len` source from both `HEAD` and the patched tree, running both against the exact length pairs from the issue reports, and feeding each result through a mirror of `_maybe_override_draft_max_model_len`: ``` case logged before logged after final override-log Qwen3.5 MTP (SurealCereal) 262144 131072 131072 before=True after=False Qwen3-Next MTP (reporter) 262144 8192 8192 before=True after=False GLM-4.5-Air (ruokee) 131072 64000 64000 before=True after=False draft shorter than target 4096 4096 4096 before=False after=False equal lengths 131072 131072 131072 before=False after=False final resolved length unchanged in every case: True ``` The final draft `max_model_len` is identical before and after in every case, so this does not change generation, accuracy, or serving behavior. It only moves an existing bound earlier so the reported value stops disagreeing with the value in use. On that basis I did not run model evals, and I am happy to add them if a reviewer disagrees with that reading. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files. ## AI assistance This change was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line, traced the two-step bound through `vllm/config/model.py` and `vllm/config/speculative.py` myself, and ran the verification above. I will respond to review feedback.
