signal.title: [ROCm] Cpu offload for ROCm 7.13+ to align the hipMemcpyBatchAsync params and perf in 7.14x
signal.text: ## Purpose This is related to the issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44341 In a previous enablement PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40549, we enabled cpu offloading on ROCm, and we noticed the shortcoming of the hipMemcpyBatchAsync API lacked support on numAttrs paramter. This PR is to fix that situation. This PR is intended to be future compatible and backward compatible. Below is the details: For the hipMemcpyBatchAsync API, (1) ROCm 7.13 will accept numAttrs > 0 while ROCm 7.2.1 - ROCm 7.2.3 do not. Prepare the code to accommodate this change so that it works now and after the vllm is upgraded to ROCm 7.13+ base. While testing, found that the hipMemcpyBatchAsync performance was not really doing any batching. Issue was discussed internally, and was addressed later and the fix would be packaged to rocm 7.14x. (2) On rocm 7.14 or rocm 7.15, the hipMemcpyBatchAsync performance is optimized comparing with the non-batching hipMemcpyAsync API. (3) When testing with a staging rocm 7.15 docker image, found an problem with `count` in the `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` API. hipMemcpyBatchAsync faults (GPU memory access fault -> abort/segfault) when count > 8192, regardless of copy size, direction, or numAttrs. This is being addressed by runtime team. For now, I added an enviornment variable VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS to chunk the batch copies to work around this problem. ## Test Plan (1) vllm unit test, regression test with vllm nightly image (1.1) Tested hipMemcpyBatchAsync API in a rocm7.13 container and verified it accepts numAttrs=1. (1.2) Tested the micro-benchmarking to compare hipMemcpyBatchAsync and hipMemcpyAsync performance, and found the performance issue of hipMemcpyBatchAsync and filed an internal ticket. (2) Tested with a rocm 7.14 or 7.15 to check the micro-benchmarking to compare hipMemcpyBatchAsync and hipMemcpyAsync performance, after the hipMemcpyBatchAsync is optimized and packaged. ## Test Result (1) micro-benchmarking test: Using a hip program to benchmark the hipMemcpyBatchAsync(numAttrs=1) performance vs hipMemcpyAsync. In ROCm 7.2.3, the performance of hipMemcpyBatchAsync is almost the same (i.e., 1x) as hipMemcpyAsync, as there is no batching implemented. The optimization is happening rocm 7.14+. So on a wheel-packaged ROCm 7.15 nightly (8× MI350X, gfx950), `hipMemcpyBatchAsync(numAttrs=1)` is now 6–19× faster than a per-op `hipMemcpyAsync` loop, reproducible across two runs: dir | block | batch | per-op | ratio -- | -- | -- | -- | -- store (D→H) | 4 KiB | 25.4 GB/s | 1.6 GB/s | ×15.4 store (D→H) | 64 KiB | 48.9 GB/s | 6.3 GB/s | ×7.7 load (H→D) | 4 KiB | 31.5 GB/s | 1.7 GB/s | ×19.1 load (H→D) | 64 KiB | 49.0 GB/s | 5.8 GB/s | ×8.4 (2) agentic workflow test: On the same rocm 7.15 docker, performed an agentx vllm workflow test, and found an issue with hipMemcpyBatchAsync api when count > 8192, GPU would seg fault. Discussed internally, and the fix is on the way, but will not be in rocm7.14x. So, for now, added an env to chunk the batches to avoid the seg fault VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS .

signal.title: [CI][AMD] Improve Kubernetes failure diagnostics
signal.text: Collect Kubernetes-scoped AMD CI failure evidence while keeping the failing test log concise and immediately visible. - Resolve the current cgroup-v2 directory through `/proc/self/cgroup` and mountinfo instead of assuming node-level resource paths. - Capture pod, namespace, node, process limits, PID/RSS state, checkout/workspace/tmp/shared-memory mounts, device-node permissions, GPU health, and network timing. - Keep infrastructure diagnostics for CPU-only AMD jobs while skipping only GPU probes. - Write detailed evidence to `artifacts/amd-gpu-diagnostics/<job-id>/diagnostics.log` without duplicating it into the terminal log. - Reject artifact paths that escape the checkout or resolve through symlinks. - Print a dependency-free two-column Bash summary at the end, with no emoji shortcode or separate Buildkite diagnostics group. - Preserve `--- Test log` so the pytest failure and infrastructure summary remain in the same last-expanded section. - Let Buildkite perform the upload after the command exits; there is no custom uploader or upload timeout in the runner. Depends on [vllm-project/ci-infra#475](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/475), which configures the exact `artifact_paths` pattern and should merge first.

signal.title: [Build] Add CUDA 13.4 prerelease image pipeline
signal.text: ## Summary Add an image-only CUDA 13.4rc1 prerelease path for Rubin (`sm_107`): - overlay NVIDIA's `cuda-toolkit==13.4.0rc1` PyPI packages when CUDA 13.4 container images are unavailable - pin mutually compatible CUDA 13.4 PyTorch, torchvision, and torchaudio nightlies - preserve the CUDA driver stub and expose linker names/NCCL needed by native and JIT extensions - install a host C/C++ compiler and set `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas` - add a manually gated, multi-arch Buildkite staging pipeline with native image smoke tests The normal CUDA image and release paths are unchanged unless the new build arguments are supplied. Tracks #49735. ## Duplicate-work check The required issue and open-PR searches found no other PR addressing the CUDA 13.4 prerelease image path. This does not duplicate the separate SM107 kernel-build and NVLink workstreams tracked by #49735. ## Validation - `bash -n .buildkite/scripts/validate-cuda134-image.sh` — passed - `pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile .buildkite/scripts/validate-cuda134-image.sh` — passed - PR DCO and pre-commit CI — passed - native ARM64 `vllm-openai` BuildKit build of exact PR head `3e400878212d939db56c24dd854309ac553dfdff` on Pirate `cpu-07` — passed - published-image validation on `linux/arm64` — passed: - exact PyTorch, torchvision, and torchaudio CUDA 13.4 nightly versions - vLLM import and `_C_stable_libtorch` extension discovery - CUDA 13.4 `nvcc` and `ptxas` - GCC/G++ compile-and-execute smoke tests - `-lcuda` JIT-style link with no undefined symbols and `libcuda.so.1` SONAME Exact PR-head ARM64 image: ```text quay.io/tms/vllm-dev:cu134-rc1-3e40087821 sha256:0c112e15ca05c16712f48514445dc08b914bcd2061efac0f0cb592281c1bb608 ``` This tag is an ARM64 manifest for Rubin validation, not a multi-platform index. The earlier staged multi-platform image validated the unchanged AMD64 path and both manifest descriptors. ## Model and Rubin validation The image changes do not intentionally affect model output. On SM107 prerelease hardware, the preceding image passed vLLM import/device-capability validation. A derived image containing the compiler and driver-link fixes also passed `torch.compile`, FlashInfer sampling JIT compilation/linking, full vLLM startup, and a GSM8K smoke evaluation. The exact PR-head image still needs the GPU-only Rubin checks (`just rubin-smoke`, `just compile-smoke`, server startup, and `just eval-smoke`). ## AI assistance and human accountability OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, build orchestration, and validation. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the image/toolkit design, and verify the GPU-only Rubin checks before marking the PR ready.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **This bug can be simply circumvented by just having a few warm up rounds, but I still report it here for the record 😶‍🌫️** Brief Env: vLLM version: 0.19.0 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB (SXM) OS: Linux (RHEL 8) CUDA: 12.x PyTorch: (matches vllm 0.19 requirements) ## Summary With `--enable-prefix-caching` (the v1 default for supported models), the same `/v1/completions` request sent multiple times sequentially to the same vLLM server returns 2 distinct outputs at `temperature=0`: - **Run 1** on a freshly started server returns output A. - **Runs 2..N** return output B ≠ A, but stable across runs. Restarting the server returns the first request to A. Disabling prefix caching with `--no-enable-prefix-caching` makes the output deterministic across all runs. This is a correctness bug, since the documented behavior at `temperature=0` is deterministic decoding. ### Server (default v1 config; prefix caching is auto-enabled for Qwen3-8B) ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --port 8002 \ --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 ``` > Note: in vLLM v1, `enable_prefix_caching` defaults to `model_config.is_prefix_caching_supported` (True for Qwen3-8B). Removing `--enable-prefix-caching` from the cmdline does NOT disable it; only `--no-enable-prefix-caching` does. ### Reproducer script [repro_for_issue.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/6002d9f3c9bf14e964ac93bffee6a686#file-repro_for_issue-py) [`repro_for_issue.py`](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/6002d9f3c9bf14e964ac93bffee6a686#file-repro_for_issue-py) sends the same prompt 5 times sequentially with `temperature=0`, `logprobs=5`, `stream=False`, and reports unique-output count: ```bash python repro_for_issue.py --base-url http://localhost:8002 --prompt-len 32 ``` ### Observed Output (default config, prefix caching ON) ``` runs: 5, prompt_seed: 'repro-issue-001' temperature: 0, logprobs: 5 run 1/5: Okay, let me try to figure out what's going on here. So, there's th run 2/5: The next completion should be deterministic because temperature is z run 3/5: The next completion should be deterministic because temperature is z run 4/5: The next completion should be deterministic because temperature is z run 5/5: The next completion should be deterministic because temperature is z unique outputs: 2 / 5 First divergence at character offset 2 (output token 0): variant 1 token = ' ' variant 2 token = ' ' ``` Re-running the script on the same server (no restart) returns `unique = 1` (variant 1 only). Restart returns the pattern. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Restore vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer shim for lm-format-enforcer
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix #52614. PR #35024 removed `vllm/transformers_utils/tokenizer.py` after lm-eval dropped its usage. However, `lm-format-enforcer==0.11.3` — pinned in `requirements/common.txt` — still does `from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer` at the top of `lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm`. That raises `ImportError`, so any structured-output request against the lm-format-enforcer backend fails with HTTP 500 (the backend module itself becomes unloadable). This PR restores `vllm/transformers_utils/tokenizer.py` as a minimal lazy `__getattr__` shim that re-exports `MistralTokenizer` from its new home (`vllm.tokenizers.mistral`) with a `DeprecationWarning` — the same pattern the removed module itself used for lm-eval before its removal. Keep until lm-format-enforcer updates its import and vLLM pins the new release. Known remaining gap (out of scope here): lm-format-enforcer 0.11.3 also imports the pre-5.0 `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` spelling from transformers; that is fixed in upstream lm-format-enforcer `main` but unreleased, so fully restoring the LMFE backend on transformers >= 5 additionally requires the next lm-format-enforcer release (no vLLM-side action possible for that import; the break this PR fixes is the only vLLM-side one). ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_tokenizer_shim.py -v ``` The legacy-path test executes the exact import line that broke (`from vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer import MistralTokenizer`) and asserts it resolves to the same class object (LMFE does an `isinstance` check against it). An end-to-end LMFE import test is intentionally not included — see "Known remaining gap" above; it would exercise a third-party break, not this shim. ## Test Result Unit tests: ``` tests/transformers_utils/test_tokenizer_shim.py::test_mistral_tokenizer_legacy_import_path PASSED tests/transformers_utils/test_tokenizer_shim.py::test_shim_rejects_unknown_attributes PASSED ============================== 2 passed in 2.20s ============================== ``` Before/after at the real consumer (`import lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm`, the exact failure point of #52614): | | without this shim | with this shim | |---|---|---| | lm-format-enforcer 0.11.3 (pinned) | `ImportError` at its line 4 (`vllm.transformers_utils.tokenizer`) | passes the vLLM import; then hits the known transformers-5 issue on LMFE's own side (see gap note) | | lm-format-enforcer @ main (has the unreleased transformers fix) | `ImportError` at line 4 | **import succeeds** | End-to-end through vLLM's production path (CPU, offline tokenizer): with this shim, `LMFormatEnforcerBackend` constructs, `compile_grammar` returns a grammar, and token allowlisting works (`accept_tokens('{') == True`, then narrows to `"`-leading tokens for the required property). Without the shim the backend construction raises `ImportError` at the tokenizer-data build (lazy-load trigger of `lmformatenforcer.integrations.vllm`). --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. (N/A — compatibility restore, no user-facing feature change) </details>

signal.title: [CI] Fix and extend PR/issue auto-labeling
signal.text: ## Purpose Auditing the labeling setup against the actual repo turned up rules that had stopped matching the code they were written for, plus issue-side labeling that covered only 6 of 62 labels. ### Rules that were missing real work - **`deepseek` missed the `vllm/models/` tree.** Newer models live in `vllm/models/<model>/` rather than `vllm/model_executor/models/`. The rule only knew the old location, so only the title match applied — **64 of 99 PRs** touching `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/` went unlabeled. Same gap for `deepseek_v32`. - **`speculative-decoding` missed the Model Runner V2 subtree.** `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/` has seen 94 PRs in 6 months, more than the original `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` at 81. This also folds `dflash` and `dspark` under the umbrella label, per review feedback that both are spec decoding techniques. ### Rules that could never fire Four conditions used `files=` (exact match) with regex syntax, or carried a doubled backslash that YAML passes through literally: ```yaml - files=^examples/features/speculative_decoding/ # never matches - files~=^\\.buildkite/intel_jobs/ # never matches ``` A further 13 conditions pointed at files that have since moved or been deleted — `harmony` moved to the Rust frontend, `pallas` is gone. Repointed where the code moved, removed where it is gone. ### Retired: `new-model` The rule fired on any PR touching a model file **and** `registry.py`. `registry.py` is edited for renames, aliases, refactors and removals, not just additions. Of the 25 most recent PRs carrying the label, 10 added a model. The rest included: - `[Model] Remove Ouro`, `[Model] Remove Plamo2`, `Remove PersimmonForCausalLM and FuyuForCausalLM` — PRs that **delete** models - `[model registry] some simple typos` - `[Perf] Optimize clamp to clamp_`, `[Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs`, `Revert "Blackwell decode optimizations"` Whether a new architecture was registered depends on what changed *inside* `registry.py`. Mergify matches file paths, not diff contents, so this rule cannot be made accurate — tightening the paths does not help. 111 open PRs currently carry the label. The label remains on issues, applied by the New Model template, where the requester states the intent explicitly. ### Rule that fired too often `nvidia` matched `requirements/cuda.txt`, so dependency bumps were tagged as NVIDIA backend work. Measured across 200 merged PRs, 17 carried the label and this was the one clear miss. ### New rules `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`, `DSv4`, `dflash`, `torch.compile`, `ray`, `vllm-ir`. ### Issue labeling Extended from 6 labels to 31. Terms match **titles only** by design: issue bodies carry pasted `collect_env` output that names unrelated hardware and libraries, which tags the reporter's environment rather than the topic. ### Guard against recurrence `tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py` fails when a file condition matches nothing in the tree, and runs via pre-commit when `mergify.yml` changes. It caught two bugs in this change while it was being written. ### Also removed: the New Model issue template `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/600-new-model.yml` is deleted. - Usage fell from 155 issues in 2025 to 30 in 2026, only 3 since July - It applied a label named `new model`, but the label is `new-model`. GitHub silently skips a label that does not exist, so requests went untagged from the March rename onward — five months, unnoticed - 292 of the 304 ever filed are closed - Model support arrives as planned work rather than as community requests `blank_issues_enabled` is `false`, so model requests route to Feature Request. **Nothing applies `new-model` after this change.** The label is left in place so it stays on the 917 PRs and 304 issues carrying it; deleting the label itself is a separate call. ## Before merging **The five new labels must be created first** — `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`. Mergify errors on a label that does not exist. Two related items a PR cannot do: - `mrv1-only`'s description currently reads "apply only to Model Runner V2 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)" — says V2 twice. - `DSv4` has a rule here mirroring the `kimi`/`k3` split, but whether to keep it as a distinct label is a maintainer call. ## Test Plan Rules were validated against the real file tree and against real issues and PRs, rather than by inspection. ```bash # every file condition in mergify.yml matches at least one tracked file python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run check-label-rules --files .github/mergify.yml pre-commit run ruff-check --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run ruff-format --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py ``` ## Test Result ``` tracked files: 6430 rules: 44 file conditions matching >=1 file: 154 file conditions matching NOTHING: 0 Check auto-label rules still match real files............................Passed ruff check...............................................................Passed ruff format..............................................................Passed ``` Negative test: injecting a condition pointing at a nonexistent path makes the check exit 1 and name the offending rule. New rules were spot-checked against the tree — `glm` matches 21 files and correctly ignores `midashenglm.py`, which contains the substring "glm" but is an unrelated model. Issue rules were replayed over 600 real issues: 43% now receive at least one label, and the existing rules agreed with hand-applied labels (`kimi` 35 fires / 31 already labeled, `rocm` 34 / 33, `k3` 27 / 26). No model evaluation is included because this change touches only CI labeling configuration. It does not affect inference, model output, accuracy, or serving. ## Note on AI assistance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to audit the existing rules, measure PR and issue volumes, and draft these changes. Every measurement quoted above is reproducible with the commands shown. I have reviewed each changed line.

signal.title: [Core] Remove is_ec_consumer check to enable correct batch queue sampling in standalone v1
signal.text: ### Title `fix(engine): remove is_ec_consumer check to enable correct batch queue sampling in standalone v1` ### Description Fixes a bug in the `EngineCore` batch queue where standard engine configurations (e.g., `is_ec_consumer=False`) would silently skip token sampling. By unconditionally setting: _`model_executed = scheduler_output.total_num_scheduled_tokens > 0`_ we eliminate the `is_ec_consumer` restriction, ensuring proper behavior for non-disaggregated standard generations (such as TPUs running standard workloads where inference and sampling stages are disjointed). ### AI Assistance (Required by `AGENTS.md`) - **AI Tools Used:** Jetski ### Non-Duplication No open duplicate PRs were found via: - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "batch queue in:body"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "is_ec_consumer"` ### Test/Eval Commands - `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -v` - Passed without `CUDA` exceptions (x86 run logic validations passed). ### Model Evaluation This PR strictly modifies internal sequencing parameters for inference pipeline scheduling. It does not manipulate numeric model outputs.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Redact api_key in non-default args log
signal.text: ## What The API server startup log prints all non-default arguments verbatim: ``` INFO ... [api_utils.py:273] non-default args: {'model_tag': 'org/model', 'api_key': 'sk-re…-123', ...} ``` So `--api-key` / `VLLM_API_KEY` lands in plain text in container and host logs. Anyone with log read access (`docker logs`, host filesystem, log shippers) recovers the API key from a single startup line. This redacts the `api_key` value to `***` in that log, keeping the field name so operators can still tell a key was configured. Only the logging path is touched; `get_non_default_args()` and the `--args-json` handoff to the Rust frontend are unchanged (the frontend stores keys as hashes). ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Searched open PRs/issues for `api_key redact`, `api_key mask`, `api_key leak` in title/body: no open PR or issue addresses this log line. ## Test commands run and results ``` ruff check vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py # All checks passed ruff format --check vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py # already formatted pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py -v # 14 passed (11 pre-existing + 3 new redaction tests) ``` ## AI-assisted This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The change is small and self-contained; please flag if the approach looks off. --- The API key was only ever logged, never sent anywhere — so the leak is free real estate for anyone reading logs. I've fixed mine by rotating; you're on your own.

signal.title: [ROCm][AMD][Installation] add LMCache kv-connector installation and runtime packages to docker image
signal.text: ## Purpose Ship the LMCache KV connector in the ROCm image so it works out of the box. Note: vLLM's CUDA `docker/Dockerfile` installs LMCache when `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`, and the release pipeline sets that for every published `vllm/vllm-openai` tag. docker/Dockerfile.rocm never referenced that arg, so vllm/vllm-openai-rocm ships without LMCache and users must build and install it themselves. This adds it so the ROCm release pipeline can enable it the same way. ### What this does - Adds a `build_lmcache` stage that obtains the wheel one of two ways, mirroring the CUDA path (`docker/Dockerfile` tries a prebuilt wheel first and falls back to a source build): 1. **Published ROCm wheel.** LMCache tags ROCm builds on GitHub Releases (`v0.5.3-rocm`), which PyPI does not carry. When the effective arch set is covered by that wheel it is downloaded — no clone, no compile. This is what the release build does. `--no-index` is deliberate: with a plain `--extra-index-url`, pip silently falls back to the **CUDA** wheel on PyPI. 2. **Source build.** A wider arch set falls back to compiling for HIP (`BUILD_WITH_HIP=1`, `CXX=hipcc`, `TORCH_DONT_CHECK_COMPILER_ABI=1`), so coverage is never silently narrowed. PyPI remains CUDA-only and ships no sdist for `>=0.4`, so `--no-binary` cannot force a HIP build — hence a source path is still required. - **Architecture selection.** The image's `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` is inherited, minus the consumer archs vLLM itself strips for its own wheel (`Dockerfile.rocm_base`), then intersected with the archs LMCache publishes ROCm wheels for. Anything dropped is named in the build log, and a set with no supported arch fails the build rather than shipping an unusable connector. On the release base this resolves to `gfx942;gfx950` — MI300X/MI325X and MI350X/MI355X. **`gfx90a` (MI200) is not covered.** vLLM builds for it, LMCache publishes no ROCm wheel for it. Rather than ship non-runnable device code, it is skipped and logged. To build it from source instead: `--build-arg LMCACHE_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950"`. - The wheel is bind-mounted for install while its `sha256` digest is `COPY`d, so a changed `LMCACHE_REF` or arch set invalidates the install layer instead of reusing a stale wheel — without committing the 7.8 MB wheel blob to a layer. - The install is placed **before** the vLLM wheel install, so vLLM source changes do not invalidate this otherwise stable connector layer. - The build asserts the wheel actually carries code objects for every requested arch, rather than only that some `.so` exists. - The source build opts into the sccache HIP wrappers when `USE_SCCACHE=1` (the contract documented in `Dockerfile.rocm_base`) and shares the ccache mount. - Installs the wheel with `--no-deps` plus four runtime packages. - `sortedcontainers` — hard requirement; without it `import lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector` fails outright. - `opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus` — `lmcache server` calls `init_observability()` unconditionally, which imports `PrometheusMetricReader` (`mp_observability/otel_init.py:96`). Omitting it builds fine but the server dies at startup. - `cupy-rocm-7-0` — GPU cache-registration path. - `aiofile` — local-disk storage tier. `--no-deps` is required, not a convenience. The published ROCm wheel declares `numpy<=2.2.6`, `opentelemetry-api<=1.40.0` and `opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus<=0.61b0`. The numpy ceiling is unsatisfiable — vLLM requires 2.3.5 — so resolving it would downgrade vLLM's own dependency. The two OpenTelemetry ceilings are upper bounds rather than known breakages; the image runs 1.44.0/0.65b0 and `lmcache server` starts and serves through `init_observability()` on those versions (see Test Result 2). Worth raising upstream so the declared ranges match what is tested. - Gates everything behind `INSTALL_LMCACHE`, defaulting to off. ### Build-arg selection `INSTALL_LMCACHE` is an independent boolean rather than being derived from an umbrella arg, so it is not an input to the cache key of unrelated stages. The release pipeline sets it explicitly. | Build args | Result | | --- | --- | | *(none)* | nothing installed (default) | | `INSTALL_LMCACHE=true` | LMCache installed | A boolean rather than a list because the build stage is selected via `FROM <stage>_${ARG}`, which needs the value in the stage name. With a list the stage would run on every build and be discarded. Arch lists (`LMCACHE_ROCM_ARCH`, `LMCACHE_SUPPORTED_ARCHS`, `LMCACHE_PREBUILT_ARCHS`) use `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`-style `;` separators; space and `,` forms are normalised so a mismatched separator cannot silently drop archs. ## Test Plan ```bash # (1) release default — inherits the base arch set, resolves to gfx942;gfx950 docker buildx build -f docker/Dockerfile.rocm --target vllm-openai \ --build-arg INSTALL_LMCACHE=true \ -t vllm-rocm-lmcache:release --load . # (2) source-build path — explicit arch set wider than the published wheel docker buildx build -f docker/Dockerfile.rocm --target vllm-openai \ --build-arg INSTALL_LMCACHE=true \ --build-arg LMCACHE_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950" \ -t vllm-rocm-lmcache:src --load . # (3) start the LMCache server from the image, installing nothing docker run --rm --network host --ipc host \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video \ -e LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906 --entrypoint bash vllm-rocm-lmcache:release -c ' lmcache server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5555 \ --http-host 127.0.0.1 --http-port 8080 \ --l1-size-gb "$LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB" --l1-init-size-gb 20 \ --l1-read-ttl-seconds 7200 --chunk-size 1536 --max-workers 8 \ --eviction-trigger-watermark 0.85 --eviction-ratio 0.10 \ --eviction-policy LRU' ``` ## Test Result Built and verified on **8x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.11**. **(1) Arch selection and both wheel paths.** The release default inherits the base's nine architectures and resolves them down, taking the published wheel: ``` [LMCACHE] not supported upstream, skipping: gfx90a [LMCACHE] effective PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH: gfx942;gfx950 [LMCACHE] using published ROCm wheel ``` An explicit wider set falls back to a source build: ``` [LMCACHE] effective PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH: gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950 [LMCACHE] building from source for gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950 ``` | | published wheel | source build | | --- | --- | --- | | wheel | `lmcache-0.5.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl` | `...-linux_x86_64.whl` | | stage time | ~1.3 s (download) | full hipcc compile | | GPU archs in `c_ops` | `gfx942`, `gfx950` | `gfx90a`, `gfx942`, `gfx950` | | `DT_NEEDED` | `libamdhip64` — **no CUDA libs** | same | | digest check | `...whl: OK` | `...whl: OK` | The arch assertion was negative-tested: forcing the published wheel to be selected for a `gfx90a` build fails the build with `wheel has no code objects for: gfx90a` (exit 1, nothing exported). All three separator forms (`;`, `,`, space) resolve identically. **(2) LMCache server starts out of the box**, nothing installed at runtime: ``` zmq 5555 -> accepting http 8080 -> HTTP 200 ``` Startup log shows shm capacity checked against the L1 request, L1 + L2 eviction controllers started, SessionManager cleanup thread, DeviceHostFuncDispatcher, mp-worker-reaper, and an 8-slot affinity pool matching `--max-workers 8`. This exercises `init_observability()` on opentelemetry 1.44.0 / exporter 0.65b0. **(3) No dependency downgrades** — the reason for `--no-deps`: | Package | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | numpy | 2.3.5 | 2.3.5 | | transformers | 5.14.1 | 5.14.1 | | opentelemetry-api / sdk | 1.44.0 | 1.44.0 | | opentelemetry-semantic-conventions | 0.65b0 | 0.65b0 | Added: `lmcache 0.5.3`, `sortedcontainers 2.4.0`, `aiofile 3.12.3`, `cupy-rocm-7-0 14.1.1`, `opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus 0.65b0`. Unchanged after moving the install ahead of the vLLM wheel. **(4) Connectors register**: `['LMCacheConnectorV1', 'LMCacheMPConnector']`. **(5) Layer and cache behaviour.** - The wheel no longer lands in a layer: `docker history` shows the LMCache install layer at **118 B** (the digest) rather than 7.82 MB. - Cache correctness verified against the failure it prevents: build a wheel, rebuild unchanged (layers cached), then change the wheel content — the install layer re-runs and picks up the new wheel. - With `INSTALL_LMCACHE=false` the stage is pruned entirely (`--target export_lmcache` produces empty output — no clone, no download, no compile). (6) Image size: 42.00 → 42.92 GB, +921 MB (+2.19%) — ~366 MB of that is CuPy, required by the GPU cache-registration path; the compiled extension is <8 MB. AI-assisted. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Do not use Dense MHA for GLM-5.2
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix incorrect short-prefill dispatch in the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 attention wrapper. The generic sparse-MLA metadata path may select dense MHA when a prefill's sequence length is at most `index_topk`. It then allows the sparse indexer to skip top-k scoring. `DeepseekV32Attention`, however, only invokes `forward_mqa`; it does not execute the dense-MHA backend. For a pure prefill above the backend's decode-like threshold, MQA therefore consumed the cleared all-`-1` top-k buffer and GLM-5.2 output degenerated into repeated tokens. This change adds a model-layer dense-prefill capability in addition to the backend capability. The NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 wrapper declares that it is MQA-only, so sparse MLA keeps its prefill on top-k MQA and the indexer does not advertise the dense-MHA scoring skip. This does not duplicate the open related work: - #51395 disables dense prefill only for the SM120 sparse-MLA backend. - #52046 adds a dense branch for the PCP path; the reproduced failure is the non-PCP SM100 path. - #49790 routes DSA architectures to the NVIDIA implementation but does not resolve this dispatch mismatch. Issue #46715 reports a different GLM-5.1 failure at a 65,536-token scheduler budget and multi-thousand-token prompts on the registered model path. ## Test Plan ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py ``` Real-model validation uses `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, the explicit NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 class override, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, eager execution, FP32 indexer logits, GVR disabled, and FlashInfer autotuning disabled. It serially probes the 128/129-token routing boundary without setting `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true`. ## Test Result - Focused pytest: `7 passed`. - Pre-commit on all three changed files: all hooks passed. - `compileall` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Before this change, the real model passed through 127 actual prompt tokens and failed at 129 and every tested larger prompt through 1,001 tokens. Adding only `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true` made all 19 boundary cases pass, causally confirming the routing mismatch. - Patched real-model result: all 19/19 cases passed exact retrieval without the force-MQA workaround, spanning 97, 101, 122, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 162, 191, 192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 257, 301, 502, and 1,001 actual prompt tokens. AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, test, and draft this change. The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend the change end-to-end before marking the PR ready for review. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan includes exact commands. - [x] Unit and real-model results are reported. - [x] Related open work was checked for duplication. </details>

signal.title: [Security] Include cache_salt in HF3FS external cache keys
signal.text: ## Summary HF3FS external cache keys were derived from token IDs alone and omitted the per-request `cache_salt`. Engines sharing an HF3FS metadata service could therefore alias the same exact prefix across different salts and expose cached-prefix membership through hit observability. This change: - carries `cache_salt` through scheduler state and HF3FS worker metadata; - injects the salt into the first full-block hash so chained descendant hashes remain isolated; - uses the salted keys consistently for metadata lookup, save, and load; and - adds CPU-only production-path tests for A-hit/B-miss isolation and save/load key agreement.
signal.author: infinityscroll

signal.title: [ROCm][DSpark][DCP] Support decode context parallelism for Kimi-K3 DSpark
signal.text: ## Purpose Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Kimi-K3 with the DSpark drafter on ROCm. Three things stood in the way: 1. **Hybrid KV cache grouping was not drafter-invariant.** The draft adds an MLA-only attention type with far fewer layers than the target, and group size was `min(bucket_sizes)`, so that small bucket over-split the target's mamba layers. It also made an engine holding the drafter group its mamba layers differently from one without it, which breaks KV transfer in PD-disaggregated serving. 2. **The draft KV cache group cannot be DCP-sharded.** The draft attends over the whole sequence and discards its decode LSE, so it needs replicated KV while the target stays sharded. 3. **A multi-token verify had no correct decode path under DCP.** The decode has to return an LSE for the merge, and the verify's causal window has to be taken in global positions rather than per-rank ones. ### Changes **Grouping** — exclude draft-only buckets, identified by the existing `non_causal_multi_token_decode` spec flag, when choosing the group size. The draft bucket is then padded up to the target's group size instead of setting it; for K3 DSpark that is the 19 padding layers vLLM already logs, which is the deliberate trade for keeping the target's grouping stable. Models without a drafter are unaffected because no spec carries the flag. **Replicated draft group** — whole-sequence block tables, an unsharded slot mapping so every rank writes the full sequence, `dcp_world_size=1` metadata, and an undivided capacity estimate. `MultiHeadLatentAttention` accepts DCP for these groups and pins their impl to `dcp_world_size=1`; the config-time guard that rejected the combination is removed. **Target decode LSE** — single-token decode runs through aiter gluon with `return_lse=True` so per-rank partials can be merged. `AiterMLAImpl` declares `can_return_lse_for_decode` and keeps queries in bf16 on the gluon path. **Multi-token verify** — the verify block is flattened onto per-row gluon decodes, so each row carries its own KV range and the kernel applies no causal tail of its own. Deriving those ranges by subtracting the causal offset from a request's length is wrong under DCP: the KV cache is sharded round-robin, so the tokens a row drops sit on `qlen - 1 - row` different ranks, while the subtraction takes one from every rank. The window is now counted in global positions and mapped onto the rank's shard with the shared `get_dcp_local_seq_lens`, evaluated per row instead of once per request. Without DCP the shard is the whole sequence and this reduces to the previous expression. The flatten also returns the per-row LSE the merge needs, and is gated on the head count gluon accepts rather than on being below 16: ROCm/aiter#4412 tiles the head range up to 96, which is what TP8 x DCP8 gathers. The bound is read off the wrapper, so an aiter without it keeps the previous behaviour and the verify is served as a prefill. Also included: two K3 GDN decode-kernel fixes that surface under spec decode — a strided `decode_conv_indices` view needs compaction, and `state_indices` only needs unit stride when `numel > 1`. ## Test Plan Single node, 8x MI355X, `Kimi-K3` (mxfp4) + `Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft, TP=8, native 1M context, prefix caching on, spec decode on (`num_speculative_tokens=2`, `method=dspark`, draft `attention_backend=TRITON_MLA`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `rejection_sample_method=block`). Baseline is TP=8 without DCP; the DCP runs add `--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1` and are otherwise byte-identical. 1. **GSM8K**, 200 items 5-shot via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, `temperature=0`, `seed=42`, `max_tokens=256`, concurrency 8. Run with an fp8 KV cache, where the verify is served as a prefill, and with a bf16 KV cache, where it reaches the gluon flatten this PR adds. 2. **Per-row window** — a brute-force check of the flattened window against a direct round-robin simulation over 3600 configurations of (`seq_len`, `qlen`, `dcp_size`, `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`, `rank`). ## Test Result The three rows below are a matched set from the same build, differing only in `decode_context_parallel_size` and `--kv-cache-dtype`. ### Accuracy, draft acceptance and KV capacity - GSM8K, 200 items 5-shot | Config | Accuracy | Invalid | Mean acceptance length | GPU KV cache | |---|---|---|---|---| | TP8 (dcp=1), fp8 KV | 0.990 | 0.005 | 2.82 | 1,289,232 tokens | | DCP=8, fp8 KV, verify as prefill | 0.990 | 0.005 | 2.80 | 1,811,564 tokens | | DCP=8, bf16 KV, verify on the gluon flatten | 0.995 | 0.005 | 2.84 | 1,726,190 tokens | The window fix is what makes the third row match the baseline: with the per-rank subtraction it scores 0.955 at the same settings, because every rank reads a slightly different wrong window. Acceptance length tracks the baseline's 2.82 throughout, so replicating the draft group is not losing proposals. Replicating only that group also preserves the target's sharding benefit: DCP=8 holds 40.6% more KV than TP8 at the same fp8 cache dtype. ### Per-row window Over 3600 configurations the per-row window matches a direct round-robin simulation exactly, while the per-rank subtraction it replaces differs in 1787 of them. Summing each row's length over all ranks reproduces the global visible count in every case, so no token is dropped or counted twice. For `dcp=8`, `interleave=1`, `qlen=3`, `seq_len=1000`, the correct per-row lengths are `[125, 125, 125]` on ranks 0-5, `[124, 125, 125]` on rank 6 and `[124, 124, 125]` on rank 7; the subtraction gave `[123, 124, 125]` on every rank. Before this PR, `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` with the DSpark drafter was rejected at config time.

signal.title: [Roadmap] Rust Frontend Feature Parity
signal.text: ## Motivation The Rust frontend has landed in the vLLM repository as a drop-in alternative to the Python API server process. It is enabled through `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and uses the existing vLLM engine/core boundary. The Rust frontend is still experimental and not yet feature-complete relative to the Python frontend. This issue tracks the roadmap for the remaining gaps in feature parity and provides community contributors with a place to find scoped work. This roadmap prioritizes user value and the Rust frontend's architectural goals over blanket 1:1 parity with the Python frontend. In particular, we may skip: - Features / endpoints / options that are not commonly used in production - Options that mainly reflect Python frontend implementation details or Python-side workarounds - Features whose Python implementation has accumulated enough complexity that redesigning or removing them may be better than porting them directly **For items marked with 🧭:** Please start with a design discussion before implementation, covering the intended API/architecture, co-design with the engine if needed, and the testing plan. Related context: - Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40846 - Integration PRs * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40848 * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43283 ## Current status - [x] Rust code lives in the main vLLM repository under `rust/` - [x] `vllm-rs` integrates with `vllm serve` as a Python-supervised frontend subprocess - [x] Core `/v1/chat/completions` support (streaming & non-streaming) - [x] Core `/v1/completions` support (streaming & non-streaming) - [x] Tool calling and reasoning output support for several key model families - [x] Commonly used OpenAI-compatible sampling options - [x] Image-only multimodal chat path for registered image processor/model specs - [x] Multi-engine internal load balancing with scheduler-stat-aware routing - [x] Admin and operational routes: health, load, version, metrics, reset-cache, sleep/wake - [x] Mock-engine and HTTP integration-test infrastructure for Rust frontend development ## Roadmap ### Distributed serving and large-scale control plane - [x] External DP load-balancing mode: support the Python-style shape where each API server connects to one DP rank 🧭 - [x] Hybrid DP load-balancing mode: support per-node internal LB plus cross-node external LB 🧭 - [ ] Elastic EP support: implement `/scale_elastic_ep`, `/is_scaling_elastic_ep`, request draining, and scaling-state rejection behavior 🧭 ### Additional APIs - [ ] Anthropic Messages API: `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` 🧭 - [ ] Non-stateful Responses API: start with `POST /v1/responses` without requiring durable response storage 🧭 - [ ] Pooling / embedding APIs: `/v1/embeddings`, `/pooling`, `/classify`, `/score`, `/v1/score`, `/rerank`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v2/rerank` 🧭 - [ ] Speech-to-text APIs: `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` 🧭 - [ ] Realtime API: WebSocket `/v1/realtime` 🧭 - [ ] Generative scoring API: `/generative_scoring` - [x] Tokenization APIs: `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, and `/tokenizer_info` - [ ] Extend the Rust gRPC interface to cover embeddings and other non-generation outputs 🧭 ### Request compatibility and validation - [ ] Audit request parameter coverage and validation, making unsupported features fail clearly - [x] `stream_options.continuous_usage_stats` - [ ] `n > 1` for chat completions and completions 🧭 - [ ] Beam search via the existing `use_beam_search` request parameter, including `length_penalty` - [ ] `truncate_prompt_tokens` - [x] `thinking_token_budget` - [x] `include_reasoning=false` - [ ] `repetition_detection` - [x] `echo` behavior for token-ID completions prompts - [x] `max_tokens=0` prompt-only behavior - [x] Request ID handling in requests and responses - [ ] Tracing 🧭 ### Production readiness - [x] TLS / SSL support: `--ssl-keyfile`, `--ssl-certfile`, and related serving arguments - [x] API key authentication: `--api-key` / `VLLM_API_KEY` - [x] CORS middleware and CLI argument parity - [ ] Reverse-proxy `--root-path` support - [x] `/server_info` route parity - [ ] Logging argument parity: max log length, output logging, delta logging, access-log exclusions, and log-level controls ### LoRA adapter support - [x] Startup LoRA adapter loading through `--lora-modules` - [x] Runtime adapter loading/unloading: `/v1/load_lora_adapter` and `/v1/unload_lora_adapter` - [x] Multiple-adapter request routing and validation ### Multimodal support - [x] `image_url` chat content path for the currently registered image model specs - [ ] Image embedding inputs - [ ] Audio inputs and audio embedding inputs 🧭 - [ ] Video inputs and video chunk inputs 🧭 - [ ] `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` - [ ] Broader model-family coverage beyond the current image-only processor registry 🧭 ### RL / admin / lifecycle APIs - [x] `/pause`, `/resume`, and `/is_paused` - [x] `/abort_requests` - [ ] `/update_weights` and `/init_weight_transfer_engine` - [x] `/get_world_size` ### Tool and reasoning parser parity - [x] `parallel_tool_calls` - [x] Tool-choice constraints: `required` and named function 🧭 - [ ] Tool-choice constraints: `allowed_tools` 🧭 - [ ] Add missing tool and reasoning parsers for currently unsupported Python parser names. - [ ] Add model-family roundtrip fixtures for newly added parsers Parser work should prioritize production use and key model families over 100% parity. Additionally, the Rust frontend has a redesigned tool and reasoning parser architecture for more efficient, robust, and maintainable parsing, so prefer adapting the current Rust design over line-by-line Python ports. <details> <summary>Full parser parity checklist</summary> #### Tool parsers - [ ] `apertus` - [ ] `cohere_command3` - [ ] `cohere_command4` - [ ] `ernie45` - [ ] `functiongemma` - [ ] `gigachat3` - [ ] `granite` - [ ] `granite-20b-fc` - [x] `granite4` - [ ] `hunyuan_a13b` - [x] `internlm` - [ ] `jamba` - [ ] `lfm2` - [ ] `llama4_pythonic` 🧭 - [ ] `longcat` - [ ] `mimo` - [x] `minimax` - [x] `minimax_m2` - [x] `minimax_m3` - [ ] `minicpm5` - [ ] `olmo3` - [x] `phi4_mini_json` - [ ] `poolside_v1` - [ ] `pythonic` 🧭 - [ ] `seed_oss` - [ ] `step3` - [ ] `step3p5` - [ ] `xlam` #### Reasoning parsers - [ ] `cohere_command3` - [ ] `cohere_command4` - [ ] `ernie45` - [ ] `granite` - [ ] `holo2` - [ ] `hunyuan_a13b` - [ ] `hy_v3` - [ ] `mimo` - [ ] `minimax_m2_append_think` - [ ] `mistral` - [ ] `olmo3` - [ ] `poolside_v1` - [x] `seed_oss` - [x] `step3p5` </details> ## Testing and compatibility infrastructure - [ ] Improve E2E coverage through real `vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` on CI - [ ] Documentation for building, testing, and contributing to the Rust frontend

signal.title: [Perf] Avoid FlashInfer MLA prefill GPU sync
signal.text: ## Purpose Avoid a GPU-to-CPU synchronization in FlashInfer MLA prefill planning. FlashInfer's ragged prefill planner needs `qo_indptr` on the host and otherwise calls `.to("cpu")` on the CUDA `query_start_loc` tensor. Thread the existing host-side prefill query offsets through `MLACommonPrefillMetadata` and pass them as `qo_indptr`. This keeps the values and planner behavior unchanged while avoiding the device-to-host copy and its synchronization. This does not duplicate an existing PR. Searches for `FlashInfer MLA qo_indptr sync` and `GPU CPU sync FlashInfer prefill` found no matching fix. #51540 addresses a different synchronization in KDA/FLA chunk-index construction. AI assistance was used to trace the synchronization, implement the change, and prepare tests. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the change. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py \ vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \ vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py ``` ## Test Result - Nearby MLA chunk tests: **11 passed**. - Kimi-K3 CUDA-only MLA tests: **9 skipped** because no CUDA device is available locally. - All pre-commit hooks on changed files: **passed**. - Model evaluations were not run because this changes only the device placement of planner metadata, not model execution or output values.

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Add Olmo3 tool parser
signal.text: ## Purpose Add the Olmo3 tool parser to the experimental Rust frontend. - Parses `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` blocks containing newline-separated Python-style calls. - Supports parallel calls, nested dict/list/tuple literals, Python and JSON boolean/null literals, parameterless calls, and arbitrary stream chunk boundaries. - Preserves visible text before and after tool calls in event order. - Falls back to ordinary text for incomplete or unsupported tool-call expressions instead of panicking. - Registers the `olmo3` parser and automatic `olmo-3` / `olmo3` model matchers. - Adds a real `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` tokenizer/template roundtrip fixture. Tracks the Olmo3 tool-parser item in #44280. ### Duplicate-work check Before implementation and again before opening this PR, I checked: - comments on #44280; - open PRs referencing #44280; - open PR searches for `olmo3 rust tool parser` and related Rust frontend keywords. I found no open PR implementing the Olmo3 Rust tool parser. #47345 is an Olmo3 reasoning-parser PR and does not overlap this change. ### AI assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the existing parser architecture, implement the Rust changes, and prepare tests. The submitting human will review every changed line and must be able to explain and maintain the implementation before this PR is marked ready for review. ## Test Plan ```bash cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip roundtrip_olmo3 cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings pre-commit run --files \ rust/Cargo.lock rust/Cargo.toml rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs \ rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/mod.rs rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/tests.rs \ rust/src/chat/tests/roundtrip.rs rust/src/parser/Cargo.toml \ rust/src/parser/src/tool/mod.rs rust/src/parser/src/tool/olmo3.rs ``` The roundtrip test uses cached tokenizer/template files from the official `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` repository; no model weights or GPU are required. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not alter model execution or generated outputs. A full-model serving regression was performed to validate parser integration, as recorded below. ## Test Result - `vllm-parser`: 421 passed. - `vllm-chat` library: 265 passed. - Olmo3 real model-family roundtrip: 1 passed. - Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks: passed. ## Full-model serving regression Downloaded and served the complete `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` checkpoint (13.59 GiB) on the CPU backend with the locally built PR Rust binary, `--tool-call-parser olmo3`, and the real model tokenizer/chat template. - `/health` and `/v1/models`: passed. - Plain chat: returned exactly `hello`. - Required single tool: returned one `get_weather` call with `{"city":"Shanghai"}` and `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`. - Required parallel tools: returned ordered Shanghai and Beijing calls. - Text before tool call: preserved `content = "I will check."` before the parsed tool call. - Streaming parallel tools: six SSE chunks reconstructed into two complete ordered calls and ended with `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`.

signal.title: fix(security): default multimodal item limit to 999 for unconfigured modalities
signal.text: The Rust frontend treated modalities absent from --limit-mm-per-prompt as unlimited, diverging from Python's default of 999. This allowed a single request within the 32 MiB body limit to trigger unbounded media-task fan-out and OOM before inference. Apply a DEFAULT_MM_ITEMS_PER_PROMPT of 999 as a fallback when no explicit count is configured, matching the Python frontend behavior and blocking the demonstrated pre-inference allocation path.

signal.title: [Bug]: [V1] `prompt_tokens_details` always `null` in API response despite `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` (14+ months, incomplete fix in PR #18149)
signal.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> - **vLLM version**: v0.22.1rc1.dev166+gd0975a4b5 (V1 engine, default) - **Launch flags**: `--enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details` - **Also confirmed broken on**: v0.22.1rc1 nightly (2026-06-01) per [forum report](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/possible-bug-enable-prompt-tokens-details-not-working/2690) </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary `usage.prompt_tokens_details` is **always `null`** in the OpenAI-compatible API response on V1 engine, even with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and `--enable-prefix-caching` enabled. This was previously reported in #16162 (2025-04) and #18062 (2025-05), and supposedly fixed by PR #18149 (merged 2025-05-23). However, **the fix is incomplete** — it only wired `num_cached_tokens` through the scheduler/output processor, but never mapped it to `prompt_tokens_details` in the OpenAI API serving layer. This bug has been open for **14+ months** and is confirmed still broken on the latest nightly. ### Prior reports confirming this bug | Reference | Date | Version | Status | |---|---|---|---| | #16162 | 2025-04-07 | V1 dev | Closed (marked fixed) | | #18062 | 2025-05-13 | V1 master | Closed by PR #18149 | | PR #18149 | 2025-05-23 | — | Merged (incomplete fix) | | [Forum report](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/possible-bug-enable-prompt-tokens-details-not-working/2690) | 2026-06-02 | v0.22.1rc1 nightly | Still broken | | #43370 | 2026-05-21 | V1 disaggregated | Separate but related | ### Root cause PR #18149 modified the **engine-internal** path: ``` vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py ✅ num_cached_tokens populated vllm/v1/engine/__init__.py ✅ propagated in EngineCoreOutput vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py ✅ stored in RequestOutput vllm/v1/request.py ✅ field added ``` But the **API server response path** was never updated: ``` [OutputProcessor] num_cached_tokens = N ✅ ↓ [OpenAI Serving Layer → UsageInfo] ❌ not mapped ↓ [API JSON Response] ❌ prompt_tokens_details: null ``` The OpenAI serving layer (e.g. `vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py` or the `UsageInfo` builder) does not read `num_cached_tokens` from `RequestOutput` and does not populate `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. ### Reproduction **Server:** ```bash vllm serve facebook/opt-125m \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details ``` **Client — send the same request twice (2nd should cache-hit):** ```bash # Run this twice curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "facebook/opt-125m", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant. Please provide detailed and comprehensive answers to all questions. This is padding to ensure enough tokens for prefix caching to activate on the second request."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"} ], "max_tokens": 20 }' | jq '.usage' ``` **Actual (all V1 versions):** ```json { "prompt_tokens": 48, "total_tokens": 68, "completion_tokens": 20, "prompt_tokens_details": null } ``` **Expected (2nd request):** ```json { "prompt_tokens": 48, "total_tokens": 68, "completion_tokens": 20, "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 32 } } ``` Note: `/metrics` confirms prefix caching **is working internally** — only the API response field is missing: ``` vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total > 0 ``` V0 engine also returns `prompt_tokens_details` correctly (`VLLM_USE_V1=0`), confirming the gap is V1-specific. ### Suggested fix Map `RequestOutput.num_cached_tokens` → `UsageInfo.prompt_tokens_details` in the OpenAI serving layer: ```python # Likely location: vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py # or wherever UsageInfo is constructed from RequestOutput if self.enable_prompt_tokens_details and request_output.num_cached_tokens is not None: usage.prompt_tokens_details = PromptTokensDetails( cached_tokens=request_output.num_cached_tokens ) ``` ### Impact - **Observability**: No per-request cache efficiency tracking via standard API - **Proxy/cost tracking**: LiteLLM and similar proxies rely on `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` — `null` breaks cost attribution - **OpenAI API compatibility**: Violates the contract vLLM aims to fulfill - **Duration**: 14+ months since first report, all V1 versions affected ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Perf] Scale num_warps with tile size in Triton reshape-and-cache kernels
signal.text: ## Purpose Both CUDA launch sites in `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py` hardcode `num_warps = 16`, i.e. 512 threads, regardless of tile size. When the tile is smaller than that, the surplus warps hold thread slots without doing work, which limits how many blocks stay resident on an SM. `_reshape_cache_per_token_head` in the same file already derives the count from the shape — `min(16, max(1, head_size_padded // 32))` — as does the CUDA version of this operation (`dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_size, 512))`). This PR applies the same rule at the two remaining sites. Only the launch geometry changes; the kernels write the same bytes to the same slots. Tiles of 512 elements or more still get 16 warps, so the shapes the original benchmarks covered are unaffected. ROCm and XPU take a separate branch and are untouched. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k diffkv ``` The DiffKV kernel had no direct coverage. The new test checks against a PyTorch reference that key and value land in their own halves of the packed cache row, over three `(head_size_k, head_size_v)` pairs, three block sizes, two dtypes and both cache dtypes, and that padded tokens leave the cache untouched. ``` python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache_flash.py \ --implementation triton --mode cudagraph --num-heads 2 --head-size 64 ``` `--num-heads 8 --head-size 64` gives n = 512, where both arms have the identical launch config. That row is the control. ## Test Result All 18 tests passed on an A100, on both the patched and the unpatched kernel (18 more skip below SM89, where the Triton fp8 path is unsupported). Latency change on an A100-SXM4-80GB, median of 5 repetitions with the arms alternated, CUDA graph mode. Negative means the patch is faster. | config | 1024 tok | 4096 | 16384 | 65536 | |---|---|---|---|---| | n=512 (control) | −0.6% | +0.2% | +0.3% | −0.05% | | n=256 | −11.2% | −26.0% | −33.5% | −45.1% | | n=128 | −10.6% | −29.6% | −50.9% | −67.7% | | n=64 | −9.2% | −27.3% | −49.1% | −73.0% | | DiffKV 192/128 (MiMo-V2 shape) | −29.8% | −40.9% | −44.6% | −47.1% | | DiffKV 256/256 | −31.9% | −41.5% | −45.2% | −46.2% | Below ~1000 tokens there are fewer blocks than the GPU has SMs, so nothing overlaps and there is no effect. Above that the gain grows with the token count, because more blocks fit on each SM and more stores are in flight. This is kernel time, not end-to-end throughput. I ran the A/B three times across two A100 variants; the control stayed within 0.08% each time, and varying the DiffKV cache strides or slot pattern moved the result by less than 0.15 points. The kernels write the same bytes to the same slots, so I did not run accuracy evals. <details> <summary>DiffKV benchmark script</summary> ```python import random, time import torch from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash import ( triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv, ) NUM_HEADS, DK, DV, BLOCK, NUM_BLOCKS, ITERS = 8, 192, 128, 16, 8192, 200 def run(num_tokens): torch.manual_seed(42) random.seed(42) dev, dt = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 key = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DK, dtype=dt, device=dev) value = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DV, dtype=dt, device=dev) slots = random.sample(range(BLOCK * NUM_BLOCKS), num_tokens) slot_mapping = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.long, device=dev) # the backends pass a (B, H, N, C).transpose(1, 2) view kv_cache = torch.empty( NUM_BLOCKS, NUM_HEADS, BLOCK, DK + DV, dtype=dt, device=dev ).transpose(1, 2) k_scale = (key.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) v_scale = (value.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(graph): triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv( key, value, kv_cache, slot_mapping, "auto", k_scale, v_scale ) torch.cuda.synchronize() def timed(n): torch.cuda.synchronize() start = time.perf_counter() for _ in range(n): graph.replay() torch.cuda.synchronize() return (time.perf_counter() - start) / n timed(3) # warm-up return timed(ITERS) for n in [64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 65536]: print(f"{n:>7} {run(n) * 1e6:9.3f} us") ``` </details> --- **AI assistance disclosure** (per `AGENTS.md`): Developed with Claude Code. I reviewed and refined every line, and ran all tests. **Duplicate check**: I did not find any open or merged PR changing `num_warps` at either site. #46060 rewrites the capability check in both launch blocks of this file; if it lands first I will rebase. #47535 adds an opt-in CUDA DiffKV op and keeps Triton as the default, which is the path this PR speeds up.

signal.title: [Bug]: [ROCm] DeepSeek-V4 sparse indexer is a dead end on non-MI3xx GPUs, though working torch fallbacks exist in-tree
signal.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Abridged environment (key versions; 2-node cluster)</summary> ```text vLLM: 0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260808 PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0 Python: 3.14.4 ROCm: 7.14, RCCL 2.30.4 GPU: 2x AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU, gfx1151), 1 GPU per node Nodes: 2-node Ray cluster, TP=2, Thunderbolt interconnect (RCCL NET/Socket) Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8, fp8_ds_mla KV cache) AITER: built from source (ROCm/aiter @ main, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151); imports and JITs fine ``` Serve command: ```bash vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --distributed-executor-backend ray ``` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Three interacting gates currently make DeepSeek-V4 (and presumably any model using the DSA sparse indexer with `fp8_ds_mla`) impossible to run on ROCm GPUs other than MI3xx — while torch reference fallbacks for exactly this situation already exist in-tree, are wired with correct arguments, and work when made reachable (verified on a 2× gfx1151 cluster, now serving). **Gate 1 — the indexer requires AITER.** During the profiling forward pass, `sparse_attn_indexer.py::forward_hip` raises: ``` Sparse attention indexer ROCm path is only supported on AITER. Please enable aiter with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 ``` **Gate 2 — the advice in that error cannot work.** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is silently ignored on non-MI3xx because `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` hard-gates on platform: ```python def is_aiter_found_and_supported() -> bool: ... if current_platform.is_rocm() and IS_AITER_FOUND: from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx return on_mi3xx() return False ``` So the user is sent in a loop: the error demands an env var that the platform gate then discards, even with AITER installed and importable. **Gate 3 — the in-tree fallbacks are unreachable.** `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` contains `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` and `fp8_mqa_logits_torch`, and both dispatchers (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) already call them in their `else` branches when the AITER Triton module is unavailable. But reaching the dispatchers requires AITER enabled (gates 1–2), and with AITER enabled the module lookup always succeeds, so the AITER Triton kernels are always selected. On RDNA3/3.5 those AITER Triton kernels cannot compile regardless (no fp8 WMMA), so whitelisting the arch in gate 2 just moves the failure into Triton: ``` triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError o = tl.dot(q, k.T) ^ Unsupported lhs dtype fp8e4nv (aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py, deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1) ``` i.e. every path on this hardware terminates in an error one step before working fallback code. ### Reproduction 1. 2× gfx1151, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, serve command in the environment section → gate 1 error. 2. Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` → identical error (gate 2). 3. Whitelist gfx1151 in `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` → Triton `fp8e4nv` CompilationError in the AITER paged-MQA kernel (gate 3). ### Tested fix (cluster is serving with this) **a) `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`** — accept gfx1151 as AITER-capable: ```diff - from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx - - return on_mi3xx() + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx, on_gfx1151 + + return on_mi3xx() or on_gfx1151() ``` **b) `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — skip the AITER Triton module lookup on gfx1151 so the existing torch fallbacks run (same change in both dispatchers): ```diff - if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled(): + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151 + + # gfx1151: Triton cannot compile tl.dot with fp8e4nv inputs; skip the + # AITER Triton kernels so the torch reference fallback below is used. + if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151(): aiter_paged_mqa_logits_module = paged_mqa_logits_module() ``` ```diff + from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151 + aiter_mqa_logits_module = None - if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled(): + if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151(): aiter_mqa_logits_module = mqa_logits_module() ``` The prefill dispatcher (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) needs the same gate: its AITER kernel performs the same fp8 `tl.dot` and fails identically on the first real prefill if only the paged path is patched. A cleaner resolution than piling onto the arch whitelist is probably per-kernel capability gating: dispatchers select the AITER Triton kernel only on archs where it is known to compile (mi3xx / gfx942 / gfx950 — the gfx942 special case already exists in `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`), else torch fallback — and gate 1's error message should not recommend an env var that gate 2 ignores. Happy to turn this into a PR if maintainers agree on the preferred shape. Note: the sparse-attention Triton kernels in the same file are unaffected — they dequantize fp8→bf16 in-kernel before `tl.dot` and compile fine on gfx1151. ### Secondary finding: torch fallback vs FULL cudagraph capture Once reachable, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` is not capture-safe (`.item()` / data-dependent host loops), but `@eager_break_during_capture` intentionally runs ops inline when `forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL` (`compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`), so FULL capture crashes: ``` File ".../rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 290, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item()) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing (hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported) ``` If the fallbacks become officially reachable, the op should be treated as non-capturable when the torch path is active (or cudagraph disabled for it). We run with `--enforce-eager` (also required on this cluster: piecewise capture deadlocked in RCCL NET/Socket collectives; related to #32180). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
