As a result, TileLang mHC kernels such as mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang may be JIT-compiled during the first real inference workload, causing a significant latency spike or request timeout. Environment vLLM version: 0.25.0 Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, downloaded from Hugging Face and served from a local directory Architecture resolved by vLLM: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM model_type: deepseek_v4 Tensor parallel size: 8 KV cache dtype: fp8_ds_mla Device: NVIDIA CUDA trust_remote_code=False Server command: python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --max-model-len 65537 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --port 8001 Expected behavior During engine initialization, vLLM should run the explicit DeepSeek V4 mHC warmup and print logs similar to: Warming up DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang kernels for token sizes: [...] DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang warmup finished in ... seconds. The relevant TileLang mHC kernels should not be compiled during real inference. Actual behavior The mHC warmup logs never appear. The subsequent DeepSeek V4 sparse-MLA warmup does run on all TP workers: Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16. I added diagnostics immediately before the silent return in deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py. The result was: Skipping DSV4 mHC warmup: no matching layer; model_class=DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, model_type='deepseek_v4', candidates=[ ( 'DeepseekV4DecoderLayer', [ 'hc_attn_fn', 'hc_attn_scale', 'hc_attn_base', 'hc_ffn_fn', 'hc_ffn_scale', 'hc_ffn_base' ] ), ... ] Every decoder layer has the expected mHC parameters, but none has hc_pre or hc_post. Suspected root cause _find_first_mhc_layer() in deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py requires the following attributes: ( "hc_pre", "hc_post", "hc_attn_fn", "hc_attn_scale", "hc_attn_base", "hc_ffn_fn", "hc_ffn_scale", "hc_ffn_base", ) The warmup later invokes: layer_input, post_mix, comb_mix = layer.hc_pre(...) layer.hc_post(...) However, the NVIDIA DeepseekV4DecoderLayer does not define self.hc_pre or self.hc_post. Its forward() directly invokes module-level TileLang functions: mhc_pre_tilelang(...) mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang(...) mhc_post_tilelang(...) This mismatch is also visible in the current main branch: Warmup implementation:https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py NVIDIA decoder implementation:https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py The same mismatch appears in the v0.25.0 NVIDIA model implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.25.0/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py Because _find_first_mhc_layer() returns None, deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup() exits silently before its first informational log. Impact The intended mHC warmup is effectively disabled for this model path. TileLang kernels can therefore be compiled after the API server has started accepting production inference traffic. In my deployment, this results in latency spikes and can cause model-service request timeouts when an uncompiled mHC kernel is first encountered. Suggested fix Adapt _warmup_layer_mhc() to exercise the same functions used by DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward(): mhc_pre_tilelang mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang mhc_post_tilelang The warmup should pass the real normalization parameters as the inference path does: layer.attn_norm.weight.data layer.attn_norm.variance_epsilon layer.ffn_norm.weight.data layer.ffn_norm.variance_epsilon This is necessary to cover kernels such as: mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang Simply removing hc_pre and hc_post from the attribute check is not sufficient, because _warmup_layer_mhc() would then fail with an AttributeError when it tries to call those missing members. It may also be useful to log the reason whenever the warmup is skipped, rather than returning silently. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Own prepared B12x W4A16 weights
signal.text: ## Purpose Draft stacked PR for the vLLM half of the explicit FlashInfer B12x W4A16 prepared-weight lifecycle. Dependencies: - vLLM #43929 supplies the W4A16 B12x routing and wrapper configuration. - FlashInfer #4560 supplies `prepare_weights()` and `run_prepared()`. Because #43929 comes from another contributor's fork, GitHub cannot use its head branch as the base of an upstream vLLM PR. The current diff therefore temporarily contains the three #43929 commits not already absorbed by `main`. Reviewers should review only the top commit, `13fafd778c2e5e7d06435838df82d7bf85312464`. This branch will be rebased to a single commit after #43929 merges. The top commit makes `FlashInferB12xExperts` prepare W4A16 weights during `process_weights_after_loading()`, retain the caller-owned prepared object, reuse the checkpoint weight storage, and execute with `run_prepared()`. The W4A4 path keeps the existing `run()` behavior. This avoids relying on FlashInfer's process-global source-pointer cache and avoids retaining a second packed W1/W2 allocation. It addresses the ownership boundary described in #49031. This is not a duplicate of #43929, which establishes W4A16 routing, or #48698, which shares B12x workspace across layers. No other open PR using `run_prepared()` in vLLM was found. AI assistance was used to implement, test, and prepare this PR. The submitter is responsible for reviewing the final diff before this Draft is marked ready. ## Test Plan 1. Install FlashInfer from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4560. 2. Run the SM120 B12x SiLU and ReLU2 tests for both W4A4 and W4A16. 3. Verify that prepared W4A16 W1/W2 tensors retain the source `data_ptr()` values when `reuse_input_storage=True`. 4. Load `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` with the FlashInfer B12x backend on SM120, capture a PIECEWISE CUDA Graph, and generate a deterministic response. 5. Run pre-commit on the full rebased stack relative to `main`. Commands used: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_b12x_moe.py E2E_CUDAGRAPH=1 .venv/bin/python /workspace/run_vllm_w4a16_e2e.py uvx pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD ``` ## Test Result - Target hardware: one NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell, 48 GiB, SM120. - Targeted B12x SiLU and ReLU2 tests passed for the validated W4A16 path. - Prepared W1 and W2 pointer-identity assertions passed, confirming that the packed object reused the checkpoint allocations. - `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` loaded with `moe_backend="flashinfer_b12x"`, captured the PIECEWISE CUDA Graph at batch size 1, and completed deterministic generation with 16 output tokens. - The corresponding FlashInfer lifecycle suite passed with 30 tests; its targeted CUDA Graph test also passed. - FlashInfer's isolated ownership benchmark reduced preparation allocation delta from 108 MiB to 12 MiB for E=64, H=1024, I=1024. The 96 MiB difference equals the source W1 and W2 storage. - CUDA Graph validation covered 1, 8, 64, and 256 tokens. Prepared-weight, workspace, input, and output pointers remained stable; eager and replay outputs had zero maximum absolute difference. - All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the full rebased stack. No separate model-quality evaluation was run because this changes weight ownership and dispatches the same prepared W4A16 kernel. Numerical equivalence is covered by the kernel-reference and eager-versus-graph comparisons above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \ --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \ --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 # env: # VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 # VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 # VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0 # Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0) resp = client.chat.completions.create( model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}], max_tokens=64, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}, ) print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.

signal.text: ## Summary - recognize the NVIDIA `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` warmup path instead of requiring the AMD/XPU `hc_pre` and `hc_post` CustomOps - warm up the same NVIDIA TileLang pre, fused post/pre, and post functions used by `forward()`, including the real attention and FFN normalization parameters - warm up the NVIDIA TileLang HC head while preserving the existing AMD/XPU CustomOp paths ## Testing - `pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py` (`6 passed`) - `ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py` - `ruff check vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py` - `git diff --check` The unit tests cover backend selection, operation order, tensor sizes, scalar arguments, normalization parameters, and preservation of the CustomOp paths. signal.title: [RFC] Sleep/Wake Correctness for RL
signal.text: **Related RFCs:** [#45585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585) (RL CI roadmap), [#48311](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48311) (engine lifecycle), [#48312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48312) (weight-update correctness), and [#48305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48305) (training-inference consistency). ## Problem Sleep/wake must preserve liveness, memory ownership, model state, request state, and output correctness across every advertised model architecture and parallelism configuration. The bugs below were discovered by downstream RL frameworks or by vLLM RL lifecycle testing in production-like environments. P0/P1 describes operational severity. `SW1`–`SW6` below is the canonical root-cause taxonomy used by tests and the RL new-model support checklist. ## Scope and complete transition This tracker owns sleep, wake, pause, drain, memory remap, and request/cache continuity. Weight mutation itself is owned by #48312. The combined RL transaction is: ```text pause/drain -> sleep -> wake(weights) -> reload/update -> post-load/finalize -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate versioned caches -> resume ``` A 200 response proves only that an endpoint returned. Correctness requires the state and output oracles below before serving resumes. ## Root-cause taxonomy | ID | Category | Required invariant | Minimum regression check | |---|---|---|---| | SW1 | Transition ordering and quiescence | No kernel, collective, scheduler step, or new request may touch memory whose required tags are unmapped; partial wake must not resume inference | in-flight decode + concurrent arrival + full/partial wake; synchronize all ranks; first post-wake request must complete | | SW2 | Memory ownership, tags, and accounting | Every CUDA graph, weight, KV/SSM, LoRA, multimodal, offload, and communicator allocation is owned and unmapped/remapped exactly once | per-tag resident-byte accounting, repeated cycles, double-free/idempotency checks, TP/PP where declared | | SW3 | State/value reconstruction | Remapped forward-visible state is initialized from an authoritative host/config value or explicitly zeroed before reuse; calibrated values must not be replaced by defaults | non-default sentinels for FP8 scales/buffers; poison discarded pages; compare fixed-token logits/logprobs before and after wake | | SW4 | Heterogeneous state topology | Wake hooks traverse the actual state pytree, not an assumed flat `list[Tensor]`; Tensor/list/tuple/mapping/None/empty leaves are handled and unknown leaves fail explicitly | attention + hybrid Mamba/GDN cache trees, including TP/PP; recursive unit test plus real-model wake | | SW5 | Cache invalidation symmetry | Paired caches and state held by different processes/layers are invalidated consistently; a sender must not claim a hit when the receiver was cleared | warm same-key prefix/MM/offload cache -> sleep/pause(clear) -> reuse -> assert both sides miss or both retain | | SW6 | Request continuity | `abort`/`wait`/`keep` semantics preserve the exact promised request state; also tracked by #48312 | | [trl#5382](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5382) | trl | SW1/SW2 candidate | Colocation + TP + tool calling hangs in NCCL | | [OpenRLHF#1162](https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF/issues/1162) | OpenRLHF | SW1/SW2 candidate | `--colocate_all_models` + TP>1 sleep crash | ## Required regression matrix Every advertised feature combination gets the applicable rows; unsupported combinations fail closed and are documented rather than silently skipped. | Axis | PR gate | Nightly / hardware lane | |---|---|---| | Sleep transition | level 1 and 2; full wake; weights-only then KV wake | reverse partial order, 20+ cycles, idempotent/repeated calls | | Request state | idle plus one in-flight/new-arrival case | `abort`/`wait`/`keep`, async depth 0/1/N, speculative placeholders | | Model state | dense baseline; every model-declared state type | MoE, hybrid Mamba/GDN, VLM, LoRA, speculative target+draft | | KV state | default KV; FP8 if advertised | non-1.0 calibrated scales, native offload, poisoned discarded pages | | Parallelism | TP=1; TP=2 if advertised | PP=2, DP/EP for advertised model paths, multi-node where supported | | Cache state | cold and one warmed relevant cache | prefix, remote/offload KV, MM sender/receiver, hybrid recurrent state | ## Four mandatory oracles 1. **Output:** replay fixed token IDs and compare raw logits/logprobs before and after sleep/wake; generated text alone is insufficient. 2. **Liveness:** the first request and a second health request after wake must finish; an HTTP 200 followed by a dead worker fails. 3. **Memory ownership:** resident bytes and tag membership match the requested transition, no allocation is unmapped/remapped twice, and repeated cycles return to the same baseline. 4. **State/cache accessibility:** every required buffer, scale, KV/SSM state, and paired cache is initialized and mutually visible before scheduler resume. ## Composite RL E2E At least one production entrypoint test must execute the whole transaction with different weight sets A and B: ```text serve/capture A -> pause and drain -> sleep(level=2) -> wake(weights) -> update A to B through the production transfer path -> post-load/finalize and #48312 checks -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate affected caches -> resume -> fixed-token logits/logprobs == cold-B engine ``` This catches interaction bugs that isolated sleep and isolated reload tests cannot catch. ## Exit criteria - Every open P0 family above is fixed or the affected feature combination is rejected before transition. - SW1–SW6 each have a regression using the mandatory oracle named in the taxonomy. - Hybrid + FP8 KV covers recursive state traversal and non-1.0 scale restoration; #41602's five-model/200-cycle evidence is represented in nightly coverage. - Discarded ordinary KV and hybrid SSM pages are initialized before first slot reuse. - Pause/resume request continuity and multimodal sender/receiver cache symmetry remain covered after their fixes merge. - The composite sleep/update/wake test jointly satisfies this RFC and #48312. - The RL CI matrix runs for 30 days with no new correctness failure.

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable medium-skinny dispatch in RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel
signal.text: ## Purpose Before this change, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` routed a decode GEMM to the HIP `wvSplitK_int4_g` kernel only when the activation row count was at most five (`M <= 5`) and the total activation size satisfied `K * M <= 32768`. The existing C++ operator supports up to five activation rows (`N_in <= 5`) and accepts `K_in * N_in` up to `int(max_lds_len * 1.2)`. With `max_lds_len = 32768`, the effective upper limit is `39321` elements. Python `M` maps to C++ `N_in`. For inputs above the regular LDS capacity, the medium kernel keeps the activation prefix in LDS and reads the remaining elements from global memory. Consequently, supported shapes with `K * M` between `32768` and `39321` (exclusive of the lower bound and inclusive of the upper bound) fell back to Triton instead of using the existing HIP kernel. This PR aligns the Python dispatch limit with the C++ operator contract. It also adds dispatch-boundary tests and numerical correctness coverage for the newly enabled range. No C++ kernel is changed. ## Duplicate-work check Open PR searches for medium-skinny, wvSplitK W4A16, and RDNA hybrid W4A16 found no duplicate. Related PRs #46186, #51511, and #50618 do not modify this hybrid dispatch threshold. ## Test Plan Test environment: All tests were run locally on the following system: | Component | Value | | --- | --- | | GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S | | GPU architecture | gfx1151 | | Memory | 128 GB unified memory (96 GiB VRAM, 32 GiB host-visible) | | Operating system | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS | | ROCm | 7.2.3 | The end-to-end comparison covered the two medium-skinny `down_proj` shapes below: | Model | Batch | `down_proj` shape | `K * M` | Before this PR | With this PR | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | --- | | `Qwen3-8B-GPTQ-Int4` | 3 | `M=3, K=12288, N=4096` | 36864 | Triton | HIP medium | | `Qwen3-4B-GPTQ-Int4` | 4 | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 38912 | Triton | HIP medium | The end-to-end benchmark used identical settings before and after this change: - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` with the `ROCM_ATTN` backend; - eager execution (`enforce_eager=True`), with HIP Graph and `torch.compile` disabled; - prefix caching disabled; - fixed prompts and random seed; - 512 output tokens per request with `temperature=0` and `ignore_eos=True`; - one warmup followed by three measured runs. Functional validation included dispatch tests at the regular and medium boundaries, FP16 and BF16 medium-kernel comparisons against an FP32 reference, and the complete hybrid W4A16 test file. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` were also run on the changed files. ## Test Result ### End-to-end decode performance Qwen3-8B (`batch=3`, `K * M=36864`): | Metric | Before this PR | With this PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Aggregate decode throughput | 41.70 tok/s | 68.16 tok/s | +63.43% | | Per-request decode throughput | 13.90 tok/s | 22.72 tok/s | +63.43% | | Batch wall time | 36.92 s | 22.60 s | -38.79% | Qwen3-4B (`batch=4`, `K * M=38912`): | Metric | Before this PR | With this PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Aggregate decode throughput | 119.30 tok/s | 126.83 tok/s | +6.31% | | Per-request decode throughput | 29.83 tok/s | 31.71 tok/s | +6.31% | | Batch wall time | 17.19 s | 16.16 s | -5.99% | ### Direct kernel timing | Shape | Triton | HIP medium | Speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `M=3, K=12288, N=4096` | 0.643 ms | 0.388 ms | 1.66x | | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 0.136 ms | 0.071 ms | 1.93x | ### Correctness and lint - Focused tests: 8 passed, 83 deselected - Complete hybrid W4A16 test file: 91 passed, 14 warnings - Applicable pre-commit hooks: passed - `git diff --check`: passed ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with this change. I reviewed and understand every submitted line and ran the validation reported above. No user-facing API or configuration is changed, so no documentation update is required. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and affected dispatch range are documented. - [x] Duplicate open PRs were searched and related PRs were reviewed. - [x] Test coverage and results are included. - [x] End-to-end and direct-kernel performance results are included. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] AI assistance is disclosed. </details>

signal.title: [Profiler] Add VLLM_ENABLE_MULTINODE_PROFILING to sync profiler start across DP ranks
signal.text: ## Purpose When profiling a multi-node data-parallel deployment, per-rank Kineto traces cannot be aligned onto a common time axis: - Kineto stamps each event on the local `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, whose origin differs per host. - `start_profile` reaches each DP rank asynchronously, at a different point in its own step loop. So traces from different nodes cover different iterations, and there is no shared landmark to line them up. ## Why not a barrier A `torch.distributed.barrier()` on the profiler control path does not work here and deadlocks: - `start_profile` is not a world collective. Under external-LB DP it is dispatched per engine core, and even when every pod is hit (e.g. sending `/start_profile` to all pods), each arrives at a different, unsynchronized step. - Every decode step, all DP ranks must jointly execute the EP all-to-all / DP coordination collective. The first rank to reach the barrier stops stepping, so the other ranks wedge on the next collective before they ever reach their own barrier. Neither side converges. ## What this does Ride the per-step DP coordination all-reduce that every rank already executes in lockstep (`coordinate_batch_across_dp` -> `_synchronize_dp_ranks`), which is correctly ordered against the EP collective. Add opt-in `VLLM_ENABLE_MULTINODE_PROFILING` (off by default, only affects `data_parallel_size > 1`). When set: 1. `start_profile` on a worker only records a pending request (`DPProfilerSync.request_start`) instead of starting capture. 2. The pending flag is OR-reduced onto the existing per-step all-reduce (one extra row in the coordination tensor). 3. Once any rank has requested it, every rank latches the decision on the same step and the worker starts capture on the next step. Consequences: - No extra collective and no new failure mode: it reuses a collective every rank already runs, so it cannot deadlock the way a control-path barrier does. - Only one rank needs to receive `start_profile`; the OR propagates the request to all ranks. - Capture begins on the same step on every rank, giving multi-node traces a shared start iteration to align on. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_profiler.py`: - `TestDPProfilerSync`: local request reaches consensus; a remote-only request still starts this rank; no request -> no start; the latch survives a later `False` observation (PP+SP double reduce in one step); `cancel()` drops a pending request; start fires exactly once. - `TestWorkerSyncedProfileStart`: `Worker._maybe_start_synced_profile` starts on consensus exactly once, does nothing without consensus, and is a no-op when the sync is disabled. - Default path unchanged: with the env var unset, `start_profile` starts capture immediately as before.

signal.title: [Bug]: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs
signal.text: ### Summary `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` let Triton specialize on the 16-byte alignment of their metadata pointers (`cache_indices_ptr`, `query_start_loc_ptr`, `conv_state_indices_ptr`, ...). Three facts make this a problem: 1. **The specialization buys nothing here.** These arrays are read one scalar at a time (a block index, an offset), so the aligned and unaligned binaries run at the same speed. Alignment specialization only pays off for wide vectorized loads (`x_ptr`, `w_ptr`, ... — not these args). 2. **Their alignment flips at runtime.** They are per-step slices of batch metadata, so the address offset depends on the batch layout of that step. 3. **Warmup can never cover the unaligned variant.** Warmup tensors are freshly allocated and therefore always aligned. So the first compile of the unaligned variant is guaranteed to happen *during inference* — this is (part of) the latency spike tracked in #43009, and `jit_monitor` (#45631) duly warns about it. In a multi-node deployment this goes from a latency nuisance to a correctness bug. ### What we hit GRPO RL training, Nemotron-3-Super-120B, 6 vLLM engines on 6 GB200 nodes, with a shared `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` on Lustre (for warm starts). Engines intermittently returned **all-NaN logits from the first prefill token** — only for long prompts, only on some engines, and unreproducible afterwards. Disk forensics (no repro needed): - These kernels compiled to disk exactly 3 times; the mtimes match the 3 NaN windows one-to-one. After the cache filled up: 40+ clean rounds, zero recurrence. - Two cache hash dirs for the same kernel appeared **within the same minute**, differing only in the `tt.divisibility=16` attribute on `cache_indices_ptr` — two nodes concurrently compiling the aligned/unaligned variants into the same shared dir. Triton's cache group write (`__grp__*.json` + cubin) is not atomic across writers. - Every failing request was ≥143K tokens (its `cache_indices` slice lands at an unaligned offset); every success ≤138K. Only some engines were poisoned — the race losers. A race loser ends up running the aligned-assumption binary on unaligned `cache_indices` → reads wrong block indices → garbage → all-NaN logits, silently. Sharing `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` across nodes is on us, and we now scope it per node. But the variant axis itself has no upside, and single-node users still pay the inference-time compile spike for it. ### Proposed fix Add the metadata pointers to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` — the same mechanism #50000 already applied to `num_cache_lines` in these exact kernels: ```python @triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[ "num_cache_lines", "cache_indices_ptr", "has_initial_states_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr", "batch_ptr", "token_chunk_offset_ptr", "block_idx_first_scheduled_token", "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx", "num_computed_tokens", ]) def _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel(...) @triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[ "num_cache_lines", "batch", "conv_state_indices_ptr", "num_accepted_tokens_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr", "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx", ]) def _causal_conv1d_update_kernel(...) ``` Effect: one binary per config, compiled without the alignment assumption, correct for any address. Warmup covers it naturally, nothing left to JIT during inference, no variants to race. Zero perf cost (scalar loads only); the wide data pointers keep their specialization. Relation to #48363: complementary. That PR warms the fwd kernel by sweeping 8 alignment combinations; with the specialization removed the sweep collapses to a single call, and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` (not covered there) is fixed as well. We're happy to open a PR (change verified against Triton 3.6: the flag drops the divisibility bit from the specialization key for pointer args, `triton/runtime/jit.py`). ### Environment Observed on vLLM 0.25.1 (aarch64, GB200, Triton 3.6.0); the kernel decorators are unchanged on current `main` (f97e502969).

signal.title: [RFC]: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM
signal.text: # RFC: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM ## Motivation The [vLLM Agentic API project](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api) has completed an MVP supporting Codex and Claude Code with vLLM as the inference engine. It is a high-performance Rust runtime for the capabilities these clients need beyond token generation: stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, MCP, streaming, and Responses/Messages compatibility. Agentic workloads are increasingly important to llm-d and the broader serving community. The question is how vLLM and Agentic API should evolve together as these workloads become more stateful and operationally complex. Emerging capabilities such as [Computer History](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/computer-history) show how agentic systems are beginning to use persistent activity, search, and external context to resume work and understand what happened across tools. vLLM already supports Responses and Messages APIs, an optional in-process Responses store, and MCP/tool-server integrations. Agentic API builds on that foundation with a broader runtime for stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, vendor-neutral integrations, and the operational needs of agentic inference workloads. These capabilities are complementary, but vLLM does not currently plan to pursue the full Agentic API scope in its existing serving surface. How should vLLM and Agentic API evolve together to support this next generation of agentic inference workloads? ## Proposed change We propose that vLLM make agentic inference a first-class supported capability by integrating more tightly with Agentic API. The project’s MVP provides a working starting point for stateful Responses and Messages APIs, tool orchestration, and vendor-neutral integrations. The options below describe different ways to bring those capabilities into the vLLM ecosystem; this RFC seeks agreement on the desired integration model and the boundaries that should remain stable. ### Goal Agentic API aims to provide a vendor-neutral integration layer connecting agentic clients to databases, third-party APIs, and external tools while preserving and optimizing vLLM’s inference capabilities. It should also provide llm-d with practical Responses API and Messages API solutions that externalize conversation state and orchestration without forcing hard affinity to the engine that served an earlier turn. ### Scope and boundary The boundary is intentional: vLLM Core focuses on model execution, scheduling, batching, tokenization, rendering, parsing, and structured decoding; Agentic API focuses on state, external integrations, tool orchestration, and client compatibility. The goal is to make these capabilities more tightly integrated and accessible through the vLLM ecosystem. ### Desired outcome The goal is for the vLLM ecosystem to expose a first-class agentic inference experience by building on vLLM’s existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and integrating the broader capabilities provided by Agentic API. This RFC seeks alignment on how Agentic API and vLLM should become more tightly integrated to reach that goal. ## Options These options are not mutually exclusive. A first-class boundary could be the near-term step before deciding whether to merge or formally package Agentic API with vLLM. | Option | Description | Proposed change | Main tradeoff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **1. Merge** | Move Agentic API into vLLM Core. | Merge the code, consolidate APIs and tests, and document the agentic serving experience in vLLM. | One project and release process, but vLLM takes on persistence, integrations, and workflow orchestration. | | **2. Remain separate** | Continue with today’s architecture and independent evolution. | Improve documentation, publish a dedicated Agentic API website or landing page, and clearly document how it integrates with vLLM. | Clear boundaries, but leaves the broader agentic workload experience outside vLLM’s existing serving surface and risks capability gaps and compatibility drift. | | **3. Official dependency** | Keep a separate repository, but officially distribute or depend on Agentic API for Responses and agentic inference. | Add supported packaging and version compatibility, vLLM documentation and examples, and a maintained integration path. | Better integration, but tighter versioning and packaging coupling. | | **4. First-class runtime boundary** | Keep the repositories separate while defining supported interfaces, compatibility guarantees, and shared tests. | Establish shared contracts, conformance tests, release coordination, and cross-linked documentation or landing pages. | Preserves flexibility, but requires sustained coordination. | ## Key questions 1. How should vLLM extend its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support to provide a broader agentic inference experience? 2. What should agentic applications, including coding harnesses, be able to rely on from the vLLM ecosystem? 3. Which responsibilities should remain separate even if the projects are distributed together? 4. What interfaces and tests should vLLM, Agentic API, and llm-d share? ## Additional context - [vLLM Responses API and Tool Calling lookahead (#34857)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34857) - [vLLM session-centric KV-cache orchestration (#48501)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48501) - [vLLM Agentic API Codex CLI integration (#54)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/54) - [vLLM Agentic API response-store semantics (#14)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/14) - [vLLM multi-turn Responses API support (#33089)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33089) - [vLLM Rust frontend / Anthropic Messages RFC (#47753)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47753) - [llm-d-router session-centric KV lifecycle orchestration (#1979)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1979) - [llm-d-router external Responses state store (#1104)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1104) - [llm-d-router Session Control Protocol (#2003)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/2003) - [llm-d-router agentic routing profiles (#1867)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1867) ## Recommended direction The long-term goal should be for vLLM to provide a first-class agentic serving experience that builds on its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and adds the orchestration and integrations needed by real agentic workloads. The immediate goal is tighter integration between Agentic API and vLLM Core so that vLLM’s support for agentic workloads is visible and accessible throughout the ecosystem. The options above provide several paths to that outcome, from merging the projects to establishing an officially supported dependency or first-class integration contract. ## CC list @qandrew @vMaroon @blasrodri @BugenZhao @njhill @chaunceyjiang @mgoin @bbrowning @robertgshaw2-redhat @noobHappylife @maralbahari @tjtanaa @ashwing

signal.text: ## Summary - extends the TurboQuant MLA work in #41803 with the GLM-5.2 sparse MLA path on current main - adds packed 4-bit latent KV storage, fused sparse decode, sparse prefill, and GLM-4 MoE MTP plumbing - adds DCP/MTP/PP correctness fixes, canonical DCP interleave handling, CUDA-graph-safe workspaces, and asynchronous MTP handoff ## Validation - end-to-end cold and hot inference workloads completed successfully - hot-cache median TTFT improved by 31x and median end-to-end latency improved by 8.26x in the validation workload - all requests completed without connector, engine, worker, or completion errors - changed-file pre-commit suite passes, including Ruff, mypy, configuration validation, and forbidden CUDA API checks ## Relationship to existing work #41803 provides the dense Triton-fused TurboQuant MLA decode foundation. signal.title: [Bugfix][gpt-oss] Strip matched stop string from Harmony reasoning/content
signal.text: FIX #52599 ## Problem For a non-streaming GPT-OSS chat completion, when a client `stop` string is matched, `finish_reason=stop` / `stop_reason` are correctly reported, but with `include_stop_str_in_output=false` the matched stop string is still present in the returned `reasoning` (or `content`) text. Repro in #52599. ## Root cause `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update()` (`vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`) already excludes a matched stop string from the character-level `output_text` when `include_stop_str_in_output` is false — but it deliberately keeps the stop-matching token in `self.token_ids` (needed elsewhere for correct usage/logprobs accounting; see the `skipped_stop_token_id` bookkeeping in `update()`). The chat serving layer (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py`) passes those untruncated `token_ids` straight into `HarmonyParser.parse()`, which reconstructs `reasoning`/`content` purely from token IDs via the Harmony streamable parser and never consults the truncated `output_text` at all. So the character-level stop-string truncation that every non-Harmony (text-based) reasoning parser inherits for free never reaches whichever Harmony channel the stop string lands in — this affects `content` too, not just `reasoning`; the issue happened to reproduce on `reasoning` because these prompts finish mid-analysis with `content: null`. ## Fix `HarmonyParser.parse()` now reuses `check_stop_strings()` — the same matching/truncation function the detokenizer already uses — and applies it to `reasoning` and `content` after the Harmony channel split, so both channels honor `include_stop_str_in_output` the same way the plain-text path does. ## Testing Added two tests to `tests/parser/test_harmony.py`: - `test_stop_string_stripped_from_reasoning`: a stop string matched inside the `analysis` channel is stripped when `include_stop_str_in_output=False`. - `test_stop_string_kept_when_include_stop_str_in_output`: unchanged when the flag is `True`. I verified the core stop-matching/truncation logic standalone against vLLM's real, unmodified `check_stop_strings` (exercised the exact repro string from #52599, multi-stop earliest-match tie-breaking, and the `include_stop_str_in_output=True` passthrough case) — all correct. I was not able to run the full `tests/parser/test_harmony.py` suite in my environment (no network access to pull the `openai/gpt-oss-20b` tokenizer / `openai_harmony` / `xgrammar`), so the added tests are unverified against the real Harmony parser end-to-end — flagging this explicitly for review rather than claiming full green CI. ## Known limitation This is scoped to the non-streaming `parse()` path, matching the reported repro. Streaming (`parse_delta()`) needs the equivalent of the detokenizer's `stop_buffer_length` buffering to avoid emitting a partial stop string before it's known to complete without more truncation; left as a follow-up rather than attempted here. ## AI assistance This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code), based on tracing the actual vLLM 0.27.0 source after reproducing the issue on NIM and the official upstream image. Marked as draft pending review and a real test run.
signal.author: lamduong0

signal.title: Optimize ppc64le vLLM runtime image size
signal.text: ## Summary Optimize the vLLM runtime image for the `ppc64le` architecture by removing unnecessary files from the Python virtual environment and excluding build-time artifacts from the final image. ## Changes - Clean up Python cache files (`__pycache__`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`). - Remove unnecessary test and documentation files. - Strip unneeded symbols from shared libraries where applicable. - Exclude temporary build artifacts and pip cache. - Copy only the required runtime virtual environment into the final image. ## Benefits - Reduces the final `ppc64le` image size. - Improves image pull and deployment time. - Reduces registry storage and network bandwidth. - No changes to runtime functionality. ## Testing - Successfully built the `ppc64le` image. - Verified the vLLM server starts successfully. - Validated model loading and inference after the image size optimizations.

signal.title: [XPU][Bugfix] Fix XPU crash with speculative decoding + prefix caching in Mamba models
signal.text: Fixes: [#48059](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48059) Alternate fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48109 Why this PR: Did not notice the reported bug and alternate fix when I created the PR, apologies. The pattern this PR implements is more consistent with implementation across codebase. Re-interpretation to a negative-int64 in the alternate fix breaks the established pattern. ## Purpose Models tested: - cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ-INT4 - cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4 - SergiioB/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4-sym-G128-MTP-BF16 HW Backend: XPU Hardware: Intel ARC Pro B70 vllm version: 0.27.2rc1.dev122+g8efa13b70 If I only enable prefix caching, I see no error and vllm can process requests. If I only use spec decoding(MTP) that works fine too. But if I use both together I get following error: ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long File "vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 767, in initialize_from_forward_context self.state_base_addrs[idx] = state.data_ptr() ``` Root cause: On XPU, `tensor.data_ptr()` can return memory addresses >= 2^63 — exceeding the signed `int64` range. The `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` class stores these addresses via element-wise assignment (`tensor[idx] = value`), which fails because PyTorch's `__setitem__` converts the scalar through C-level long() before any dtype check, regardless of the tensor's declared dtype. Fix applied: Two changes, both in `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: 1. Change dtype from int64 to uint64 for state_base_addrs and block_table_ptrs — matching the existing pattern in block_table.py (# NOTE(woosuk): Use uint64 instead of int64 to cover all possible addresses). 2. Collect pointers into a list and bulk-create the tensor instead of element-wise assignment. torch.tensor(list, dtype=torch.uint64) correctly handles large pointer values; tensor[idx] = large_int does not (even with uint64 dtype). ## Test Plan Re-build and run the same model with both `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` and `--enable-prefix-caching`. signal.title: [BugFix] Skip GDN/KDA recurrent state updates for stale zero-accept s…
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes an illegal memory access (CUDA crash) in the GDN and Kimi-K3 KDA attention backends when speculative decoding runs with async scheduling. When an async-scheduling step is discarded, `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change` writes the row's `valid_sampled_token_count` — which is `0` for a row whose sampled tokens were thrown away — into `num_accepted_tokens`. Every consumer of that tensor assumes the count is in `1..1+num_speculative_tokens` and indexes the request's state slots with `num_accepted_tokens - 1`. A `0` therefore produces index `-1`: - In the Triton kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`, `causal_conv1d_update`, and the vendored KDA recurrent kernels) that is an out-of-bounds load → illegal memory access. `causal_conv1d_update` usually faults first. - On the CPU align-mode paths in `mamba_utils.py` it is worse than a crash: `-1` is a *valid* Python index, so the copy silently reads from the end of the state and corrupts output with no error. The fix treats `0` as what it actually means — "this row is stale, it has no valid spec state to resume from" — rather than as a count to be clamped. In the metadata builders, stale rows get their whole `spec_state_indices_tensor` row set to `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, which makes the existing `state_idx <= 0` guards in the FLA kernels and the null-block check in `causal_conv1d_update` skip those rows entirely: no initial-state read, and no final-state write. That last part matters — a clamp-only patch keeps the row in bounds but lets the kernel advance the recurrent state of a request whose step was discarded, silently corrupting it. Both ops are elementwise and introduce no CPU sync, and they sit before the full-cudagraph buffer copies, so the eager and cudagraph paths both inherit the fix. The kernel-level clamps are kept as defense in depth, mirroring the existing pattern in `mamba_ssm.py` and `bailing_linear_attn.py`. Note that `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` subclasses `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` but fully overrides `build`, so it does **not** inherit the builder-level fix and needs its own copy. Its version is deliberately out-of-place (`masked_fill`, not `masked_fill_`): the packed-decode branch slices `block_table_tensor` with a basic slice, and in `"all"`/`"none"` cache modes `_mamba_get_block_table_tensor` returns the runner's persistent block table unchanged — an in-place fill there would write `NULL_BLOCK_ID` into the block table and corrupt subsequent steps. The GDN builder is safe in-place because both of its branches build the tensor via boolean-mask indexing, which copies. Deliberately left alone: the CPU GDN backend (asserts spec decode unsupported), and the Mamba2/Bailing paths (already memory-safe via existing clamps; their clamp-to-slot-0 semantics are unchanged). The bogus 100%-acceptance metric reported for all-invalid draft rows is cosmetic and independent of this crash. Related bug reports: - #41190 - #40756 Related open PR (proposing a workaround): - #48475 ## Test Plan ```bash # Builders directly modified by this PR pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -v pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py -v # Kernels modified by this PR pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py -v pytest tests/kernels/mamba/ -v # Async spec-decode path that produces the zero count pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_backup_token_async_spec.py -v pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py -v # E2E reproduction: GDN-backed model, spec decode + async scheduling, # concurrent streams, eager and cudagraph ``` Before this PR the existing builder suites all passed `torch.ones(...)` for `num_accepted_tokens`, so no test exercised the zero case at all. This PR adds that coverage: - `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots` — stale rows nulled, live rows untouched, counts clamped; parametrized over cudagraph modes. - `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_does_not_corrupt_block_table` — guards the in-place-fill hazard. - `test_kda_metadata.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots[_cuda]` — same contract for the overriding KDA builder, across `none`/`align` cache modes and both cudagraph modes. - `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py::test_spec_decoding_null_state_row_leaves_state_untouched` — asserts a nulled row's state blocks are **bit-identical** after the kernel runs, i.e. no state advanced, while a live row in the same batch still updates. This is the property that distinguishes this fix from a clamp-only patch like proposed in PR #48475. - `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py::test_spec_decoding_zero_accepted_tokens_is_in_bounds` — defense-in-depth: a raw `0` reaching the kernel is clamped rather than indexing at `-1`. ## Test Result Run on a single RTX 5090 (sm_120), CUDA 13.0, torch from `--torch-backend=auto`. ### Suites | Suite | Result | | --- | --- | | `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py` | 12 passed | | `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py` | 17 passed | | `tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py` + `test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py` | 57 passed (combined with the two above) | | `tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | 164 passed | | `tests/kernels/mamba/` (rest) | 567 passed, 26 skipped (18m51s) | | `tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py`, `test_gdn_forward_core_split.py`, `test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py` | 109 passed, 1 skipped | | `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_step_kernel.py`, `test_rejection_sampler_utils.py` | 45 passed | `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. ### Before/after on the new tests The new tests were run against the parent commit's source (fix reverted, tests kept). **9 fail without the fix, all pass with it:** ``` FAILED test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots[False] E AssertionError: every state slot of a stale row must be nulled so the kernel's state_idx <= 0 guard skips it, got [944, 944, 944, 944] ``` i.e. without the fix the stale row keeps a live block (944) that the kernel then both reads and **writes**. For the KDA builder, which overrides `build()` and does not inherit the GDN fix: ``` pre-fix KDA stale row: [776, 425, 274, 182] counts: [0, 2] post-fix KDA stale row: [0, 0, 0, 0] counts: [1, 2] block table intact: True ``` ### Correction to the crash characterization Under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck`, the pre-fix kernel at these tensor shapes reports **`ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`** — the `-1` index lands inside the allocation, on the neighbouring row. What it actually produces is silent numerical corruption: ``` E AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal! E Mismatched elements: 24870 / 32768 (75.9%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 0, 2, 86) ``` So at these shapes the bug is **NaN output, not a fault**; whether it faults depends on allocation layout. This does not change the fix, but it means the failure mode in the wild may be bad output rather than a clean crash. With the fix applied, the same sanitizer run is clean (4 passed, 0 errors). --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Let an optional Literal flag accept the None it advertises
signal.text: ## Problem `_compute_kwargs` makes an optional field's flag accept `None` by wrapping its type, then advertising the sentinel: ```python if type(None) in type_hints and not contains_type(type_hints, bool): kwargs[name]["type"] = optional_type(kwargs[name]["type"]) if kwargs[name].get("choices"): kwargs[name]["choices"].append("None") ``` but `optional_type` returns the **object** `None`, not the string: ```python def _optional_type(val: str) -> T | None: if val == "" or val == "None": return None return parse_type(return_type)(val) ``` argparse applies `type` **before** it checks `choices`, so the converted value is `None` while the registered choice is `"None"`, and the flag rejects the value its own help text offers: ``` $ vllm serve ... --collect-detailed-traces None error: argument --collect-detailed-traces: invalid choice: None (choose from 'all', 'model', 'worker', 'None') ``` The message is self-contradictory: it lists `'None'` among the valid choices in the same breath as refusing it. The empty string, the other spelling `optional_type` accepts, fails identically. There is no way to pass these flags the value they document, so the only route to `None` is to omit the flag entirely. 16 flags are affected: ``` --kv-role --pooling-type --profiler --safetensors-load-strategy --seq-pooling-type --proton-backend --ssu-algorithm --tok-pooling-type --proton-hook --mm-encoder-attn-dtype --task --proton-output-format --collect-detailed-traces --method --moe-backend --kv-cache-dtype ``` ## Fix Append the sentinel that survives the conversion: ```python kwargs[name]["choices"].append(None) ``` argparse `str()`s choices when it renders help, so `--help` is byte-identical: ``` before: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] after: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] ``` ## Not a duplicate Searched `argparse_utils`, `load_config_file`, `optional_type`, `choices`, and `"invalid choice"` across open issues and PRs. The nearby open work is on a different defect in a different file: #49057 fixes `false` booleans in YAML configs and #51623 / #52077 handle empty YAML configs, all in `vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py`. This one is in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` and is about CLI choices, and this PR does not touch `argparse_utils.py` at all. ## Tests `test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli` in `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`, built on the `DummyConfig.optional_literal` fixture that file already defines. It pins both spellings `optional_type` accepts, that a real choice still works, and that `None` is still advertised in help, which is what made the rejection contradictory. ``` before after test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli FAIL PASS (SystemExit 2) ``` **How it was run.** `python -m pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` exits 139 on this machine, on a clean tree as well as with this change, because collection segfaults inside native `xgrammar` init. That is unrelated to this PR, so the test body was executed standalone against the real `get_kwargs` and the real `DummyConfig` lifted from the file with `ast`, once against unmodified `arg_utils.py` and once with the change. The 16-flag list above was produced the same way, by running `get_kwargs` over every dataclass in `vllm.config` and reporting fields whose choices contain the string `"None"` but not the object; it goes from 16 to 0 with this change. `ruff check` gains no new findings (the file's 2 pre-existing ones are unchanged) and `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. **No model evaluation results.** This changes argument parsing only: nothing about model output, accuracy or serving behaviour moves. The sole behavioural difference is that a value already listed in `--help` is now accepted instead of erroring out, so there is nothing to evaluate. AI assistance was used for this change.

signal.title: Fix for Issue 52413: causal_conv1d Alignment Specialization Race Condition
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes issue #52413: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs. **Problem:** - Triton kernels allowed alignment specialization on dynamic metadata pointers that change per-request - This caused unnecessary inference-time JIT recompiles - Concurrent JIT cache writes led to corrupted kernels producing silent all-NaN outputs (data corruption) **Solution:** Added dynamic metadata pointers to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` in both `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` decorators to prevent alignment-based specialization. ## Test Plan - [x] Added regression test `test_causal_conv1d_metadata_ptrs_not_alignment_specialized()` that validates kernel decorators keep metadata pointers in alignment exemption list - [x] Test command: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --noconftest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d_jit_metadata.py` - [x] Verified fix doesn't break existing kernel signatures or math - [ ] Full causal_conv1d test suite on Linux with CUDA (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py`) ## Test Results - [x] Regression test **PASSED**: `test_causal_conv1d_metadata_ptrs_not_alignment_specialized` - [x] No compile errors in modified files - [x] Code changes verified to be minimal and isolated to kernel specialization metadata only - [ ] Full functional test suite pending (requires Linux CUDA environment) --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm] Enable RDNA3 W4A16 GEMM kernels on gfx1151 (Strix Halo)
signal.text: ## Purpose This fixes Q4 / W4A16 GPTQ MoE inference on gfx1151 / Strix Halo. The motivating repro is: ```text palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 ``` This model works on gfx1100, but did not run correctly on gfx1151. The issue is that the existing RDNA3 W4A16 C++ kernels were scoped to gfx1100 only, so gfx1151 could fall back to the generic Q4 MoE path (which deadlocks) instead of using the native RDNA3 W4A16 path. This PR extends the scalar RDNA3 W4A16 GEMM/MoE kernels to gfx1151 while keeping the existing gfx1100 behavior intact. Scope: - Enable scalar RDNA3 W4A16 dense/MoE kernels for gfx1100 and gfx1151. - Keep the WMMA prefill translation unit/op gfx1100-only. - Add a runtime gcnArchName guard so fat binaries containing both gfx1100 and gfx1151 still dispatch WMMA only on actual gfx1100 devices. - Update Python selection/routing so gfx1151 can use the RDNA3 W4A16 kernels. - Add/update compile-guard and runtime tests for the gfx1100/gfx1151 split. This is intentionally scoped to Q4 / W4A16. It does not attempt to fix other model quants like FP8 MoE (which remain broken for gfx1151). ### gfx1100 safety gfx1100 already works and should not regress. This PR preserves the existing gfx1100 behavior: - gfx1100 keeps scalar RDNA3 W4A16 kernels. - gfx1100 keeps the WMMA prefill path. - gfx1151 gets the scalar RDNA3 W4A16 path but not the gfx1100-only WMMA path. - Fat-binary builds are guarded at runtime so gfx1151 cannot accidentally call the gfx1100-only WMMA implementation. ### Duplicate-work check These open PRs were checked before preparing this: - #44331: tuned Triton MoE configs - #43389: Triton int4 repacking - #40977: dense hybrid W4A16 work Those are related to ROCm/Q4/MoE performance or routing, but they do not enable the existing native RDNA3 W4A16 kernels on gfx1151 while preserving the gfx1100 WMMA split. ### Notes Local gfx1151 validation required the separate ROCm platform-detection fix from #46110 to be applied temporarily. That platform-detection issue is intentionally not included in this kernel PR. ### AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance, but has been fully reviewed and human verified before submission. Signed-off: lhl ## Test Plan gfx1151 / Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo local validation. Targeted RDNA3 W4A16 tests: ```bash PYTHONPATH=~/vllm/vllm-lhl \ PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151 \ PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 \ VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 \ python -m pytest \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_compile_guards.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_moe_w4a16.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_selection.py \ -q ``` Manual e2e repro smoke: ```text model: palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 prompt: Hello, my name is settings: enforce_eager=True max_model_len=128 max_num_seqs=1 skip_mm_profiling=True VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 ``` Additional local synthetic MoE validation was run to check that the gfx1151 Q4 MoE path completes without hanging. ## Test Result Targeted RDNA3 W4A16 tests: ```text 151 passed, 6 skipped ``` E2E repro model: ```text palmfuture/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 ``` Result: ```text prompt: Hello, my name is generated: John. I am E2E_OK ``` This is the model that worked on gfx1100 but did not work on gfx1151 before this fix.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Hardware][Intel] Disable compiled grouped_topk on XPU
signal.text: ## Purpose On the affected Intel XPU stack, compiling the Python `grouped_topk` router produced invalid expert IDs during NemotronH native-MTP draft warmup: ```text Assertion `index out of bounds: 0 <= tmp0 < 128` failed. ``` The base WNA16 MoE path can avoid this Python router through the fused XPU implementation, while the MTP draft fallback reaches it during engine compile/warmup. **Fix:** keep `grouped_topk` eager only on XPU with `torch.compiler.disable`. Other platforms retain the existing `torch.compile` decorator. This is a narrow correctness workaround pending an XPU-safe compiled implementation; it does not clamp IDs or disable compilation for the surrounding model. The unrelated `test_outputs.py` portability change was removed during rebase because upstream #52237 already contains it. ## Test plan ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_grouped_topk_xpu.py ``` The XPU-only coverage checks softmax/sigmoid with and without correction bias, validates finite weights and expert IDs in `[0, 128)`, and verifies that an outer compiled graph can cross the XPU-eager router without a device assertion. Non-XPU environments skip this file; existing CUDA coverage is unchanged. ## Reproduction The reliable trigger is the compiled NemotronH MTP draft warmup path. A standalone random decomposition of the individual top-k operations did not reproduce the assertion, so it is not presented as the reproducer. Environment and exact command are posted in the PR discussion. ## Validation status - Branch rebased onto current `main`; PR is mergeable. - Python syntax compilation and `git diff --check`: pass. - Focused local pytest was not available in this checkout (`pytest` is not installed). - Intel CI and upstream checks were retriggered by the rewritten branch.
signal.author: SergiioB

signal.title: [K3] support recoverssm for K3
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose This PR adds RecoverSSM, a Kimi-K3-specific state recovery path for speculative KDA decoding on NVIDIA Model Runner V2. It is enabled through `--use-replayssm`, is intended for Kimi-K3 serving with DSpark, and supports `mamba_cache_mode=align` prefix caching. Without RecoverSSM, KDA speculative decoding materializes a full recurrent state for every speculative position. RecoverSSM keeps one checkpoint and compact per-token records, then reconstructs the state at the accepted position after every verify. Under the tested TP8 Kimi-K3 configuration, this increases the effective cache capacity by 10.97% at the same 46.48 GiB cache-memory budget. ## Design ### Kimi-K3-specific MRV2 integration The implementation is contained in the Kimi-K3 KDA metadata, layer, and RecoverSSM operator paths. The metadata builder gives speculative rows one KDA checkpoint slot and creates a model-specific post-sampling committer. RecoverSSM is selected through the existing `--use-replayssm` option. The regular KDA prefill and non-speculative decode paths are unchanged. ### Verify records FP32 corrections KDA verify reads the checkpoint without modifying it and computes the normal speculative outputs. For each speculative token it records: - the correction vector `u` in FP32; - the key and raw gate in the activation dtype. Recording `u` removes `v` and `beta` from the commit path and avoids recomputing the state-dependent correction. FP32 is used for `u` to preserve reconstruction accuracy; keys and gates remain BF16 in the evaluated configuration. ### Direct accepted-position reconstruction After verification determines the accepted length, one Triton kernel reconstructs the required checkpoint directly. For the KDA recurrence: ```text S_t = S_{t-1} * exp(g_t) + u_t outer k_t ``` The accepted state is: ```text S_p = S_0 * exp(sum(g_1 ... g_p)) + sum_j u_j outer (k_j * exp(sum(g_{j+1} ... g_p))) ``` The commit kernel evaluates this expression in reverse token order. It loads the original state once and does not recursively update or write intermediate states. The loop bound is the runtime accepted length rather than the complete eight-token DSpark activation window. In align mode, the same launch also reconstructs the next prefix-cache boundary when the accepted range crosses it. Convolution history is compacted to the accepted position and to the boundary using the same commit plan. ### Cache layout Each KDA page contains: ```text (convolution state, KDA checkpoint, FP32 correction records, key/gate records) ``` Recovery records are transient and are not included in prefix-cache state copies. The checkpoint and convolution state remain the prefix-cache boundary state. ## Scope - NVIDIA Kimi-K3 KDA - Model Runner V2 - speculative decoding, validated with Kimi-K3-DSpark and seven draft tokens - `mamba_cache_mode=align` prefix caching Shared changes are limited to the derived KDA RecoverSSM flag, state-layout helpers, and the post-sampling commit lifecycle. The recovery algorithm and cache layout remain Kimi-K3-specific, and this PR does not add Mamba2 support. ## Test Plan and Results ### Unit tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -v ``` Result: `69 passed`. The 18 RecoverSSM cases cover: - the actual eight-token DSpark window; - partial and full acceptance lengths; - direct final-state and align-boundary reconstruction; - both convolution-state layouts; - request-index remapping; - gates with and without a lower bound; - cache shape and dtype derivation. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_utils.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py ``` Result: all hooks passed. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` Result: passed for Python 3.12. ### End-to-end accuracy Controlled setup: - Kimi-K3 target and Kimi-K3-DSpark draft model, TP8 on two GB300 nodes; - seven greedy draft tokens and block rejection sampling; - align-mode Mamba cache, prefix caching, FP8 MLA cache, FlashInfer MLA, and fastsafetensors; - identical datasets, prompts, scorers, and serving parameters for RecoverSSM ON and OFF. | GSM8K, 1,319 samples | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | ON - OFF | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Flexible extract | 96.3609% | 96.1334% | +0.2274 pp | | Strict match | 96.0576% | 95.9060% | +0.1516 pp | The paired 95% confidence intervals were `[-0.4549, +0.9098]` pp for flexible extract and `[-0.6065, +0.9098]` pp for strict match. Both runs completed all 1,319 requests with zero request errors. Independently initialized greedy serving runs are not bitwise deterministic, so the paired score comparison is used instead of exact generated-text equality. | MRCR, 40 long prompts run cold and warm | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | |---|---:|---:| | Cold score | 0.74879 | 0.66791 | | Warm score | 0.74879 | 0.66791 | | Cold/warm exact-output consistency | 100% | 97.5% | | Warm prefix-cache token hit rate | 89.13% | 90.50% | The MRCR prompts ranged from 16,757 to 33,772 tokens and contained 991,216 prompt tokens per pass. RecoverSSM completed both passes without request errors. Total DSpark acceptance was 53.3514% with RecoverSSM and 53.4062% without it, a difference of -0.0548 percentage points. GSM8K-only acceptance was 50.0899% with RecoverSSM and 50.0336% without it. ### Memory capacity Both variants used a fixed 46.48 GiB cache-memory budget. | Metric | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Effective cache capacity | 2,856,170 tokens | 2,573,777 tokens | +10.97% | | Max 262k-request concurrency | 10.895x | 9.818x | +10.97% | ### Nsight Systems profile The profile used batch 32, 128 forced output tokens, and 80 captured decode steps per GPU on the same two-node TP8 setup. The aggregate results below include eight initial small-batch steps. | KDA work per decode step | Initial recurrent recovery | RecoverSSM | |---|---:|---:| | Verify | 3.115 ms | 3.540 ms | | Commit | 4.793 ms | 1.464 ms | | Commit auxiliaries | 0.081 ms | 0.081 ms | | Total | 7.989 ms | 5.085 ms | The direct reconstruction makes the commit kernel 3.27x faster and reduces total RecoverSSM KDA time by 36.34%. The FP32 correction write increases verify time by 13.66%, but commit time falls by 69.45%. Native KDA without recovery took 2.772 ms per step in the corresponding OFF trace. The 72 steady batch-32 steps each verified 256 tokens. Their CUDA-graph model-forward GPU wall time was 65.208 ms with RecoverSSM and 64.873 ms without it, a 0.335 ms or 0.52% difference. Kernel residence exceeds wall time because kernels on concurrent streams overlap. | RecoverSSM ON steady forward kernel residence | Time per step | Share | |---|---:|---:| | DeepGEMM and nvJet GEMM | 38.760 ms | 56.5% | | MoE routing and packing | 8.121 ms | 11.8% | | SiTU activation | 7.682 ms | 11.2% | | TP collectives | 6.136 ms | 8.9% | | RecoverSSM verify | 3.791 ms | 5.5% | | KDA convolution and normalization | 0.938 ms | 1.4% | | MLA attention kernels | 0.519 ms | 0.8% | | Other kernels | 2.658 ms | 3.9% | | Total kernel residence | 68.603 ms | 100% | RecoverSSM verify runs inside model forward and replaces the native KDA recurrent kernel. Its steady kernel residence was 3.791 ms versus 3.009 ms for native KDA, an increase of 0.782 ms. The smaller 0.335 ms forward wall-time difference reflects kernel overlap and run-to-run variation. Commit runs after sampling determines the accepted length, so it is not part of model forward. Across the 72 steady batch-32 steps it took 1.711 ms per step and varied with the accepted length. | Post-sampling RecoverSSM commit | Time per step | Share | |---|---:|---:| | FP32 correction state reconstruction | 1.618 ms | 94.5% | | Convolution-state compaction | 0.081 ms | 4.7% | | Commit-plan preparation | 0.0069 ms | 0.4% | | Align bookkeeping | 0.0061 ms | 0.4% | | Total | 1.711 ms | 100% | Adding the steady model-forward difference and post-sampling commit gives an estimated RecoverSSM GPU critical-path cost of 2.046 ms per batch-32 decode step, before common sampling and postprocessing work. ## Duplicate-work check The following searches were run against open vLLM PRs: ```bash gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "ReplaySSM Kimi K3" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA speculative decoding" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "ReplaySSM in:title,body" ``` No other open PR implements this Kimi-K3 KDA RecoverSSM integration. Related work is materially different: - #49847 targets Mamba2; - #49887 targets Gated DeltaNet; - #50140 is a WIP FlashInfer ReplaySSM kernel; - #42792 adds generic Mamba align-prefix speculative support rather than Kimi-K3 KDA RecoverSSM. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, profiling analysis, model evaluation analysis, and this PR description. The submitting human must review every changed line, reproduce the relevant tests, and understand and defend the design end-to-end. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan and exact commands. - [x] Unit, end-to-end accuracy, memory, acceptance, and performance results. - [x] Duplicate-work check and AI-assistance disclosure. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

signal.title: fix(anthropic): convert tool_reference items to template-safe text
signal.text: Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52489 ## Summary `AnthropicServingMessages._convert_user_tool_result` converted `text` and `image` items inside a `tool_result` block into template-safe OpenAI content, but passed `tool_reference` items through **raw** (`{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}`). That raw dict went straight into a `tool`-role message's `content`, and strict Jinja chat templates (e.g. Qwen3's) hit their catch-all `raise_exception` branch — so any conversation containing a `tool_reference` block (common with Claude Code + multiple MCP servers, where the API's dynamic-tool-discovery lets a result reference another tool by name) failed on every subsequent request. Changed `tool_reference` items to a template-safe `text` item — `{"type": "text", "text": "[tool reference: {name}]"}` — mirroring how `text`/`image` are already handled. ## Test Added `test_tool_result_tool_reference_becomes_text` to `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`, asserting the converted `tool` message content is `done\n[tool reference: search_web]`. Conversion logic verified standalone (vLLM's full test env needs torch, unavailable here).
signal.author: chjnett

signal.title: fix: propagate precompiled wheel variant lookup failure instead of falling back
signal.text: Fixes vllm-project/vllm#52544 ## Summary For Python-only builds, when the precompiled-wheel metadata lookup for the selected CUDA variant fails, `setup.py` fell back to the root/default variant index. Nothing downstream checks that the fallback wheel matches the CUDA variant that was selected (or auto-detected) — the issue reporter hit exactly this: PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, its metadata lookup failed, and the fallback picked a native artifact requiring CUDA 13. The fix propagates the variant lookup failure instead of retrying the root index: once a variant is selected, only that variant's metadata is fetched. A wrong-CUDA wheel is worse than an install failure, because it fails far from the config that caused it. ## Verification - `setup.py` parses cleanly (`ast.parse`). - No other code path depends on the removed `try_default`/`download_filename` initializer — `download_filename` is still assigned in the wheel-selection branches that follow.

signal.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix Mamba state pointer overflow
signal.text: Fixes #48059 ## Purpose XPU USM device pointers can exceed the positive signed int64 range. The Mamba align-mode fused copy path stores state tensor and block-table `data_ptr()` values in `torch.int64` metadata buffers before passing them to Triton kernels, so assigning a high-bit XPU pointer directly can raise: ```text ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long ``` This preserves the 64-bit pointer pattern by reinterpreting unsigned pointer values as signed int64 before storing them in the existing metadata buffers. The Triton kernel ABI stays unchanged. Duplicate-work check: no open PR currently references #48059 or matches the `state_base_addrs` / overflow keywords. ## Test Plan - `pre-commit run ruff-format --files vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py` - `pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py` - `python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py -q` ## Test Result - `ruff-format` passed - `ruff-check` passed - `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py`: 3 passed, 17 skipped I could not run the full XPU serving repro locally because this environment does not have the reported Intel Arc/XPU setup and hybrid checkpoint. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>
